    FileUtils.chmod('u=wrx,go=rx', 'src1.txt', noop: true, verbose: true)
    FileUtils.chmod('u=wrx,go=rx', '/usr/bin/ruby', noop: true, verbose: true)

  Output:

    chmod 755 src0.txt
    chmod 644 src0.txt src0.dat
    chmod u=wrx,go=rx src1.txt
    chmod u=wrx,go=rx /usr/bin/ruby

Related: FileUtils.chmod_R.

FileUtils::chmod_R.name: chmod_R
FileUtils::chmod_R.params: (mode, list, noop: nil, verbose: nil, force: nil)
FileUtils::chmod_R.comment: Like FileUtils.chmod, but changes permissions recursively.

FileUtils::chown.name: chown
FileUtils::chown.params: (user, group, list, noop: nil, verbose: nil)
FileUtils::chown.comment:
Changes the owner and group on the entries at the paths given in <tt>list</tt>
(a single path or an array of paths) to the given <tt>user</tt> and
<tt>group</tt>; returns <tt>list</tt> if it is an array, <tt>[list]</tt>
otherwise:

* Modifies each entry that is a regular file using
  {File.chown}[rdoc-ref:File.chown].
* Modifies each entry that is a symbolic link using
  {File.lchown}[rdoc-ref:File.lchown].

Argument <tt>list</tt> or its elements should be {interpretable as
paths}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Path+Arguments].

User and group:

* Argument <tt>user</tt> may be a user name or a user id; if <tt>nil</tt> or
  <tt>-1</tt>, the user is not changed.
* Argument <tt>group</tt> may be a group name or a group id; if <tt>nil</tt>
  or <tt>-1</tt>, the group is not changed.
* The user must be a member of the group.

Examples:

  # One path.
  # User and group as string names.
  File.stat('src0.txt').uid # => 1004
  File.stat('src0.txt').gid # => 1004
  FileUtils.chown('user2', 'group1', 'src0.txt')
  File.stat('src0.txt').uid # => 1006
  File.stat('src0.txt').gid # => 1005

  # User and group as uid and gid.
  FileUtils.chown(1004, 1004, 'src0.txt')
  File.stat('src0.txt').uid # => 1004
  File.stat('src0.txt').gid # => 1004

  # Array of paths.
  FileUtils.chown(1006, 1005, ['src0.txt', 'src0.dat'])

  # Directory (not recursive).
  FileUtils.chown('user2', 'group1', '.')

Keyword arguments:

* <tt>noop: true</tt> - does not change permissions; returns <tt>nil</tt>.
* <tt>verbose: true</tt> - prints an equivalent command:

    FileUtils.chown('user2', 'group1', 'src0.txt', noop: true, verbose: true)
    FileUtils.chown(1004, 1004, 'src0.txt', noop: true, verbose: true)
    FileUtils.chown(1006, 1005, ['src0.txt', 'src0.dat'], noop: true, verbose: true)
    FileUtils.chown('user2', 'group1', path, noop: true, verbose: true)
    FileUtils.chown('user2', 'group1', '.', noop: true, verbose: true)

  Output:

    chown user2:group1 src0.txt
    chown 1004:1004 src0.txt
    chown 1006:1005 src0.txt src0.dat
    chown user2:group1 src0.txt
    chown user2:group1 .

Related: FileUtils.chown_R.

FileUtils::chown_R.name: chown_R
FileUtils::chown_R.params: (user, group, list, noop: nil, verbose: nil, force: nil)
FileUtils::chown_R.comment: Like FileUtils.chown, but changes owner and group recursively.

FileUtils::collect_method.name: collect_method
FileUtils::collect_method.comment:
Returns an array of the string method names of the methods that accept the
given keyword option <tt>opt</tt>; the argument must be a symbol:

  FileUtils.collect_method(:preserve) # => ["cp", "copy", "cp_r", "install"]

FileUtils::commands.name: commands
FileUtils::commands.comment:
Returns an array of the string names of FileUtils methods that accept one or
more keyword arguments:

  FileUtils.commands.sort.take(3) # => ["cd", "chdir", "chmod"]

FileUtils::compare_file.name: compare_file
FileUtils::compare_file.comment:
Returns <tt>true</tt> if the contents of files <tt>a</tt> and <tt>b</tt> are
identical, <tt>false</tt> otherwise.

Arguments <tt>a</tt> and <tt>b</tt> should be {interpretable as a
path}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Path+Arguments].

FileUtils.identical? and FileUtils.cmp are aliases for FileUtils.compare_file.

Related: FileUtils.compare_stream.

FileUtils::compare_stream.name: compare_stream
FileUtils::compare_stream.comment:
Returns <tt>true</tt> if the contents of streams <tt>a</tt> and <tt>b</tt> are
identical, <tt>false</tt> otherwise.

Arguments <tt>a</tt> and <tt>b</tt> should be {interpretable as a
path}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Path+Arguments].

Related: FileUtils.compare_file.

FileUtils::copy.name: copy
FileUtils::copy.params: (src, dest, preserve: nil, noop: nil, verbose: nil)

FileUtils::copy_entry.name: copy_entry
FileUtils::copy_entry.params: (src, dest, preserve = false, dereference_root = false, remove_destination = false)
FileUtils::copy_entry.comment:
Recursively copies files from <tt>src</tt> to <tt>dest</tt>.

Arguments <tt>src</tt> and <tt>dest</tt> should be {interpretable as
paths}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Path+Arguments].

If <tt>src</tt> is the path to a file, copies <tt>src</tt> to <tt>dest</tt>:

  FileUtils.touch('src0.txt')
  File.exist?('dest0.txt') # => false
  FileUtils.copy_entry('src0.txt', 'dest0.txt')
  File.file?('dest0.txt')  # => true

If <tt>src</tt> is a directory, recursively copies <tt>src</tt> to
<tt>dest</tt>:

  tree('src1')
  # => src1
  #    |-- dir0
  #    |   |-- src0.txt
  #    |   `-- src1.txt
  #    `-- dir1
  #        |-- src2.txt
  #        `-- src3.txt
  FileUtils.copy_entry('src1', 'dest1')
  tree('dest1')
  # => dest1
  #    |-- dir0
  #    |   |-- src0.txt
  #    |   `-- src1.txt
  #    `-- dir1
  #        |-- src2.txt
  #        `-- src3.txt

The recursive copying preserves file types for regular files, directories, and
symbolic links; other file types (FIFO streams, device files, etc.) are not
supported.

Optional arguments:

* <tt>dereference_root</tt> - if <tt>src</tt> is a symbolic link, follows the
  link (<tt>false</tt> by default).
* <tt>preserve</tt> - preserves file times (<tt>false</tt> by default).
* <tt>remove_destination</tt> - removes <tt>dest</tt> before copying files
  (<tt>false</tt> by default).

Related: {methods for copying}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Copying].

FileUtils::copy_file.name: copy_file
FileUtils::copy_file.comment:
Copies file from <tt>src</tt> to <tt>dest</tt>, which should not be
directories.

Arguments <tt>src</tt> and <tt>dest</tt> should be {interpretable as
paths}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Path+Arguments].

Examples:

  FileUtils.touch('src0.txt')
  FileUtils.copy_file('src0.txt', 'dest0.txt')
  File.file?('dest0.txt') # => true

Optional arguments:

* <tt>dereference</tt> - if <tt>src</tt> is a symbolic link, follows the link
  (<tt>true</tt> by default).
* <tt>preserve</tt> - preserves file times (<tt>false</tt> by default).
* <tt>remove_destination</tt> - removes <tt>dest</tt> before copying files
  (<tt>false</tt> by default).

Related: {methods for copying}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Copying].

FileUtils::copy_stream.name: copy_stream
FileUtils::copy_stream.comment:
Copies IO stream <tt>src</tt> to IO stream <tt>dest</tt> via
{IO.copy_stream}[rdoc-ref:IO.copy_stream].

Related: {methods for copying}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Copying].

FileUtils::cp.name: cp
FileUtils::cp.params: (src, dest, preserve: nil, noop: nil, verbose: nil)
FileUtils::cp.comment:
Copies files.

Arguments <tt>src</tt> (a single path or an array of paths) and <tt>dest</tt>
(a single path) should be {interpretable as
paths}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Path+Arguments].

If <tt>src</tt> is the path to a file and <tt>dest</tt> is not the path to a
directory, copies <tt>src</tt> to <tt>dest</tt>:

  FileUtils.touch('src0.txt')
  File.exist?('dest0.txt') # => false
  FileUtils.cp('src0.txt', 'dest0.txt')
  File.file?('dest0.txt')  # => true

If <tt>src</tt> is the path to a file and <tt>dest</tt> is the path to a
directory, copies <tt>src</tt> to <tt>dest/src</tt>:

  FileUtils.touch('src1.txt')
  FileUtils.mkdir('dest1')
  FileUtils.cp('src1.txt', 'dest1')
  File.file?('dest1/src1.txt') # => true

If <tt>src</tt> is an array of paths to files and <tt>dest</tt> is the path to
a directory, copies from each <tt>src</tt> to <tt>dest</tt>:

  src_file_paths = ['src2.txt', 'src2.dat']
  FileUtils.touch(src_file_paths)
  FileUtils.mkdir('dest2')
  FileUtils.cp(src_file_paths, 'dest2')
  File.file?('dest2/src2.txt') # => true
  File.file?('dest2/src2.dat') # => true

Keyword arguments:

* <tt>preserve: true</tt> - preserves file times.
* <tt>noop: true</tt> - does not copy files.
* <tt>verbose: true</tt> - prints an equivalent command:

    FileUtils.cp('src0.txt', 'dest0.txt', noop: true, verbose: true)
    FileUtils.cp('src1.txt', 'dest1', noop: true, verbose: true)
    FileUtils.cp(src_file_paths, 'dest2', noop: true, verbose: true)

  Output:

    cp src0.txt dest0.txt
    cp src1.txt dest1
    cp src2.txt src2.dat dest2

Raises an exception if <tt>src</tt> is a directory.

Related: {methods for copying}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Copying].

FileUtils::cp_lr.name: cp_lr
FileUtils::cp_lr.params: (src, dest, noop: nil, verbose: nil, dereference_root: true, remove_destination: false)
FileUtils::cp_lr.comment:
Creates {hard links}[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hard_link].

Arguments <tt>src</tt> (a single path or an array of paths) and <tt>dest</tt>
(a single path) should be {interpretable as
paths}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Path+Arguments].

If <tt>src</tt> is the path to a directory and <tt>dest</tt> does not exist,
creates links <tt>dest</tt> and descendents pointing to <tt>src</tt> and its
descendents:

  tree('src0')
  # => src0
  #    |-- sub0
  #    |   |-- src0.txt
  #    |   `-- src1.txt
  #    `-- sub1
  #        |-- src2.txt
  #        `-- src3.txt
  File.exist?('dest0') # => false
  FileUtils.cp_lr('src0', 'dest0')
  tree('dest0')
  # => dest0
  #    |-- sub0
  #    |   |-- src0.txt
  #    |   `-- src1.txt
  #    `-- sub1
  #        |-- src2.txt
  #        `-- src3.txt

If <tt>src</tt> and <tt>dest</tt> are both paths to directories, creates links
<tt>dest/src</tt> and descendents pointing to <tt>src</tt> and its
descendents:

  tree('src1')
  # => src1
  #    |-- sub0
  #    |   |-- src0.txt
  #    |   `-- src1.txt
  #    `-- sub1
  #        |-- src2.txt
  #        `-- src3.txt
  FileUtils.mkdir('dest1')
  FileUtils.cp_lr('src1', 'dest1')
  tree('dest1')
  # => dest1
  #    `-- src1
  #        |-- sub0
  #        |   |-- src0.txt
  #        |   `-- src1.txt
  #        `-- sub1
  #            |-- src2.txt
  #            `-- src3.txt

If <tt>src</tt> is an array of paths to entries and <tt>dest</tt> is the path
to a directory, for each path <tt>filepath</tt> in <tt>src</tt>, creates a
link at <tt>dest/filepath</tt> pointing to that path:

  tree('src2')
  # => src2
  #    |-- sub0
  #    |   |-- src0.txt
  #    |   `-- src1.txt
  #    `-- sub1
  #        |-- src2.txt
  #        `-- src3.txt
  FileUtils.mkdir('dest2')
  FileUtils.cp_lr(['src2/sub0', 'src2/sub1'], 'dest2')
  tree('dest2')
  # => dest2
  #    |-- sub0
  #    |   |-- src0.txt
  #    |   `-- src1.txt
  #    `-- sub1
  #        |-- src2.txt
  #        `-- src3.txt

Keyword arguments:

* <tt>dereference_root: false</tt> - if <tt>src</tt> is a symbolic link, does
  not dereference it.
* <tt>noop: true</tt> - does not create links.
* <tt>remove_destination: true</tt> - removes <tt>dest</tt> before creating
  links.
* <tt>verbose: true</tt> - prints an equivalent command:

    FileUtils.cp_lr('src0', 'dest0', noop: true, verbose: true)
    FileUtils.cp_lr('src1', 'dest1', noop: true, verbose: true)
    FileUtils.cp_lr(['src2/sub0', 'src2/sub1'], 'dest2', noop: true, verbose: true)

  Output:

    cp -lr src0 dest0
    cp -lr src1 dest1
    cp -lr src2/sub0 src2/sub1 dest2

Raises an exception if <tt>dest</tt> is the path to an existing file or
directory and keyword argument <tt>remove_destination: true</tt> is not given.

Related: {methods for copying}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Copying].

FileUtils::cp_r.name: cp_r
FileUtils::cp_r.params: (src, dest, preserve: nil, noop: nil, verbose: nil, dereference_root: true, remove_destination: nil)
FileUtils::cp_r.comment:
Recursively copies files.

Arguments <tt>src</tt> (a single path or an array of paths) and <tt>dest</tt>
(a single path) should be {interpretable as
paths}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Path+Arguments].

The mode, owner, and group are retained in the copy; to change those, use
FileUtils.install instead.

If <tt>src</tt> is the path to a file and <tt>dest</tt> is not the path to a
directory, copies <tt>src</tt> to <tt>dest</tt>:

  FileUtils.touch('src0.txt')
  File.exist?('dest0.txt') # => false
  FileUtils.cp_r('src0.txt', 'dest0.txt')
  File.file?('dest0.txt')  # => true

If <tt>src</tt> is the path to a file and <tt>dest</tt> is the path to a
directory, copies <tt>src</tt> to <tt>dest/src</tt>:

  FileUtils.touch('src1.txt')
  FileUtils.mkdir('dest1')
  FileUtils.cp_r('src1.txt', 'dest1')
  File.file?('dest1/src1.txt') # => true

If <tt>src</tt> is the path to a directory and <tt>dest</tt> does not exist,
recursively copies <tt>src</tt> to <tt>dest</tt>:

  tree('src2')
  # => src2
  #    |-- dir0
  #    |   |-- src0.txt
  #    |   `-- src1.txt
  #    `-- dir1
  #    |-- src2.txt
  #    `-- src3.txt
  FileUtils.exist?('dest2') # => false
  FileUtils.cp_r('src2', 'dest2')
  tree('dest2')
  # => dest2
  #    |-- dir0
  #    |   |-- src0.txt
  #    |   `-- src1.txt
  #    `-- dir1
  #    |-- src2.txt
  #    `-- src3.txt

If <tt>src</tt> and <tt>dest</tt> are paths to directories, recursively copies
<tt>src</tt> to <tt>dest/src</tt>:

  tree('src3')
  # => src3
  #    |-- dir0
  #    |   |-- src0.txt
  #    |   `-- src1.txt
  #    `-- dir1
  #    |-- src2.txt
  #    `-- src3.txt
  FileUtils.mkdir('dest3')
  FileUtils.cp_r('src3', 'dest3')
  tree('dest3')
  # => dest3
  #    `-- src3
  #      |-- dir0
  #      |   |-- src0.txt
  #      |   `-- src1.txt
  #      `-- dir1
  #          |-- src2.txt
  #          `-- src3.txt

If <tt>src</tt> is an array of paths and <tt>dest</tt> is a directory,
recursively copies from each path in <tt>src</tt> to <tt>dest</tt>; the paths
in <tt>src</tt> may point to files and/or directories.

Keyword arguments:

* <tt>dereference_root: false</tt> - if <tt>src</tt> is a symbolic link, does
  not dereference it.
* <tt>noop: true</tt> - does not copy files.
* <tt>preserve: true</tt> - preserves file times.
* <tt>remove_destination: true</tt> - removes <tt>dest</tt> before copying
  files.
* <tt>verbose: true</tt> - prints an equivalent command:

    FileUtils.cp_r('src0.txt', 'dest0.txt', noop: true, verbose: true)
    FileUtils.cp_r('src1.txt', 'dest1', noop: true, verbose: true)
    FileUtils.cp_r('src2', 'dest2', noop: true, verbose: true)
    FileUtils.cp_r('src3', 'dest3', noop: true, verbose: true)

  Output:

    cp -r src0.txt dest0.txt
    cp -r src1.txt dest1
    cp -r src2 dest2
    cp -r src3 dest3

Raises an exception of <tt>src</tt> is the path to a directory and
<tt>dest</tt> is the path to a file.

Related: {methods for copying}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Copying].

FileUtils::have_option?.name: have_option?
FileUtils::have_option?.comment:
Returns <tt>true</tt> if method <tt>mid</tt> accepts the given option
<tt>opt</tt>, <tt>false</tt> otherwise; the arguments may be strings or
symbols:

  FileUtils.have_option?(:chmod, :noop) # => true
  FileUtils.have_option?('chmod', 'secure') # => false

FileUtils::install.name: install
FileUtils::install.params: (src, dest, mode: nil, owner: nil, group: nil, preserve: nil, noop: nil, verbose: nil)
FileUtils::install.comment: Copies a file entry. See {install(1)}[https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man1/install.1.html]. Arguments src (a single path or an array of paths) and dest (a single path) should be {interpretable as paths}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Path+Arguments]; If the entry at dest does not exist, copies from src to dest: File.read('src0.txt') # => "aaa\n" File.exist?('dest0.txt') # => false FileUtils.install('src0.txt', 'dest0.txt') File.read('dest0.txt') # => "aaa\n" If dest is a file entry, copies from src to dest, overwriting: File.read('src1.txt') # => "aaa\n" File.read('dest1.txt') # => "bbb\n" FileUtils.install('src1.txt', 'dest1.txt') File.read('dest1.txt') # => "aaa\n" If dest is a directory entry, copies from src to dest/src, overwriting if necessary: File.read('src2.txt') # => "aaa\n" File.read('dest2/src2.txt') # => "bbb\n" FileUtils.install('src2.txt', 'dest2') File.read('dest2/src2.txt') # => "aaa\n" If src is an array of paths and dest points to a directory, copies each path path in src to dest/path: File.file?('src3.txt') # => true File.file?('src3.dat') # => true FileUtils.mkdir('dest3') FileUtils.install(['src3.txt', 'src3.dat'], 'dest3') File.file?('dest3/src3.txt') # => true File.file?('dest3/src3.dat') # => true Keyword arguments: * group: group - changes the group if not nil, using {File.chown}[rdoc-ref:File.chown]. * mode: permissions - changes the permissions. using {File.chmod}[rdoc-ref:File.chmod]. * noop: true - does not copy entries; returns nil. * owner: owner - changes the owner if not nil, using {File.chown}[rdoc-ref:File.chown]. * preserve: true - preserve timestamps using {File.utime}[rdoc-ref:File.utime]. * verbose: true - prints an equivalent command: FileUtils.install('src0.txt', 'dest0.txt', noop: true, verbose: true) FileUtils.install('src1.txt', 'dest1.txt', noop: true, verbose: true) FileUtils.install('src2.txt', 'dest2', noop: true, verbose: true) Output: install -c src0.txt dest0.txt install -c src1.txt dest1.txt install -c src2.txt dest2 Related: {methods for copying}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Copying].

FileUtils::link.name: link
FileUtils::link.params: (src, dest, force: nil, noop: nil, verbose: nil)

FileUtils::link_entry.name: link_entry
FileUtils::link_entry.comment:
Creates {hard links}[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hard_link]; returns
<tt>nil</tt>.

Arguments <tt>src</tt> and <tt>dest</tt> should be {interpretable as
paths}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Path+Arguments].

If <tt>src</tt> is the path to a file and <tt>dest</tt> does not exist,
creates a hard link at <tt>dest</tt> pointing to <tt>src</tt>:

  FileUtils.touch('src0.txt')
  File.exist?('dest0.txt') # => false
  FileUtils.link_entry('src0.txt', 'dest0.txt')
  File.file?('dest0.txt')  # => true

If <tt>src</tt> is the path to a directory and <tt>dest</tt> does not exist,
recursively creates hard links at <tt>dest</tt> pointing to paths in
<tt>src</tt>:

  FileUtils.mkdir_p(['src1/dir0', 'src1/dir1'])
  src_file_paths = [
    'src1/dir0/t0.txt',
    'src1/dir0/t1.txt',
    'src1/dir1/t2.txt',
    'src1/dir1/t3.txt',
    ]
  FileUtils.touch(src_file_paths)
  File.directory?('dest1')        # => true
  FileUtils.link_entry('src1', 'dest1')
  File.file?('dest1/dir0/t0.txt') # => true
  File.file?('dest1/dir0/t1.txt') # => true
  File.file?('dest1/dir1/t2.txt') # => true
  File.file?('dest1/dir1/t3.txt') # => true

Optional arguments:

* <tt>dereference_root</tt> - dereferences <tt>src</tt> if it is a symbolic
  link (<tt>false</tt> by default).
* <tt>remove_destination</tt> - removes <tt>dest</tt> before creating links
  (<tt>false</tt> by default).

Raises an exception if <tt>dest</tt> is the path to an existing file or
directory and optional argument <tt>remove_destination</tt> is not given.

Related: FileUtils.ln (has different options).

FileUtils::ln.name: ln
FileUtils::ln.params: (src, dest, force: nil, noop: nil, verbose: nil)
FileUtils::ln.comment:
Creates {hard links}[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hard_link].

Arguments <tt>src</tt> (a single path or an array of paths) and <tt>dest</tt>
(a single path) should be {interpretable as
paths}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Path+Arguments].

When <tt>src</tt> is the path to an existing file and <tt>dest</tt> is the
path to a non-existent file, creates a hard link at <tt>dest</tt> pointing to
<tt>src</tt>; returns zero:

  Dir.children('tmp0/')                    # => ["t.txt"]
  Dir.children('tmp1/')                    # => []
  FileUtils.ln('tmp0/t.txt', 'tmp1/t.lnk') # => 0
  Dir.children('tmp1/')                    # => ["t.lnk"]

When <tt>src</tt> is the path to an existing file and <tt>dest</tt> is the
path to an existing directory, creates a hard link at <tt>dest/src</tt>
pointing to <tt>src</tt>; returns zero:

  Dir.children('tmp2')               # => ["t.dat"]
  Dir.children('tmp3')               # => []
  FileUtils.ln('tmp2/t.dat', 'tmp3') # => 0
  Dir.children('tmp3')               # => ["t.dat"]

When <tt>src</tt> is an array of paths to existing files and <tt>dest</tt> is
the path to an existing directory, then for each path <tt>target</tt> in
<tt>src</tt>, creates a hard link at <tt>dest/target</tt> pointing to
<tt>target</tt>; returns <tt>src</tt>:

  Dir.children('tmp4/')                               # => []
  FileUtils.ln(['tmp0/t.txt', 'tmp2/t.dat'], 'tmp4/') # => ["tmp0/t.txt", "tmp2/t.dat"]
  Dir.children('tmp4/')                               # => ["t.dat", "t.txt"]

Keyword arguments:

* <tt>force: true</tt> - overwrites <tt>dest</tt> if it exists.
* <tt>noop: true</tt> - does not create links.
* <tt>verbose: true</tt> - prints an equivalent command:

    FileUtils.ln('tmp0/t.txt', 'tmp1/t.lnk', verbose: true)
    FileUtils.ln('tmp2/t.dat', 'tmp3', verbose: true)
    FileUtils.ln(['tmp0/t.txt', 'tmp2/t.dat'], 'tmp4/', verbose: true)

  Output:

    ln tmp0/t.txt tmp1/t.lnk
    ln tmp2/t.dat tmp3
    ln tmp0/t.txt tmp2/t.dat tmp4/

Raises an exception if <tt>dest</tt> is the path to an existing file and
keyword argument <tt>force</tt> is not <tt>true</tt>.

Related: FileUtils.link_entry (has different options).

FileUtils::ln_s.name: ln_s
FileUtils::ln_s.params: (src, dest, force: nil, relative: false, target_directory: true, noop: nil, verbose: nil)
FileUtils::ln_s.comment:
Creates {symbolic links}[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Symbolic_link].

Arguments <tt>src</tt> (a single path or an array of paths) and <tt>dest</tt>
(a single path) should be {interpretable as
paths}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Path+Arguments].

If <tt>src</tt> is the path to an existing file:

* When <tt>dest</tt> is the path to a non-existent file, creates a symbolic
  link at <tt>dest</tt> pointing to <tt>src</tt>:

    FileUtils.touch('src0.txt')
    File.exist?('dest0.txt')   # => false
    FileUtils.ln_s('src0.txt', 'dest0.txt')
    File.symlink?('dest0.txt') # => true

* When <tt>dest</tt> is the path to an existing file, creates a symbolic link
  at <tt>dest</tt> pointing to <tt>src</tt> if and only if keyword argument
  <tt>force: true</tt> is given (raises an exception otherwise):

    FileUtils.touch('src1.txt')
    FileUtils.touch('dest1.txt')
    FileUtils.ln_s('src1.txt', 'dest1.txt', force: true)
    FileTest.symlink?('dest1.txt') # => true

    FileUtils.ln_s('src1.txt', 'dest1.txt') # Raises Errno::EEXIST.

If <tt>dest</tt> is the path to a directory, creates a symbolic link at
<tt>dest/src</tt> pointing to <tt>src</tt>:

  FileUtils.touch('src2.txt')
  FileUtils.mkdir('destdir2')
  FileUtils.ln_s('src2.txt', 'destdir2')
  File.symlink?('destdir2/src2.txt') # => true

If <tt>src</tt> is an array of paths to existing files and <tt>dest</tt> is a
directory, for each child <tt>child</tt> in <tt>src</tt> creates a symbolic
link <tt>dest/child</tt> pointing to <tt>child</tt>:

  FileUtils.mkdir('srcdir3')
  FileUtils.touch('srcdir3/src0.txt')
  FileUtils.touch('srcdir3/src1.txt')
  FileUtils.mkdir('destdir3')
  FileUtils.ln_s(['srcdir3/src0.txt', 'srcdir3/src1.txt'], 'destdir3')
  File.symlink?('destdir3/src0.txt') # => true
  File.symlink?('destdir3/src1.txt') # => true

Keyword arguments:

* <tt>force: true</tt> - overwrites <tt>dest</tt> if it exists.
* <tt>relative: true</tt> - create links relative to <tt>dest</tt>.
* <tt>noop: true</tt> - does not create links.
* <tt>verbose: true</tt> - prints an equivalent command:

    FileUtils.ln_s('src0.txt', 'dest0.txt', noop: true, verbose: true)
    FileUtils.ln_s('src1.txt', 'destdir1', noop: true, verbose: true)
    FileUtils.ln_s('src2.txt', 'dest2.txt', force: true, noop: true, verbose: true)
    FileUtils.ln_s(['srcdir3/src0.txt', 'srcdir3/src1.txt'], 'destdir3', noop: true, verbose: true)

  Output:

    ln -s src0.txt dest0.txt
    ln -s src1.txt destdir1
    ln -sf src2.txt dest2.txt
    ln -s srcdir3/src0.txt srcdir3/src1.txt destdir3

Related: FileUtils.ln_sf.

FileUtils::ln_sf.name: ln_sf
FileUtils::ln_sf.comment:
Like FileUtils.ln_s, but always with keyword argument <tt>force: true</tt>
given.

FileUtils::ln_sr.name: ln_sr
FileUtils::ln_sr.params: (src, dest, target_directory: true, force: nil, noop: nil, verbose: nil)
FileUtils::ln_sr.comment: Like FileUtils.ln_s, but create links relative to <tt>dest</tt>.

FileUtils::makedirs.name: makedirs
FileUtils::makedirs.params: (list, mode: nil, noop: nil, verbose: nil)

FileUtils::mkdir.name: mkdir
FileUtils::mkdir.params: (list, mode: nil, noop: nil, verbose: nil)
FileUtils::mkdir.call_seq: FileUtils.mkdir(*paths, mode: 0775, noop: nil, verbose: nil) -> array_of_paths or nil
FileUtils::mkdir.comment:
Argument <tt>paths</tt> may be one path or an array of paths;
each must be {interpretable as a path}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Path+Arguments].
By default, creates a directory entry at each of the given <tt>paths</tt>;
each directory has permissions <tt>0775</tt>;
returns an array of the paths:
  FileUtils.mkdir('foo')                 # => ["foo"]
FileUtils.mkdir(%w[bar baz])           # => ["bar", "baz"]
File.stat(Dir.new('foo')).mode.to_s(8) # => "40775"
File.stat(Dir.new('bar')).mode.to_s(8) # => "40775"
File.stat(Dir.new('baz')).mode.to_s(8) # => "40775"
FileUtils.rmdir(%w[foo bar baz])       # => ["foo", "bar", "baz"]

Raises an exception if for any reason a directory cannot be created;
a common reason is that the directory already exists.
With keyword argument <tt>mode</tt> given,
creates directories with the given permissions:
  FileUtils.mkdir('bar', mode: 0664)
File.stat(Dir.new('bar')).mode.to_s(8) # => "40664"
FileUtils.rmdir('bar')

With keyword argument <tt>noop</tt> given as <tt>true</tt>,
does not create directories;
returns <tt>nil</tt>
  FileUtils.mkdir('foo', noop: true) # => nil
Dir.exist?('foo')                  # => false

With keyword argument <tt>verbose</tt> given as <tt>true</tt>,
prints a shell command:
  FileUtils.mkdir('foo', verbose: true)
FileUtils.mkdir(%w[bar baz], mode: 0644, verbose: true)
FileUtils.mkdir(%w[bar baz], mode: 0644, verbose: true, noop: true)

Output:
  mkdir foo
mkdir -m 644 bar baz
mkdir -m 644 bar baz

Note that in the last call above (containing <tt>noop: true</tt>)
the existence of the directory is not checked.
Related: FileUtils.mkdir_p.

FileUtils::mkdir_p.name: mkdir_p
FileUtils::mkdir_p.params: (list, mode: nil, noop: nil, verbose: nil)
FileUtils::mkdir_p.comment: Creates directories at the paths in the given list (a single path or an array of paths), also creating ancestor directories as needed; returns list if it is an array, [list] otherwise. Argument list or its elements should be {interpretable as paths}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Path+Arguments]. With no keyword arguments, creates a directory at each path in list, along with any needed ancestor directories, by calling: Dir.mkdir(path, mode); see {Dir.mkdir}[rdoc-ref:Dir.mkdir]: FileUtils.mkdir_p(%w[tmp0/tmp1 tmp2/tmp3]) # => ["tmp0/tmp1", "tmp2/tmp3"] FileUtils.mkdir_p('tmp4/tmp5') # => ["tmp4/tmp5"] Keyword arguments: * mode: mode - also calls File.chmod(mode, path); see {File.chmod}[rdoc-ref:File.chmod]. * noop: true - does not create directories. * verbose: true - prints an equivalent command: FileUtils.mkdir_p(%w[tmp0 tmp1], verbose: true) FileUtils.mkdir_p(%w[tmp2 tmp3], mode: 0700, verbose: true) Output: mkdir -p tmp0 tmp1 mkdir -p -m 700 tmp2 tmp3 Raises an exception if for any reason a directory cannot be created. FileUtils.mkpath and FileUtils.makedirs are aliases for FileUtils.mkdir_p. Related: FileUtils.mkdir.

FileUtils::mkpath.name: mkpath
FileUtils::mkpath.params: (list, mode: nil, noop: nil, verbose: nil)

FileUtils::move.name: move
FileUtils::move.params: (src, dest, force: nil, noop: nil, verbose: nil, secure: nil)

FileUtils::mv.name: mv
FileUtils::mv.params: (src, dest, force: nil, noop: nil, verbose: nil, secure: nil)
FileUtils::mv.comment:
Moves entries.

Arguments <tt>src</tt> (a single path or an array of paths) and <tt>dest</tt>
(a single path) should be {interpretable as
paths}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Path+Arguments].

If <tt>src</tt> and <tt>dest</tt> are on different file systems, first copies,
then removes <tt>src</tt>.

May cause a local vulnerability if not called with keyword argument
<tt>secure: true</tt>; see {Avoiding the TOCTTOU
Vulnerability}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Avoiding+the+TOCTTOU+Vulnerability].

If <tt>src</tt> is the path to a single file or directory and <tt>dest</tt>
does not exist, moves <tt>src</tt> to <tt>dest</tt>:

  tree('src0')
  # => src0
  #    |-- src0.txt
  #    `-- src1.txt
  File.exist?('dest0') # => false
  FileUtils.mv('src0', 'dest0')
  File.exist?('src0')  # => false
  tree('dest0')
  # => dest0
  #    |-- src0.txt
  #    `-- src1.txt

If <tt>src</tt> is an array of paths to files and directories and
<tt>dest</tt> is the path to a directory, copies from each path in the array
to <tt>dest</tt>:

  File.file?('src1.txt') # => true
  tree('src1')
  # => src1
  #    |-- src.dat
  #    `-- src.txt
  Dir.empty?('dest1')    # => true
  FileUtils.mv(['src1.txt', 'src1'], 'dest1')
  tree('dest1')
  # => dest1
  #    |-- src1
  #    |   |-- src.dat
  #    |   `-- src.txt
  #    `-- src1.txt

Keyword arguments:

* <tt>force: true</tt> - if the move includes removing <tt>src</tt> (that is,
  if <tt>src</tt> and <tt>dest</tt> are on different file systems), ignores
  raised exceptions of StandardError and its descendants.
* <tt>noop: true</tt> - does not move files.
* <tt>secure: true</tt> - removes <tt>src</tt> securely; see details at
  FileUtils.remove_entry_secure.
* <tt>verbose: true</tt> - prints an equivalent command:

    FileUtils.mv('src0', 'dest0', noop: true, verbose: true)
    FileUtils.mv(['src1.txt', 'src1'], 'dest1', noop: true, verbose: true)

  Output:

    mv src0 dest0
    mv src1.txt src1 dest1

FileUtils::options.name: options
FileUtils::options.comment:
Returns an array of the string keyword names:

  FileUtils.options.take(3) # => ["noop", "verbose", "force"]

FileUtils::options_of.name: options_of
FileUtils::options_of.comment:
Returns an array of the string keyword name for method <tt>mid</tt>; the
argument may be a string or a symbol:

  FileUtils.options_of(:rm) # => ["force", "noop", "verbose"]
  FileUtils.options_of('mv') # => ["force", "noop", "verbose", "secure"]

FileUtils::pwd.name: pwd
FileUtils::pwd.comment:
Returns a string containing the path to the current directory:

  FileUtils.pwd # => "/rdoc/fileutils"

Related: FileUtils.cd.

FileUtils::remove.name: remove
FileUtils::remove.params: (list, force: nil, noop: nil, verbose: nil)

FileUtils::remove_dir.name: remove_dir
FileUtils::remove_dir.comment:
Recursively removes the directory entry given by <tt>path</tt>, which should
be the entry for a regular file, a symbolic link, or a directory.

Argument <tt>path</tt> should be {interpretable as a
path}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Path+Arguments].

Optional argument <tt>force</tt> specifies whether to ignore raised exceptions
of StandardError and its descendants.

Related: {methods for deleting}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Deleting].

FileUtils::remove_entry.name: remove_entry
FileUtils::remove_entry.comment:
Removes the entry given by <tt>path</tt>, which should be the entry for a
regular file, a symbolic link, or a directory.

Argument <tt>path</tt> should be {interpretable as a
path}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Path+Arguments].

Optional argument <tt>force</tt> specifies whether to ignore raised exceptions
of StandardError and its descendants.

Related: FileUtils.remove_entry_secure.

FileUtils::remove_entry_secure.name: remove_entry_secure
FileUtils::remove_entry_secure.comment:
Securely removes the entry given by <tt>path</tt>, which should be the entry
for a regular file, a symbolic link, or a directory.

Argument <tt>path</tt> should be {interpretable as a
path}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Path+Arguments].

Avoids a local vulnerability that can exist in certain circumstances; see
{Avoiding the TOCTTOU
Vulnerability}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Avoiding+the+TOCTTOU+Vulnerability].

Optional argument <tt>force</tt> specifies whether to ignore raised exceptions
of StandardError and its descendants.

Related: {methods for deleting}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Deleting].

FileUtils::remove_file.name: remove_file
FileUtils::remove_file.comment:
Removes the file entry given by <tt>path</tt>, which should be the entry for a
regular file or a symbolic link.

Argument <tt>path</tt> should be {interpretable as a
path}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Path+Arguments].

Optional argument <tt>force</tt> specifies whether to ignore raised exceptions
of StandardError and its descendants.

Related: {methods for deleting}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Deleting].

FileUtils::rm.name: rm
FileUtils::rm.params: (list, force: nil, noop: nil, verbose: nil)
FileUtils::rm.comment:
Removes entries at the paths in the given <tt>list</tt> (a single path or an
array of paths) returns <tt>list</tt>, if it is an array, <tt>[list]</tt>
otherwise.

Argument <tt>list</tt> or its elements should be {interpretable as
paths}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Path+Arguments].

With no keyword arguments, removes files at the paths given in <tt>list</tt>:

  FileUtils.touch(['src0.txt', 'src0.dat'])
  FileUtils.rm(['src0.dat', 'src0.txt']) # => ["src0.dat", "src0.txt"]

Keyword arguments:

* <tt>force: true</tt> - ignores raised exceptions of StandardError and its
  descendants.
* <tt>noop: true</tt> - does not remove files; returns <tt>nil</tt>.
* <tt>verbose: true</tt> - prints an equivalent command:

    FileUtils.rm(['src0.dat', 'src0.txt'], noop: true, verbose: true)

  Output:

    rm src0.dat src0.txt

Related: {methods for deleting}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Deleting].

FileUtils::rm_f.name: rm_f
FileUtils::rm_f.comment:
Equivalent to:

  FileUtils.rm(list, force: true, **kwargs)

Argument <tt>list</tt> (a single path or an array of paths) should be
{interpretable as paths}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Path+Arguments].

See FileUtils.rm for keyword arguments.

Related: {methods for deleting}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Deleting].

FileUtils::rm_r.name: rm_r
FileUtils::rm_r.params: (list, force: nil, noop: nil, verbose: nil, secure: nil)
FileUtils::rm_r.comment:
Removes entries at the paths in the given <tt>list</tt> (a single path or an
array of paths); returns <tt>list</tt>, if it is an array, <tt>[list]</tt>
otherwise.

Argument <tt>list</tt> or its elements should be {interpretable as
paths}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Path+Arguments].

May cause a local vulnerability if not called with keyword argument
<tt>secure: true</tt>; see {Avoiding the TOCTTOU
Vulnerability}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Avoiding+the+TOCTTOU+Vulnerability].

For each file path, removes the file at that path:

  FileUtils.touch(['src0.txt', 'src0.dat'])
  FileUtils.rm_r(['src0.dat', 'src0.txt'])
  File.exist?('src0.txt') # => false
  File.exist?('src0.dat') # => false

For each directory path, recursively removes files and directories:

  tree('src1')
  # => src1
  #    |-- dir0
  #    |   |-- src0.txt
  #    |   `-- src1.txt
  #    `-- dir1
  #        |-- src2.txt
  #        `-- src3.txt
  FileUtils.rm_r('src1')
  File.exist?('src1') # => false

Keyword arguments:

* <tt>force: true</tt> - ignores raised exceptions of StandardError and its
  descendants.
* <tt>noop: true</tt> - does not remove entries; returns <tt>nil</tt>.
* <tt>secure: true</tt> - removes <tt>src</tt> securely; see details at
  FileUtils.remove_entry_secure.
* <tt>verbose: true</tt> - prints an equivalent command:

    FileUtils.rm_r(['src0.dat', 'src0.txt'], noop: true, verbose: true)
    FileUtils.rm_r('src1', noop: true, verbose: true)

  Output:

    rm -r src0.dat src0.txt
    rm -r src1

Related: {methods for deleting}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Deleting].

FileUtils::rm_rf.name: rm_rf
FileUtils::rm_rf.params: (list, noop: nil, verbose: nil, secure: nil)
FileUtils::rm_rf.comment:
Equivalent to:

  FileUtils.rm_r(list, force: true, **kwargs)

Argument <tt>list</tt> or its elements should be {interpretable as
paths}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Path+Arguments].

May cause a local vulnerability if not called with keyword argument
<tt>secure: true</tt>; see {Avoiding the TOCTTOU
Vulnerability}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Avoiding+the+TOCTTOU+Vulnerability].

See FileUtils.rm_r for keyword arguments.

Related: {methods for deleting}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Deleting].

FileUtils::rmdir.name: rmdir
FileUtils::rmdir.params: (list, parents: nil, noop: nil, verbose: nil)
FileUtils::rmdir.comment:
Removes directories at the paths in the given <tt>list</tt> (a single path or
an array of paths); returns <tt>list</tt>, if it is an array, <tt>[list]</tt>
otherwise.

Argument <tt>list</tt> or its elements should be {interpretable as
paths}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Path+Arguments].

With no keyword arguments, removes the directory at each <tt>path</tt> in
<tt>list</tt>, by calling: <tt>Dir.rmdir(path)</tt>; see
{Dir.rmdir}[rdoc-ref:Dir.rmdir]:

  FileUtils.rmdir(%w[tmp0/tmp1 tmp2/tmp3]) # => ["tmp0/tmp1", "tmp2/tmp3"]
  FileUtils.rmdir('tmp4/tmp5')             # => ["tmp4/tmp5"]

Keyword arguments:

* <tt>parents: true</tt> - removes successive ancestor directories if empty.
* <tt>noop: true</tt> - does not remove directories.
* <tt>verbose: true</tt> - prints an equivalent command:

    FileUtils.rmdir(%w[tmp0/tmp1 tmp2/tmp3], parents: true, verbose: true)
    FileUtils.rmdir('tmp4/tmp5', parents: true, verbose: true)

  Output:

    rmdir -p tmp0/tmp1 tmp2/tmp3
    rmdir -p tmp4/tmp5

Raises an exception if a directory does not exist or if for any reason a
directory cannot be removed.

Related: {methods for deleting}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Deleting].

FileUtils::rmtree.name: rmtree
FileUtils::rmtree.params: (list, noop: nil, verbose: nil, secure: nil)

FileUtils::symlink.name: symlink
FileUtils::symlink.params: (src, dest, force: nil, relative: false, target_directory: true, noop: nil, verbose: nil)

FileUtils::touch.name: touch
FileUtils::touch.params: (list, noop: nil, verbose: nil, mtime: nil, nocreate: nil)
FileUtils::touch.comment: Updates modification times (mtime) and access times (atime) of the entries given by the paths in list (a single path or an array of paths); returns list if it is an array, [list] otherwise. By default, creates an empty file for any path to a non-existent entry; use keyword argument nocreate to raise an exception instead. Argument list or its elements should be {interpretable as paths}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Path+Arguments]. Examples: # Single path. f = File.new('src0.txt') # Existing file. f.atime # => 2022-06-10 11:11:21.200277 -0700 f.mtime # => 2022-06-10 11:11:21.200277 -0700 FileUtils.touch('src0.txt') f = File.new('src0.txt') f.atime # => 2022-06-11 08:28:09.8185343 -0700 f.mtime # => 2022-06-11 08:28:09.8185343 -0700 # Array of paths. FileUtils.touch(['src0.txt', 'src0.dat']) Keyword arguments: * mtime: time - sets the entry's mtime to the given time, instead of the current time. * nocreate: true - raises an exception if the entry does not exist. * noop: true - does not touch entries; returns nil. * verbose: true - prints an equivalent command: FileUtils.touch('src0.txt', noop: true, verbose: true) FileUtils.touch(['src0.txt', 'src0.dat'], noop: true, verbose: true) FileUtils.touch(path, noop: true, verbose: true) Output: touch src0.txt touch src0.txt src0.dat touch src0.txt Related: FileUtils.uptodate?.

FileUtils::uptodate?.name: uptodate?
FileUtils::uptodate?.comment:
Returns <tt>true</tt> if the file at path <tt>new</tt> is newer than all the
files at paths in array <tt>old_list</tt>; <tt>false</tt> otherwise.

Argument <tt>new</tt> and the elements of <tt>old_list</tt> should be
{interpretable as paths}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Path+Arguments]:

  FileUtils.uptodate?('Rakefile', ['Gemfile', 'README.md']) # => true
  FileUtils.uptodate?('Gemfile', ['Rakefile', 'README.md']) # => false

A non-existent file is considered to be infinitely old.

Related: FileUtils.touch.

FileUtils#cd.name: cd
FileUtils#cd.comment:
Changes the working directory to the given <tt>dir</tt>, which should be
{interpretable as a path}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Path+Arguments]:

With no block given, changes the current directory to the directory at
<tt>dir</tt>; returns zero:

  FileUtils.pwd # => "/rdoc/fileutils"
  FileUtils.cd('..')
  FileUtils.pwd # => "/rdoc"
  FileUtils.cd('fileutils')

With a block given, changes the current directory to the directory at
<tt>dir</tt>, calls the block with argument <tt>dir</tt>, and restores the
original current directory; returns the block's value:

  FileUtils.pwd                                     # => "/rdoc/fileutils"
  FileUtils.cd('..') { |arg| [arg, FileUtils.pwd] } # => ["..", "/rdoc"]
  FileUtils.pwd                                     # => "/rdoc/fileutils"

Keyword arguments:

* <tt>verbose: true</tt> - prints an equivalent command:

    FileUtils.cd('..')
    FileUtils.cd('fileutils')

  Output:

    cd ..
    cd fileutils

Related: FileUtils.pwd.

FileUtils#chmod.name: chmod
FileUtils#chmod.comment:
Changes permissions on the entries at the paths given in <tt>list</tt> (a
single path or an array of paths) to the permissions given by <tt>mode</tt>;
returns <tt>list</tt> if it is an array, <tt>[list]</tt> otherwise:

* Modifies each entry that is a regular file using
  {File.chmod}[rdoc-ref:File.chmod].
* Modifies each entry that is a symbolic link using
  {File.lchmod}[rdoc-ref:File.lchmod].

Argument <tt>list</tt> or its elements should be {interpretable as
paths}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Path+Arguments].

Argument <tt>mode</tt> may be either an integer or a string:

* Integer <tt>mode</tt>: represents the permission bits to be set:

    FileUtils.chmod(0755, 'src0.txt')
    FileUtils.chmod(0644, ['src0.txt', 'src0.dat'])

* String <tt>mode</tt>: represents the permissions to be set:

  The string is of the form <tt>[targets][[operator][perms[,perms]]</tt>,
  where:

  * <tt>targets</tt> may be any combination of these letters:

    * <tt>'u'</tt>: permissions apply to the file's owner.
    * <tt>'g'</tt>: permissions apply to users in the file's group.
    * <tt>'o'</tt>: permissions apply to other users not in the file's group.
    * <tt>'a'</tt> (the default): permissions apply to all users.

  * <tt>operator</tt> may be one of these letters:

    * <tt>'+'</tt>: adds permissions.
    * <tt>'-'</tt>: removes permissions.
    * <tt>'='</tt>: sets (replaces) permissions.

  * <tt>perms</tt> (may be repeated, with separating commas) may be any
    combination of these letters:

    * <tt>'r'</tt>: Read.
    * <tt>'w'</tt>: Write.
    * <tt>'x'</tt>: Execute (search, for a directory).
    * <tt>'X'</tt>: Search (for a directories only; must be used with
      <tt>'+'</tt>)
    * <tt>'s'</tt>: Uid or gid.
    * <tt>'t'</tt>: Sticky bit.

  Examples:

    FileUtils.chmod('u=wrx,go=rx', 'src1.txt')
    FileUtils.chmod('u=wrx,go=rx', '/usr/bin/ruby')

Keyword arguments:

* <tt>noop: true</tt> - does not change permissions; returns <tt>nil</tt>.
* <tt>verbose: true</tt> - prints an equivalent command:

    FileUtils.chmod(0755, 'src0.txt', noop: true, verbose: true)
    FileUtils.chmod(0644, ['src0.txt', 'src0.dat'], noop: true, verbose: true)
    FileUtils.chmod('u=wrx,go=rx', 'src1.txt', noop: true, verbose: true)
    FileUtils.chmod('u=wrx,go=rx', '/usr/bin/ruby', noop: true, verbose: true)

  Output:

    chmod 755 src0.txt
    chmod 644 src0.txt src0.dat
    chmod u=wrx,go=rx src1.txt
    chmod u=wrx,go=rx /usr/bin/ruby

Related: FileUtils.chmod_R.

FileUtils#chmod_R.name: chmod_R
FileUtils#chmod_R.params: (mode, list, noop: nil, verbose: nil, force: nil)
FileUtils#chmod_R.comment: Like FileUtils.chmod, but changes permissions recursively.

FileUtils#chown.name: chown
FileUtils#chown.params: (user, group, list, noop: nil, verbose: nil)
FileUtils#chown.comment:
Changes the owner and group on the entries at the paths given in <tt>list</tt>
(a single path or an array of paths) to the given <tt>user</tt> and
<tt>group</tt>; returns <tt>list</tt> if it is an array, <tt>[list]</tt>
otherwise:

* Modifies each entry that is a regular file using
  {File.chown}[rdoc-ref:File.chown].
* Modifies each entry that is a symbolic link using
  {File.lchown}[rdoc-ref:File.lchown].

Argument <tt>list</tt> or its elements should be {interpretable as
paths}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Path+Arguments].

User and group:

* Argument <tt>user</tt> may be a user name or a user id; if <tt>nil</tt> or
  <tt>-1</tt>, the user is not changed.
* Argument <tt>group</tt> may be a group name or a group id; if <tt>nil</tt>
  or <tt>-1</tt>, the group is not changed.
* The user must be a member of the group.

Examples:

  # One path.
  # User and group as string names.
  File.stat('src0.txt').uid # => 1004
  File.stat('src0.txt').gid # => 1004
  FileUtils.chown('user2', 'group1', 'src0.txt')
  File.stat('src0.txt').uid # => 1006
  File.stat('src0.txt').gid # => 1005

  # User and group as uid and gid.
  FileUtils.chown(1004, 1004, 'src0.txt')
  File.stat('src0.txt').uid # => 1004
  File.stat('src0.txt').gid # => 1004

  # Array of paths.
  FileUtils.chown(1006, 1005, ['src0.txt', 'src0.dat'])

  # Directory (not recursive).
  FileUtils.chown('user2', 'group1', '.')

Keyword arguments:

* <tt>noop: true</tt> - does not change permissions; returns <tt>nil</tt>.
* <tt>verbose: true</tt> - prints an equivalent command:

    FileUtils.chown('user2', 'group1', 'src0.txt', noop: true, verbose: true)
    FileUtils.chown(1004, 1004, 'src0.txt', noop: true, verbose: true)
    FileUtils.chown(1006, 1005, ['src0.txt', 'src0.dat'], noop: true, verbose: true)
    FileUtils.chown('user2', 'group1', path, noop: true, verbose: true)
    FileUtils.chown('user2', 'group1', '.', noop: true, verbose: true)

  Output:

    chown user2:group1 src0.txt
    chown 1004:1004 src0.txt
    chown 1006:1005 src0.txt src0.dat
    chown user2:group1 src0.txt
    chown user2:group1 .

Related: FileUtils.chown_R.

FileUtils#chown_R.name: chown_R
FileUtils#chown_R.params: (user, group, list, noop: nil, verbose: nil, force: nil)
FileUtils#chown_R.comment: Like FileUtils.chown, but changes owner and group recursively.

FileUtils#compare_file.name: compare_file
FileUtils#compare_file.comment:
Returns <tt>true</tt> if the contents of files <tt>a</tt> and <tt>b</tt> are
identical, <tt>false</tt> otherwise.

Arguments <tt>a</tt> and <tt>b</tt> should be {interpretable as a
path}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Path+Arguments].

FileUtils.identical? and FileUtils.cmp are aliases for FileUtils.compare_file.

Related: FileUtils.compare_stream.

FileUtils#compare_stream.name: compare_stream
FileUtils#compare_stream.comment:
Returns <tt>true</tt> if the contents of streams <tt>a</tt> and <tt>b</tt> are
identical, <tt>false</tt> otherwise.

Arguments <tt>a</tt> and <tt>b</tt> should be {interpretable as a
path}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Path+Arguments].

Related: FileUtils.compare_file.

FileUtils#copy.name: copy
FileUtils#copy.params: (src, dest, preserve: nil, noop: nil, verbose: nil)

FileUtils#copy_entry.name: copy_entry
FileUtils#copy_entry.params: (src, dest, preserve = false, dereference_root = false, remove_destination = false)
FileUtils#copy_entry.comment:
Recursively copies files from <tt>src</tt> to <tt>dest</tt>.

Arguments <tt>src</tt> and <tt>dest</tt> should be {interpretable as
paths}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Path+Arguments].

If <tt>src</tt> is the path to a file, copies <tt>src</tt> to <tt>dest</tt>:

  FileUtils.touch('src0.txt')
  File.exist?('dest0.txt') # => false
  FileUtils.copy_entry('src0.txt', 'dest0.txt')
  File.file?('dest0.txt')  # => true

If <tt>src</tt> is a directory, recursively copies <tt>src</tt> to
<tt>dest</tt>:

  tree('src1')
  # => src1
  #    |-- dir0
  #    |   |-- src0.txt
  #    |   `-- src1.txt
  #    `-- dir1
  #        |-- src2.txt
  #        `-- src3.txt
  FileUtils.copy_entry('src1', 'dest1')
  tree('dest1')
  # => dest1
  #    |-- dir0
  #    |   |-- src0.txt
  #    |   `-- src1.txt
  #    `-- dir1
  #        |-- src2.txt
  #        `-- src3.txt

The recursive copying preserves file types for regular files, directories, and
symbolic links; other file types (FIFO streams, device files, etc.) are not
supported.

Optional arguments:

* <tt>dereference_root</tt> - if <tt>src</tt> is a symbolic link, follows the
  link (<tt>false</tt> by default).
* <tt>preserve</tt> - preserves file times (<tt>false</tt> by default).
* <tt>remove_destination</tt> - removes <tt>dest</tt> before copying files
  (<tt>false</tt> by default).

Related: {methods for copying}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Copying].

FileUtils#copy_file.name: copy_file
FileUtils#copy_file.comment:
Copies file from <tt>src</tt> to <tt>dest</tt>, which should not be
directories.

Arguments <tt>src</tt> and <tt>dest</tt> should be {interpretable as
paths}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Path+Arguments].

Examples:

  FileUtils.touch('src0.txt')
  FileUtils.copy_file('src0.txt', 'dest0.txt')
  File.file?('dest0.txt') # => true

Optional arguments:

* <tt>dereference</tt> - if <tt>src</tt> is a symbolic link, follows the link
  (<tt>true</tt> by default).
* <tt>preserve</tt> - preserves file times (<tt>false</tt> by default).
* <tt>remove_destination</tt> - removes <tt>dest</tt> before copying files
  (<tt>false</tt> by default).

Related: {methods for copying}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Copying].

FileUtils#copy_stream.name: copy_stream
FileUtils#copy_stream.comment:
Copies IO stream <tt>src</tt> to IO stream <tt>dest</tt> via
{IO.copy_stream}[rdoc-ref:IO.copy_stream].

Related: {methods for copying}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Copying].

FileUtils#cp.name: cp
FileUtils#cp.params: (src, dest, preserve: nil, noop: nil, verbose: nil)
FileUtils#cp.comment:
Copies files.

Arguments <tt>src</tt> (a single path or an array of paths) and <tt>dest</tt>
(a single path) should be {interpretable as
paths}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Path+Arguments].

If <tt>src</tt> is the path to a file and <tt>dest</tt> is not the path to a
directory, copies <tt>src</tt> to <tt>dest</tt>:

  FileUtils.touch('src0.txt')
  File.exist?('dest0.txt') # => false
  FileUtils.cp('src0.txt', 'dest0.txt')
  File.file?('dest0.txt')  # => true

If <tt>src</tt> is the path to a file and <tt>dest</tt> is the path to a
directory, copies <tt>src</tt> to <tt>dest/src</tt>:

  FileUtils.touch('src1.txt')
  FileUtils.mkdir('dest1')
  FileUtils.cp('src1.txt', 'dest1')
  File.file?('dest1/src1.txt') # => true

If <tt>src</tt> is an array of paths to files and <tt>dest</tt> is the path to
a directory, copies from each <tt>src</tt> to <tt>dest</tt>:

  src_file_paths = ['src2.txt', 'src2.dat']
  FileUtils.touch(src_file_paths)
  FileUtils.mkdir('dest2')
  FileUtils.cp(src_file_paths, 'dest2')
  File.file?('dest2/src2.txt') # => true
  File.file?('dest2/src2.dat') # => true

Keyword arguments:

* <tt>preserve: true</tt> - preserves file times.
* <tt>noop: true</tt> - does not copy files.
* <tt>verbose: true</tt> - prints an equivalent command:

    FileUtils.cp('src0.txt', 'dest0.txt', noop: true, verbose: true)
    FileUtils.cp('src1.txt', 'dest1', noop: true, verbose: true)
    FileUtils.cp(src_file_paths, 'dest2', noop: true, verbose: true)

  Output:

    cp src0.txt dest0.txt
    cp src1.txt dest1
    cp src2.txt src2.dat dest2

Raises an exception if <tt>src</tt> is a directory.

Related: {methods for copying}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Copying].

FileUtils#cp_lr.name: cp_lr
FileUtils#cp_lr.params: (src, dest, noop: nil, verbose: nil, dereference_root: true, remove_destination: false)
FileUtils#cp_lr.comment:
Creates {hard links}[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hard_link].

Arguments <tt>src</tt> (a single path or an array of paths) and <tt>dest</tt>
(a single path) should be {interpretable as
paths}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Path+Arguments].

If <tt>src</tt> is the path to a directory and <tt>dest</tt> does not exist,
creates links <tt>dest</tt> and descendents pointing to <tt>src</tt> and its
descendents:

  tree('src0')
  # => src0
  #    |-- sub0
  #    |   |-- src0.txt
  #    |   `-- src1.txt
  #    `-- sub1
  #        |-- src2.txt
  #        `-- src3.txt
  File.exist?('dest0') # => false
  FileUtils.cp_lr('src0', 'dest0')
  tree('dest0')
  # => dest0
  #    |-- sub0
  #    |   |-- src0.txt
  #    |   `-- src1.txt
  #    `-- sub1
  #        |-- src2.txt
  #        `-- src3.txt

If <tt>src</tt> and <tt>dest</tt> are both paths to directories, creates links
<tt>dest/src</tt> and descendents pointing to <tt>src</tt> and its
descendents:

  tree('src1')
  # => src1
  #    |-- sub0
  #    |   |-- src0.txt
  #    |   `-- src1.txt
  #    `-- sub1
  #        |-- src2.txt
  #        `-- src3.txt
  FileUtils.mkdir('dest1')
  FileUtils.cp_lr('src1', 'dest1')
  tree('dest1')
  # => dest1
  #    `-- src1
  #        |-- sub0
  #        |   |-- src0.txt
  #        |   `-- src1.txt
  #        `-- sub1
  #            |-- src2.txt
  #            `-- src3.txt

If <tt>src</tt> is an array of paths to entries and <tt>dest</tt> is the path
to a directory, for each path <tt>filepath</tt> in <tt>src</tt>, creates a
link at <tt>dest/filepath</tt> pointing to that path:

  tree('src2')
  # => src2
  #    |-- sub0
  #    |   |-- src0.txt
  #    |   `-- src1.txt
  #    `-- sub1
  #        |-- src2.txt
  #        `-- src3.txt
  FileUtils.mkdir('dest2')
  FileUtils.cp_lr(['src2/sub0', 'src2/sub1'], 'dest2')
  tree('dest2')
  # => dest2
  #    |-- sub0
  #    |   |-- src0.txt
  #    |   `-- src1.txt
  #    `-- sub1
  #        |-- src2.txt
  #        `-- src3.txt

Keyword arguments:

* <tt>dereference_root: false</tt> - if <tt>src</tt> is a symbolic link, does
  not dereference it.
* <tt>noop: true</tt> - does not create links.
* <tt>remove_destination: true</tt> - removes <tt>dest</tt> before creating
  links.
* <tt>verbose: true</tt> - prints an equivalent command:

    FileUtils.cp_lr('src0', 'dest0', noop: true, verbose: true)
    FileUtils.cp_lr('src1', 'dest1', noop: true, verbose: true)
    FileUtils.cp_lr(['src2/sub0', 'src2/sub1'], 'dest2', noop: true, verbose: true)

  Output:

    cp -lr src0 dest0
    cp -lr src1 dest1
    cp -lr src2/sub0 src2/sub1 dest2

Raises an exception if <tt>dest</tt> is the path to an existing file or
directory and keyword argument <tt>remove_destination: true</tt> is not given.

Related: {methods for copying}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Copying].

FileUtils#cp_r.name: cp_r
FileUtils#cp_r.params: (src, dest, preserve: nil, noop: nil, verbose: nil, dereference_root: true, remove_destination: nil)
FileUtils#cp_r.comment:
Recursively copies files.

Arguments <tt>src</tt> (a single path or an array of paths) and <tt>dest</tt>
(a single path) should be {interpretable as
paths}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Path+Arguments].

The mode, owner, and group are retained in the copy; to change those, use
FileUtils.install instead.

If <tt>src</tt> is the path to a file and <tt>dest</tt> is not the path to a
directory, copies <tt>src</tt> to <tt>dest</tt>:

  FileUtils.touch('src0.txt')
  File.exist?('dest0.txt') # => false
  FileUtils.cp_r('src0.txt', 'dest0.txt')
  File.file?('dest0.txt')  # => true

If <tt>src</tt> is the path to a file and <tt>dest</tt> is the path to a
directory, copies <tt>src</tt> to <tt>dest/src</tt>:

  FileUtils.touch('src1.txt')
  FileUtils.mkdir('dest1')
  FileUtils.cp_r('src1.txt', 'dest1')
  File.file?('dest1/src1.txt') # => true

If <tt>src</tt> is the path to a directory and <tt>dest</tt> does not exist,
recursively copies <tt>src</tt> to <tt>dest</tt>:

  tree('src2')
  # => src2
  #    |-- dir0
  #    |   |-- src0.txt
  #    |   `-- src1.txt
  #    `-- dir1
  #    |-- src2.txt
  #    `-- src3.txt
  FileUtils.exist?('dest2') # => false
  FileUtils.cp_r('src2', 'dest2')
  tree('dest2')
  # => dest2
  #    |-- dir0
  #    |   |-- src0.txt
  #    |   `-- src1.txt
  #    `-- dir1
  #    |-- src2.txt
  #    `-- src3.txt

If <tt>src</tt> and <tt>dest</tt> are paths to directories, recursively copies
<tt>src</tt> to <tt>dest/src</tt>:

  tree('src3')
  # => src3
  #    |-- dir0
  #    |   |-- src0.txt
  #    |   `-- src1.txt
  #    `-- dir1
  #    |-- src2.txt
  #    `-- src3.txt
  FileUtils.mkdir('dest3')
  FileUtils.cp_r('src3', 'dest3')
  tree('dest3')
  # => dest3
  #    `-- src3
  #      |-- dir0
  #      |   |-- src0.txt
  #      |   `-- src1.txt
  #      `-- dir1
  #          |-- src2.txt
  #          `-- src3.txt

If <tt>src</tt> is an array of paths and <tt>dest</tt> is a directory,
recursively copies from each path in <tt>src</tt> to <tt>dest</tt>; the paths
in <tt>src</tt> may point to files and/or directories.

Keyword arguments:

* <tt>dereference_root: false</tt> - if <tt>src</tt> is a symbolic link, does
  not dereference it.
* <tt>noop: true</tt> - does not copy files.
* <tt>preserve: true</tt> - preserves file times.
* <tt>remove_destination: true</tt> - removes <tt>dest</tt> before copying
  files.
* <tt>verbose: true</tt> - prints an equivalent command:

    FileUtils.cp_r('src0.txt', 'dest0.txt', noop: true, verbose: true)
    FileUtils.cp_r('src1.txt', 'dest1', noop: true, verbose: true)
    FileUtils.cp_r('src2', 'dest2', noop: true, verbose: true)
    FileUtils.cp_r('src3', 'dest3', noop: true, verbose: true)

  Output:

    cp -r src0.txt dest0.txt
    cp -r src1.txt dest1
    cp -r src2 dest2
    cp -r src3 dest3

Raises an exception of <tt>src</tt> is the path to a directory and
<tt>dest</tt> is the path to a file.

Related: {methods for copying}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Copying].

FileUtils#install.name: install
FileUtils#install.params: (src, dest, mode: nil, owner: nil, group: nil, preserve: nil, noop: nil, verbose: nil)
FileUtils#install.comment: Copies a file entry. See {install(1)}[https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man1/install.1.html]. Arguments src (a single path or an array of paths) and dest (a single path) should be {interpretable as paths}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Path+Arguments]; If the entry at dest does not exist, copies from src to dest: File.read('src0.txt') # => "aaa\n" File.exist?('dest0.txt') # => false FileUtils.install('src0.txt', 'dest0.txt') File.read('dest0.txt') # => "aaa\n" If dest is a file entry, copies from src to dest, overwriting: File.read('src1.txt') # => "aaa\n" File.read('dest1.txt') # => "bbb\n" FileUtils.install('src1.txt', 'dest1.txt') File.read('dest1.txt') # => "aaa\n" If dest is a directory entry, copies from src to dest/src, overwriting if necessary: File.read('src2.txt') # => "aaa\n" File.read('dest2/src2.txt') # => "bbb\n" FileUtils.install('src2.txt', 'dest2') File.read('dest2/src2.txt') # => "aaa\n" If src is an array of paths and dest points to a directory, copies each path path in src to dest/path: File.file?('src3.txt') # => true File.file?('src3.dat') # => true FileUtils.mkdir('dest3') FileUtils.install(['src3.txt', 'src3.dat'], 'dest3') File.file?('dest3/src3.txt') # => true File.file?('dest3/src3.dat') # => true Keyword arguments: * group: group - changes the group if not nil, using {File.chown}[rdoc-ref:File.chown]. * mode: permissions - changes the permissions. using {File.chmod}[rdoc-ref:File.chmod]. * noop: true - does not copy entries; returns nil. * owner: owner - changes the owner if not nil, using {File.chown}[rdoc-ref:File.chown]. * preserve: true - preserve timestamps using {File.utime}[rdoc-ref:File.utime]. * verbose: true - prints an equivalent command: FileUtils.install('src0.txt', 'dest0.txt', noop: true, verbose: true) FileUtils.install('src1.txt', 'dest1.txt', noop: true, verbose: true) FileUtils.install('src2.txt', 'dest2', noop: true, verbose: true) Output: install -c src0.txt dest0.txt install -c src1.txt dest1.txt install -c src2.txt dest2 Related: {methods for copying}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Copying].

FileUtils#link.name: link
FileUtils#link.params: (src, dest, force: nil, noop: nil, verbose: nil)

FileUtils#link_entry.name: link_entry
FileUtils#link_entry.comment:
Creates {hard links}[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hard_link]; returns
<tt>nil</tt>.

Arguments <tt>src</tt> and <tt>dest</tt> should be {interpretable as
paths}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Path+Arguments].

If <tt>src</tt> is the path to a file and <tt>dest</tt> does not exist,
creates a hard link at <tt>dest</tt> pointing to <tt>src</tt>:

  FileUtils.touch('src0.txt')
  File.exist?('dest0.txt') # => false
  FileUtils.link_entry('src0.txt', 'dest0.txt')
  File.file?('dest0.txt')  # => true

If <tt>src</tt> is the path to a directory and <tt>dest</tt> does not exist,
recursively creates hard links at <tt>dest</tt> pointing to paths in
<tt>src</tt>:

  FileUtils.mkdir_p(['src1/dir0', 'src1/dir1'])
  src_file_paths = [
    'src1/dir0/t0.txt',
    'src1/dir0/t1.txt',
    'src1/dir1/t2.txt',
    'src1/dir1/t3.txt',
    ]
  FileUtils.touch(src_file_paths)
  File.directory?('dest1')        # => true
  FileUtils.link_entry('src1', 'dest1')
  File.file?('dest1/dir0/t0.txt') # => true
  File.file?('dest1/dir0/t1.txt') # => true
  File.file?('dest1/dir1/t2.txt') # => true
  File.file?('dest1/dir1/t3.txt') # => true

Optional arguments:

* <tt>dereference_root</tt> - dereferences <tt>src</tt> if it is a symbolic
  link (<tt>false</tt> by default).
* <tt>remove_destination</tt> - removes <tt>dest</tt> before creating links
  (<tt>false</tt> by default).

Raises an exception if <tt>dest</tt> is the path to an existing file or
directory and optional argument <tt>remove_destination</tt> is not given.

Related: FileUtils.ln (has different options).

FileUtils#ln.name: ln
FileUtils#ln.params: (src, dest, force: nil, noop: nil, verbose: nil)
FileUtils#ln.comment:
Creates {hard links}[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hard_link].

Arguments <tt>src</tt> (a single path or an array of paths) and <tt>dest</tt>
(a single path) should be {interpretable as
paths}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Path+Arguments].

When <tt>src</tt> is the path to an existing file and <tt>dest</tt> is the
path to a non-existent file, creates a hard link at <tt>dest</tt> pointing to
<tt>src</tt>; returns zero:

  Dir.children('tmp0/')                    # => ["t.txt"]
  Dir.children('tmp1/')                    # => []
  FileUtils.ln('tmp0/t.txt', 'tmp1/t.lnk') # => 0
  Dir.children('tmp1/')                    # => ["t.lnk"]

When <tt>src</tt> is the path to an existing file and <tt>dest</tt> is the
path to an existing directory, creates a hard link at <tt>dest/src</tt>
pointing to <tt>src</tt>; returns zero:

  Dir.children('tmp2')               # => ["t.dat"]
  Dir.children('tmp3')               # => []
  FileUtils.ln('tmp2/t.dat', 'tmp3') # => 0
  Dir.children('tmp3')               # => ["t.dat"]

When <tt>src</tt> is an array of paths to existing files and <tt>dest</tt> is
the path to an existing directory, then for each path <tt>target</tt> in
<tt>src</tt>, creates a hard link at <tt>dest/target</tt> pointing to
<tt>target</tt>; returns <tt>src</tt>:

  Dir.children('tmp4/')                               # => []
  FileUtils.ln(['tmp0/t.txt', 'tmp2/t.dat'], 'tmp4/') # => ["tmp0/t.txt", "tmp2/t.dat"]
  Dir.children('tmp4/')                               # => ["t.dat", "t.txt"]

Keyword arguments:

* <tt>force: true</tt> - overwrites <tt>dest</tt> if it exists.
* <tt>noop: true</tt> - does not create links.
* <tt>verbose: true</tt> - prints an equivalent command:

    FileUtils.ln('tmp0/t.txt', 'tmp1/t.lnk', verbose: true)
    FileUtils.ln('tmp2/t.dat', 'tmp3', verbose: true)
    FileUtils.ln(['tmp0/t.txt', 'tmp2/t.dat'], 'tmp4/', verbose: true)

  Output:

    ln tmp0/t.txt tmp1/t.lnk
    ln tmp2/t.dat tmp3
    ln tmp0/t.txt tmp2/t.dat tmp4/

Raises an exception if <tt>dest</tt> is the path to an existing file and
keyword argument <tt>force</tt> is not <tt>true</tt>.

Related: FileUtils.link_entry (has different options).

FileUtils#ln_s.name: ln_s
FileUtils#ln_s.params: (src, dest, force: nil, relative: false, target_directory: true, noop: nil, verbose: nil)
FileUtils#ln_s.comment:
Creates {symbolic links}[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Symbolic_link].

Arguments <tt>src</tt> (a single path or an array of paths) and <tt>dest</tt>
(a single path) should be {interpretable as
paths}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Path+Arguments].

If <tt>src</tt> is the path to an existing file:

* When <tt>dest</tt> is the path to a non-existent file, creates a symbolic
  link at <tt>dest</tt> pointing to <tt>src</tt>:

    FileUtils.touch('src0.txt')
    File.exist?('dest0.txt')   # => false
    FileUtils.ln_s('src0.txt', 'dest0.txt')
    File.symlink?('dest0.txt') # => true

* When <tt>dest</tt> is the path to an existing file, creates a symbolic link
  at <tt>dest</tt> pointing to <tt>src</tt> if and only if keyword argument
  <tt>force: true</tt> is given (raises an exception otherwise):

    FileUtils.touch('src1.txt')
    FileUtils.touch('dest1.txt')
    FileUtils.ln_s('src1.txt', 'dest1.txt', force: true)
    FileTest.symlink?('dest1.txt') # => true

    FileUtils.ln_s('src1.txt', 'dest1.txt') # Raises Errno::EEXIST.

If <tt>dest</tt> is the path to a directory, creates a symbolic link at
<tt>dest/src</tt> pointing to <tt>src</tt>:

  FileUtils.touch('src2.txt')
  FileUtils.mkdir('destdir2')
  FileUtils.ln_s('src2.txt', 'destdir2')
  File.symlink?('destdir2/src2.txt') # => true

If <tt>src</tt> is an array of paths to existing files and <tt>dest</tt> is a
directory, for each child <tt>child</tt> in <tt>src</tt> creates a symbolic
link <tt>dest/child</tt> pointing to <tt>child</tt>:

  FileUtils.mkdir('srcdir3')
  FileUtils.touch('srcdir3/src0.txt')
  FileUtils.touch('srcdir3/src1.txt')
  FileUtils.mkdir('destdir3')
  FileUtils.ln_s(['srcdir3/src0.txt', 'srcdir3/src1.txt'], 'destdir3')
  File.symlink?('destdir3/src0.txt') # => true
  File.symlink?('destdir3/src1.txt') # => true

Keyword arguments:

* <tt>force: true</tt> - overwrites <tt>dest</tt> if it exists.
* <tt>relative: true</tt> - create links relative to <tt>dest</tt>.
* <tt>noop: true</tt> - does not create links.
* <tt>verbose: true</tt> - prints an equivalent command:

    FileUtils.ln_s('src0.txt', 'dest0.txt', noop: true, verbose: true)
    FileUtils.ln_s('src1.txt', 'destdir1', noop: true, verbose: true)
    FileUtils.ln_s('src2.txt', 'dest2.txt', force: true, noop: true, verbose: true)
    FileUtils.ln_s(['srcdir3/src0.txt', 'srcdir3/src1.txt'], 'destdir3', noop: true, verbose: true)

  Output:

    ln -s src0.txt dest0.txt
    ln -s src1.txt destdir1
    ln -sf src2.txt dest2.txt
    ln -s srcdir3/src0.txt srcdir3/src1.txt destdir3

Related: FileUtils.ln_sf.

FileUtils#ln_sf.name: ln_sf
FileUtils#ln_sf.comment:
Like FileUtils.ln_s, but always with keyword argument <tt>force: true</tt>
given.

FileUtils#ln_sr.name: ln_sr
FileUtils#ln_sr.params: (src, dest, target_directory: true, force: nil, noop: nil, verbose: nil)
FileUtils#ln_sr.comment: Like FileUtils.ln_s, but create links relative to <tt>dest</tt>.

FileUtils#makedirs.name: makedirs
FileUtils#makedirs.params: (list, mode: nil, noop: nil, verbose: nil)

FileUtils#mkdir.name: mkdir
FileUtils#mkdir.params: (list, mode: nil, noop: nil, verbose: nil)
FileUtils#mkdir.call_seq: FileUtils.mkdir(*paths, mode: 0775, noop: nil, verbose: nil) -> array_of_paths or nil
FileUtils#mkdir.comment:
Argument <tt>paths</tt> may be one path or an array of paths;
each must be {interpretable as a path}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Path+Arguments].
By default, creates a directory entry at each of the given <tt>paths</tt>;
each directory has permissions <tt>0775</tt>;
returns an array of the paths:
  FileUtils.mkdir('foo')                 # => ["foo"]
FileUtils.mkdir(%w[bar baz])           # => ["bar", "baz"]
File.stat(Dir.new('foo')).mode.to_s(8) # => "40775"
File.stat(Dir.new('bar')).mode.to_s(8) # => "40775"
File.stat(Dir.new('baz')).mode.to_s(8) # => "40775"
FileUtils.rmdir(%w[foo bar baz])       # => ["foo", "bar", "baz"]

Raises an exception if for any reason a directory cannot be created;
a common reason is that the directory already exists.
With keyword argument <tt>mode</tt> given,
creates directories with the given permissions:
  FileUtils.mkdir('bar', mode: 0664)
File.stat(Dir.new('bar')).mode.to_s(8) # => "40664"
FileUtils.rmdir('bar')

With keyword argument <tt>noop</tt> given as <tt>true</tt>,
does not create directories;
returns <tt>nil</tt>
  FileUtils.mkdir('foo', noop: true) # => nil
Dir.exist?('foo')                  # => false

With keyword argument <tt>verbose</tt> given as <tt>true</tt>,
prints a shell command:
  FileUtils.mkdir('foo', verbose: true)
FileUtils.mkdir(%w[bar baz], mode: 0644, verbose: true)
FileUtils.mkdir(%w[bar baz], mode: 0644, verbose: true, noop: true)

Output:
  mkdir foo
mkdir -m 644 bar baz
mkdir -m 644 bar baz

Note that in the last call above (containing <tt>noop: true</tt>)
the existence of the directory is not checked.
Related: FileUtils.mkdir_p.

FileUtils#mkdir_p.name: mkdir_p
FileUtils#mkdir_p.params: (list, mode: nil, noop: nil, verbose: nil)
FileUtils#mkdir_p.comment: Creates directories at the paths in the given list (a single path or an array of paths), also creating ancestor directories as needed; returns list if it is an array, [list] otherwise. Argument list or its elements should be {interpretable as paths}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Path+Arguments]. With no keyword arguments, creates a directory at each path in list, along with any needed ancestor directories, by calling: Dir.mkdir(path, mode); see {Dir.mkdir}[rdoc-ref:Dir.mkdir]: FileUtils.mkdir_p(%w[tmp0/tmp1 tmp2/tmp3]) # => ["tmp0/tmp1", "tmp2/tmp3"] FileUtils.mkdir_p('tmp4/tmp5') # => ["tmp4/tmp5"] Keyword arguments: * mode: mode - also calls File.chmod(mode, path); see {File.chmod}[rdoc-ref:File.chmod]. * noop: true - does not create directories. * verbose: true - prints an equivalent command: FileUtils.mkdir_p(%w[tmp0 tmp1], verbose: true) FileUtils.mkdir_p(%w[tmp2 tmp3], mode: 0700, verbose: true) Output: mkdir -p tmp0 tmp1 mkdir -p -m 700 tmp2 tmp3 Raises an exception if for any reason a directory cannot be created. FileUtils.mkpath and FileUtils.makedirs are aliases for FileUtils.mkdir_p. Related: FileUtils.mkdir.

FileUtils#mkpath.name: mkpath
FileUtils#mkpath.params: (list, mode: nil, noop: nil, verbose: nil)

FileUtils#move.name: move
FileUtils#move.params: (src, dest, force: nil, noop: nil, verbose: nil, secure: nil)

FileUtils#mv.name: mv
FileUtils#mv.params: (src, dest, force: nil, noop: nil, verbose: nil, secure: nil)
FileUtils#mv.comment:
Moves entries.

Arguments <tt>src</tt> (a single path or an array of paths) and <tt>dest</tt>
(a single path) should be {interpretable as
paths}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Path+Arguments].

If <tt>src</tt> and <tt>dest</tt> are on different file systems, first copies,
then removes <tt>src</tt>.

May cause a local vulnerability if not called with keyword argument
<tt>secure: true</tt>; see {Avoiding the TOCTTOU
Vulnerability}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Avoiding+the+TOCTTOU+Vulnerability].

If <tt>src</tt> is the path to a single file or directory and <tt>dest</tt>
does not exist, moves <tt>src</tt> to <tt>dest</tt>:

  tree('src0')
  # => src0
  #    |-- src0.txt
  #    `-- src1.txt
  File.exist?('dest0') # => false
  FileUtils.mv('src0', 'dest0')
  File.exist?('src0')  # => false
  tree('dest0')
  # => dest0
  #    |-- src0.txt
  #    `-- src1.txt

If <tt>src</tt> is an array of paths to files and directories and
<tt>dest</tt> is the path to a directory, copies from each path in the array
to <tt>dest</tt>:

  File.file?('src1.txt') # => true
  tree('src1')
  # => src1
  #    |-- src.dat
  #    `-- src.txt
  Dir.empty?('dest1')    # => true
  FileUtils.mv(['src1.txt', 'src1'], 'dest1')
  tree('dest1')
  # => dest1
  #    |-- src1
  #    |   |-- src.dat
  #    |   `-- src.txt
  #    `-- src1.txt

Keyword arguments:

* <tt>force: true</tt> - if the move includes removing <tt>src</tt> (that is,
  if <tt>src</tt> and <tt>dest</tt> are on different file systems), ignores
  raised exceptions of StandardError and its descendants.
* <tt>noop: true</tt> - does not move files.
* <tt>secure: true</tt> - removes <tt>src</tt> securely; see details at
  FileUtils.remove_entry_secure.
* <tt>verbose: true</tt> - prints an equivalent command:

    FileUtils.mv('src0', 'dest0', noop: true, verbose: true)
    FileUtils.mv(['src1.txt', 'src1'], 'dest1', noop: true, verbose: true)

  Output:

    mv src0 dest0
    mv src1.txt src1 dest1

FileUtils#pwd.name: pwd
FileUtils#pwd.comment:
Returns a string containing the path to the current directory:

  FileUtils.pwd # => "/rdoc/fileutils"

Related: FileUtils.cd.

FileUtils#remove.name: remove
FileUtils#remove.params: (list, force: nil, noop: nil, verbose: nil)

FileUtils#remove_dir.name: remove_dir
FileUtils#remove_dir.comment:
Recursively removes the directory entry given by <tt>path</tt>, which should
be the entry for a regular file, a symbolic link, or a directory.

Argument <tt>path</tt> should be {interpretable as a
path}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Path+Arguments].

Optional argument <tt>force</tt> specifies whether to ignore raised exceptions
of StandardError and its descendants.

Related: {methods for deleting}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Deleting].

FileUtils#remove_entry.name: remove_entry
FileUtils#remove_entry.comment:
Removes the entry given by <tt>path</tt>, which should be the entry for a
regular file, a symbolic link, or a directory.

Argument <tt>path</tt> should be {interpretable as a
path}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Path+Arguments].

Optional argument <tt>force</tt> specifies whether to ignore raised exceptions
of StandardError and its descendants.

Related: FileUtils.remove_entry_secure.

FileUtils#remove_entry_secure.name: remove_entry_secure
FileUtils#remove_entry_secure.comment:
Securely removes the entry given by <tt>path</tt>, which should be the entry
for a regular file, a symbolic link, or a directory.

Argument <tt>path</tt> should be {interpretable as a
path}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Path+Arguments].

Avoids a local vulnerability that can exist in certain circumstances; see
{Avoiding the TOCTTOU
Vulnerability}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Avoiding+the+TOCTTOU+Vulnerability].

Optional argument <tt>force</tt> specifies whether to ignore raised exceptions
of StandardError and its descendants.

Related: {methods for deleting}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Deleting].

FileUtils#remove_file.name: remove_file
FileUtils#remove_file.comment:
Removes the file entry given by <tt>path</tt>, which should be the entry for a
regular file or a symbolic link.

Argument <tt>path</tt> should be {interpretable as a
path}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Path+Arguments].

Optional argument <tt>force</tt> specifies whether to ignore raised exceptions
of StandardError and its descendants.

Related: {methods for deleting}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Deleting].

FileUtils#rm.name: rm
FileUtils#rm.params: (list, force: nil, noop: nil, verbose: nil)
FileUtils#rm.comment:
Removes entries at the paths in the given <tt>list</tt> (a single path or an
array of paths) returns <tt>list</tt>, if it is an array, <tt>[list]</tt>
otherwise.

Argument <tt>list</tt> or its elements should be {interpretable as
paths}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Path+Arguments].

With no keyword arguments, removes files at the paths given in <tt>list</tt>:

  FileUtils.touch(['src0.txt', 'src0.dat'])
  FileUtils.rm(['src0.dat', 'src0.txt']) # => ["src0.dat", "src0.txt"]

Keyword arguments:

* <tt>force: true</tt> - ignores raised exceptions of StandardError and its
  descendants.
* <tt>noop: true</tt> - does not remove files; returns <tt>nil</tt>.
* <tt>verbose: true</tt> - prints an equivalent command:

    FileUtils.rm(['src0.dat', 'src0.txt'], noop: true, verbose: true)

  Output:

    rm src0.dat src0.txt

Related: {methods for deleting}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Deleting].

FileUtils#rm_f.name: rm_f
FileUtils#rm_f.comment:
Equivalent to:

  FileUtils.rm(list, force: true, **kwargs)

Argument <tt>list</tt> (a single path or an array of paths) should be
{interpretable as paths}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Path+Arguments].

See FileUtils.rm for keyword arguments.

Related: {methods for deleting}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Deleting].

FileUtils#rm_r.name: rm_r
FileUtils#rm_r.params: (list, force: nil, noop: nil, verbose: nil, secure: nil)
FileUtils#rm_r.comment:
Removes entries at the paths in the given <tt>list</tt> (a single path or an
array of paths); returns <tt>list</tt>, if it is an array, <tt>[list]</tt>
otherwise.

Argument <tt>list</tt> or its elements should be {interpretable as
paths}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Path+Arguments].

May cause a local vulnerability if not called with keyword argument
<tt>secure: true</tt>; see {Avoiding the TOCTTOU
Vulnerability}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Avoiding+the+TOCTTOU+Vulnerability].

For each file path, removes the file at that path:

  FileUtils.touch(['src0.txt', 'src0.dat'])
  FileUtils.rm_r(['src0.dat', 'src0.txt'])
  File.exist?('src0.txt') # => false
  File.exist?('src0.dat') # => false

For each directory path, recursively removes files and directories:

  tree('src1')
  # => src1
  #    |-- dir0
  #    |   |-- src0.txt
  #    |   `-- src1.txt
  #    `-- dir1
  #        |-- src2.txt
  #        `-- src3.txt
  FileUtils.rm_r('src1')
  File.exist?('src1') # => false

Keyword arguments:

* <tt>force: true</tt> - ignores raised exceptions of StandardError and its
  descendants.
* <tt>noop: true</tt> - does not remove entries; returns <tt>nil</tt>.
* <tt>secure: true</tt> - removes <tt>src</tt> securely; see details at
  FileUtils.remove_entry_secure.
* <tt>verbose: true</tt> - prints an equivalent command:

    FileUtils.rm_r(['src0.dat', 'src0.txt'], noop: true, verbose: true)
    FileUtils.rm_r('src1', noop: true, verbose: true)

  Output:

    rm -r src0.dat src0.txt
    rm -r src1

Related: {methods for deleting}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Deleting].

FileUtils#rm_rf.name: rm_rf
FileUtils#rm_rf.params: (list, noop: nil, verbose: nil, secure: nil)
FileUtils#rm_rf.comment:
Equivalent to:

  FileUtils.rm_r(list, force: true, **kwargs)

Argument <tt>list</tt> or its elements should be {interpretable as
paths}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Path+Arguments].

May cause a local vulnerability if not called with keyword argument
<tt>secure: true</tt>; see {Avoiding the TOCTTOU
Vulnerability}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Avoiding+the+TOCTTOU+Vulnerability].

See FileUtils.rm_r for keyword arguments.

Related: {methods for deleting}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Deleting].

FileUtils#rmdir.name: rmdir
FileUtils#rmdir.params: (list, parents: nil, noop: nil, verbose: nil)
FileUtils#rmdir.comment:
Removes directories at the paths in the given <tt>list</tt> (a single path or
an array of paths); returns <tt>list</tt>, if it is an array, <tt>[list]</tt>
otherwise.

Argument <tt>list</tt> or its elements should be {interpretable as
paths}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Path+Arguments].

With no keyword arguments, removes the directory at each <tt>path</tt> in
<tt>list</tt>, by calling: <tt>Dir.rmdir(path)</tt>; see
{Dir.rmdir}[rdoc-ref:Dir.rmdir]:

  FileUtils.rmdir(%w[tmp0/tmp1 tmp2/tmp3]) # => ["tmp0/tmp1", "tmp2/tmp3"]
  FileUtils.rmdir('tmp4/tmp5')             # => ["tmp4/tmp5"]

Keyword arguments:

* <tt>parents: true</tt> - removes successive ancestor directories if empty.
* <tt>noop: true</tt> - does not remove directories.
* <tt>verbose: true</tt> - prints an equivalent command:

    FileUtils.rmdir(%w[tmp0/tmp1 tmp2/tmp3], parents: true, verbose: true)
    FileUtils.rmdir('tmp4/tmp5', parents: true, verbose: true)

  Output:

    rmdir -p tmp0/tmp1 tmp2/tmp3
    rmdir -p tmp4/tmp5

Raises an exception if a directory does not exist or if for any reason a
directory cannot be removed.

Related: {methods for deleting}[rdoc-ref:FileUtils@Deleting].

FileUtils#rmtree.name: rmtree
FileUtils#rmtree.params: (list, noop: nil, verbose: nil, secure: nil)

FileUtils#symlink.name: symlink
FileUtils#symlink.params: (src, dest, force: nil, relative: false, target_directory: true, noop: nil, verbose: nil)

FileUtils#touch.name: touch
FileUtils#touch.params: (list, noop: nil, verbose: nil, mtime: nil, nocreate: nil)
