Gem::read_binary.name: read_binary
Gem::read_binary.comment: Safely read a file in binary mode on all platforms.

Gem::register_default_spec.name: register_default_spec
Gem::register_default_spec.comment:
Register a Gem::Specification for default gem.

Two formats for the specification are supported:

* MRI 2.0 style, where spec.files contains unprefixed require names. The
  spec's filenames will be registered as-is.
* New style, where spec.files contains files prefixed with paths from
  spec.require_paths. The prefixes are stripped before registering the spec's
  filenames. Unprefixed files are omitted.

Gem::ruby.name: ruby
Gem::ruby.comment: The path to the running Ruby interpreter.

Gem::ruby_abi.name: ruby_abi
Gem::ruby_abi.comment: The ABI scope for the currently running Ruby.

Gem::ruby_api_version.name: ruby_api_version
Gem::ruby_api_version.comment: Returns a String containing the API compatibility version of Ruby

Gem::ruby_version.name: ruby_version
Gem::ruby_version.comment: A Gem::Version for the currently running Ruby.

Gem::rubygems_version.name: rubygems_version
Gem::rubygems_version.comment: A Gem::Version for the currently running RubyGems

Gem::source_date_epoch.name: source_date_epoch
Gem::source_date_epoch.comment:
Returns the value of Gem.source_date_epoch_string, as a Time object.

This is used throughout RubyGems for enabling reproducible builds.

Gem::source_date_epoch_string.name: source_date_epoch_string
Gem::source_date_epoch_string.comment:
If the SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH environment variable is set, returns it's value.
Otherwise, returns DEFAULT_SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH as a string.

NOTE(@duckinator): The implementation is a tad weird because we want to:
  1. Make builds reproducible by default, by having this function always
     return the same result during a given run.
  2. Allow changing ENV['SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH'] at runtime, since multiple
     tests that set this variable will be run in a single process.

If you simplify this function and a lot of tests fail, that is likely due to
#2 above.

Details on SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH:
https://reproducible-builds.org/specs/source-date-epoch/

Gem::sources.name: sources
Gem::sources.comment:
Returns an Array of sources to fetch remote gems from. Uses default_sources if
the sources list is empty.

Gem::sources=.name: sources=
Gem::sources=.comment:
Need to be able to set the sources without calling Gem.sources.replace since
that would cause an infinite loop.

DOC: This comment is not documentation about the method itself, it's more of a
code comment about the implementation.

Gem::state_file.name: state_file
Gem::state_file.comment: The path to standard location of the user's state file.

Gem::state_home.name: state_home
Gem::state_home.comment: The path to standard location of the user's state directory.

Gem::suffix_pattern.name: suffix_pattern
Gem::suffix_pattern.comment: Glob pattern for require-able path suffixes.

Gem::target_rbconfig.name: target_rbconfig
Gem::target_rbconfig.comment:
The RbConfig object for the deployment target platform.

This is usually the same as the running platform, but may be different if you
are cross-compiling.

Gem::time.name: time
Gem::time.comment:
Prints the amount of time the supplied block takes to run using the debug UI
output.

Gem::try_activate.name: try_activate
Gem::try_activate.comment:
Try to activate a gem containing <tt>path</tt>. Returns true if activation
succeeded or wasn't needed because it was already activated. Returns false if
it can't find the path in a gem.

Gem::ui.name: ui
Gem::ui.comment: Lazily loads DefaultUserInteraction and returns the default UI.

Gem::use_gemdeps.name: use_gemdeps
Gem::use_gemdeps.comment:
Looks for a gem dependency file at <tt>path</tt> and activates the gems in the
file if found.  If the file is not found an ArgumentError is raised.

If <tt>path</tt> is not given the RUBYGEMS_GEMDEPS environment variable is
used, but if no file is found no exception is raised.

If '-' is given for <tt>path</tt> RubyGems searches up from the current
working directory for gem dependency files (gem.deps.rb, Gemfile, Isolate) and
activates the gems in the first one found.

You can run this automatically when rubygems starts.  To enable, set the
<tt>RUBYGEMS_GEMDEPS</tt> environment variable to either the path of your gem
dependencies file or "-" to auto-discover in parent directories.

NOTE: Enabling automatic discovery on multiuser systems can lead to execution
of arbitrary code when used from directories outside your control.

Gem::use_paths.name: use_paths
Gem::use_paths.comment:
Use the <tt>home</tt> and <tt>paths</tt> values for Gem.dir and Gem.path.
Used mainly by the unit tests to provide environment isolation.

Gem::use_psych?.name: use_psych?
Gem::use_psych?.comment: Returns true if the Psych YAML parser is enabled via configuration.

Gem::user_dir.name: user_dir
Gem::user_dir.comment: Path for gems in the user's home directory

Gem::user_home.name: user_home
Gem::user_home.comment: The home directory for the user.

Gem::write_binary.name: write_binary
Gem::write_binary.comment: Atomically write a file in binary mode on all platforms.

Gem::AtomicFileWriter::open.name: open
Gem::AtomicFileWriter::open.comment:
Write to a file atomically. Useful for situations where you don't want other
processes or threads to see half-written files.

Gem::AtomicFileWriter::byteslice_at_char.name: byteslice_at_char_boundary
Gem::AtomicFileWriter::byteslice_at_char.comment:
Returns the longest prefix of string that is at most max_bytesize bytes and
ends on a character boundary. A string that is invalid in its own encoding
would be cut back to its last valid prefix, discarding an unbounded part of
the name, so it is sliced as raw bytes instead and can still be cut
mid-character.

Gem::AvailableSet#each.name: each
Gem::AvailableSet#each.comment: Yields each Tuple in this AvailableSet

Gem::AvailableSet#each_spec.name: each_spec
Gem::AvailableSet#each_spec.comment: Yields the Gem::Specification for each Tuple in this AvailableSet

Gem::AvailableSet#find_all.name: find_all
Gem::AvailableSet#find_all.comment: Used by the Resolver, the protocol to use a AvailableSet as a search Set.

Gem::AvailableSet#to_request_set.name: to_request_set
Gem::AvailableSet#to_request_set.comment:
Converts this AvailableSet into a RequestSet that can be used to install gems.

If <tt>development</tt> is :none then no development dependencies are
installed. Other options are :shallow for only direct development dependencies
of the gems in this set or :all for all development dependencies.

Gem::BasicSpecification.name: Gem::BasicSpecification
Gem::BasicSpecification.comment:
BasicSpecification is an abstract class which implements some common code used
by both Specification and StubSpecification.

Gem::BasicSpecification#activated?.name: activated?
Gem::BasicSpecification#activated?.comment: True when the gem has been activated

Gem::BasicSpecification#base_dir.name: base_dir
Gem::BasicSpecification#base_dir.comment:
Returns the full path to the base gem directory.

eg: /usr/local/lib/ruby/gems/1.8

Gem::BasicSpecification#base_dir_priorit.name: base_dir_priority
Gem::BasicSpecification#base_dir_priorit.comment: Gems higher up in <tt>gem_path</tt> take precedence

Gem::BasicSpecification#contains_requira.name: contains_requirable_file?
Gem::BasicSpecification#contains_requira.comment: Return true if this spec can require <tt>file</tt>.

Gem::BasicSpecification#content_address.name: content_address
Gem::BasicSpecification#content_address.comment:
The content address of this gem, or <tt>nil</tt> when it is not
content-addressable.

Gem::BasicSpecification#default_gem_prio.name: default_gem_priority
Gem::BasicSpecification#default_gem_prio.comment: Regular gems take precedence over default gems

Gem::BasicSpecification#extension_dir.name: extension_dir
Gem::BasicSpecification#extension_dir.comment: Returns full path to the directory where gem's extensions are installed.

Gem::BasicSpecification#extensions_dir.name: extensions_dir
Gem::BasicSpecification#extensions_dir.comment: Returns path to the extensions directory.

Gem::BasicSpecification#full_gem_path.name: full_gem_path
Gem::BasicSpecification#full_gem_path.comment:
The full path to the gem (install path + full name).

TODO: This is duplicated with #gem_dir. Eventually either of them should be
deprecated.

Gem::BasicSpecification#full_name.name: full_name
Gem::BasicSpecification#full_name.comment:
Returns the full name (name-version) of this Gem. Content address is included
(name-version-content_address) if the gem is content-addressed (eligible and
has a valid content address). Platform information is included
(name-version-platform) if it is specified and not the default Ruby platform.

Gem::BasicSpecification#full_name_with_l.name: full_name_with_location
Gem::BasicSpecification#full_name_with_l.comment:
Returns the full name of this Gem (see `Gem::BasicSpecification#full_name`).
Information about where the gem is installed is also included if not installed
in the default GEM_HOME.

Gem::BasicSpecification#full_require_pat.name: full_require_paths
Gem::BasicSpecification#full_require_pat.comment:
Full paths in the gem to add to <tt>$LOAD_PATH</tt> when this gem is
activated.

Gem::BasicSpecification#gem_dir.name: gem_dir
Gem::BasicSpecification#gem_dir.comment:
Returns the full path to this spec's gem directory. eg:
/usr/local/lib/ruby/1.8/gems/mygem-1.0

TODO: This is duplicated with #full_gem_path. Eventually either of them should
be deprecated.

Gem::BasicSpecification#gems_dir.name: gems_dir
Gem::BasicSpecification#gems_dir.comment:
Returns the full path to the gems directory containing this spec's gem
directory. eg: /usr/local/lib/ruby/1.8/gems

Gem::BasicSpecification#ignored?.name: ignored?
Gem::BasicSpecification#ignored?.comment: Return true if this spec should be ignored because it's missing extensions.

Gem::BasicSpecification#lib_dirs_glob.name: lib_dirs_glob
Gem::BasicSpecification#lib_dirs_glob.comment:
Returns a string usable in Dir.glob to match all requirable paths for this
spec.

Gem::BasicSpecification#matches_for_glob.name: matches_for_glob
Gem::BasicSpecification#matches_for_glob.comment: Return all files in this gem that match for <tt>glob</tt>.

Gem::BasicSpecification#plugins.name: plugins
Gem::BasicSpecification#plugins.comment: Returns the list of plugins in this spec.

Gem::BasicSpecification#require_paths.name: require_paths
Gem::BasicSpecification#require_paths.comment:
Paths in the gem to add to <tt>$LOAD_PATH</tt> when this gem is activated.

See also #require_paths=

If you have an extension you do not need to add <tt>"ext"</tt> to the require
path, the extension build process will copy the extension files into "lib" for
you.

The default value is <tt>"lib"</tt>

Usage:

  # If all library files are in the root directory...
  spec.require_path = '.'

Gem::BasicSpecification#source_paths.name: source_paths
Gem::BasicSpecification#source_paths.comment:
Returns the paths to the source files for use with analysis and documentation
tools.  These paths are relative to full_gem_path.

Gem::BasicSpecification#stubbed?.name: stubbed?
Gem::BasicSpecification#stubbed?.comment:
Whether this specification is stubbed - i.e. we have information about the gem
from a stub line, without having to evaluate the entire gemspec file.

Gem::BasicSpecification#to_fullpath.name: to_fullpath
Gem::BasicSpecification#to_fullpath.comment:
Full path of the target library file. If the file is not in this gem, return
nil.

Gem::BasicSpecification#to_spec.name: to_spec
Gem::BasicSpecification#to_spec.comment: Return a Gem::Specification from this gem

Gem::BasicSpecification#lib_dirs.name: lib_dirs
Gem::BasicSpecification#lib_dirs.comment:
Returns the require_paths of this gem as a string usable in Dir.glob, relative
to full_gem_path.

Gem::BundlerSettings.name: Gem::BundlerSettings
Gem::BundlerSettings.comment:
Reads Bundler's settings without loading Bundler, for the RubyGems commands
that have to agree with something the user configured for Bundler.

Follows Bundler::Settings: the application config file wins over the
BUNDLE_<NAME> environment variable, which wins over the user config file, and
BUNDLE_IGNORE_CONFIG drops both files.

Gem::BundlerSettings::[].comment:
The configured value of Bundler setting <tt>name</tt>, or nil when it is
unset.

Gem::BundlerSettings::env.name: env
Gem::BundlerSettings::env.comment:
The value of Bundler setting <tt>name</tt> from the environment, or nil when
the variable is unset or empty.

Gem::BundlerSettings::from_config_files.name: from_config_files
Gem::BundlerSettings::from_config_files.comment:
The value of Bundler setting <tt>name</tt> from the config files only,
application file first.  Callers that read the environment variable ahead of
the files pair this with .env.

Gem::BundlerSettings::gemfile_path.name: gemfile_path
Gem::BundlerSettings::gemfile_path.comment:
The gem dependencies file above the working directory, or nil when there is
none.  RubyGems recognizes a couple of names Bundler does not, so a directory
holding only one of those is where the two disagree.

Gem::BundlerSettings::app_config_file.name: app_config_file
Gem::BundlerSettings::app_config_file.comment:
The config file for the application, honoring BUNDLE_APP_CONFIG the way
Bundler.app_config_path does: an absolute path is used as given, and a
relative one is resolved against the directory holding the Gemfile.

Gem::BundlerSettings::config_value.name: config_value
Gem::BundlerSettings::config_value.comment:
A config file that cannot be read or parsed leaves the setting unconfigured
rather than aborting the gem command that only wanted to consult it.  The
rescue is deliberately broad: Gem::YAMLSerializer signals a bad document with
Psych::DisallowedClass, Psych::BadAlias and Psych::SyntaxError, which share no
class this method could name, and a reader that only ever returns a value or
nil gains nothing from letting a newly added one through.

Gem::BundlerVersionFinder::bundle_config.name: bundle_config_version
Gem::BundlerVersionFinder::bundle_config.comment:
BUNDLE_VERSION is read before the config files here, unlike everywhere else in
Bundler, so the env var alone is enough to pick the version that runs without
editing a config file first.

Gem::Command.name: Gem::Command
Gem::Command.comment:
Base class for all Gem commands.  When creating a new gem command, define
#initialize, #execute, #arguments, #defaults_str, #description and #usage (as
appropriate).  See the above mentioned methods for details.

A very good example to look at is Gem::Commands::ContentsCommand

Gem::Command::add_specific_extra_args.name: add_specific_extra_args
Gem::Command::add_specific_extra_args.comment:
Add a list of extra arguments for the given command.  <tt>args</tt> may be an
array or a string to be split on white space.

Gem::Command::new.name: new
Gem::Command::new.comment:
Initializes a generic gem command named <tt>command</tt>.  <tt>summary</tt> is
a short description displayed in `gem help commands`.  <tt>defaults</tt> are
the default options.  Defaults should be mirrored in #defaults_str, unless
there are none.

When defining a new command subclass, use add_option to add command-line
switches.

Unhandled arguments (gem names, files, etc.) are left in
<tt>options[:args]</tt>.

Gem::Command::specific_extra_args.name: specific_extra_args
Gem::Command::specific_extra_args.comment:
Return an array of extra arguments for the command.  The extra arguments come
from the gem configuration file read at program startup.

Gem::Command::specific_extra_args_hash.name: specific_extra_args_hash
Gem::Command::specific_extra_args_hash.comment: Accessor for the specific extra args hash (self initializing).

Gem::Command#add_option.name: add_option
Gem::Command#add_option.comment:
Add a command-line option and handler to the command.

See Gem::OptionParser#make_switch for an explanation of <tt>opts</tt>.

<tt>handler</tt> will be called with two values, the value of the argument and
the options hash.

If the first argument of add_option is a Symbol, it's used to group options in
output.  See `gem help list` for an example.

Gem::Command#arguments.name: arguments
Gem::Command#arguments.comment:
Override to provide details of the arguments a command takes.  It should
return a left-justified string, one argument per line.

For example:

  def usage
    "#{program_name} FILE [FILE ...]"
  end

  def arguments
    "FILE          name of file to find"
  end

Gem::Command#begins?.name: begins?
Gem::Command#begins?.comment: True if <tt>long</tt> begins with the characters from <tt>short</tt>.

Gem::Command#defaults_str.name: defaults_str
Gem::Command#defaults_str.comment:
Override to display the default values of the command options. (similar to
<tt>arguments</tt>, but displays the default values).

For example:

  def defaults_str
    --no-gems-first --no-all
  end

Gem::Command#deprecate_option.name: deprecate_option
Gem::Command#deprecate_option.comment:
Mark a command-line option as deprecated, and optionally specify a deprecation
horizon.

Note that with the current implementation, every version of the option needs
to be explicitly deprecated, so to deprecate an option defined as

  add_option('-t', '--[no-]test', 'Set test mode') do |value, options|
    # ... stuff ...
  end

you would need to explicitly add a call to `deprecate_option` for every
version of the option you want to deprecate, like

  deprecate_option('-t')
  deprecate_option('--test')
  deprecate_option('--no-test')

Gem::Command#description.name: description
Gem::Command#description.comment: Override to display a longer description of what this command does.

Gem::Command#execute.name: execute
Gem::Command#execute.comment:
Override to provide command handling.

#options will be filled in with your parsed options, unparsed options will be
left in <tt>options[:args]</tt>.

See also: #get_all_gem_names, #get_one_gem_name, #get_one_optional_argument

Gem::Command#get_all_gem_names.name: get_all_gem_names
Gem::Command#get_all_gem_names.comment: Get all gem names from the command line.

Gem::Command#get_all_gem_names_and_versi.name: get_all_gem_names_and_versions
Gem::Command#get_all_gem_names_and_versi.comment:
Get all [gem, version] from the command line.

An argument in the form gem:ver is pull apart into the gen name and version,
respectively.

Gem::Command#get_one_gem_name.name: get_one_gem_name
Gem::Command#get_one_gem_name.comment:
Get a single gem name from the command line.  Fail if there is no gem name or
if there is more than one gem name given.

Gem::Command#get_one_optional_argument.name: get_one_optional_argument
Gem::Command#get_one_optional_argument.comment:
Get a single optional argument from the command line.  If more than one
argument is given, return only the first. Return nil if none are given.

Gem::Command#handle_options.name: handle_options
Gem::Command#handle_options.comment: Handle the given list of arguments by parsing them and recording the results.

Gem::Command#handles?.name: handles?
Gem::Command#handles?.comment: True if the command handles the given argument list.

Gem::Command#invoke.name: invoke
Gem::Command#invoke.comment: Invoke the command with the given list of arguments.

Gem::Command#invoke_with_build_args.name: invoke_with_build_args
Gem::Command#invoke_with_build_args.comment:
Invoke the command with the given list of normal arguments and additional
build arguments.

Gem::Command#merge_options.name: merge_options
Gem::Command#merge_options.comment:
Merge a set of command options with the set of default options (without
modifying the default option hash).

Gem::Command#show_help.name: show_help
Gem::Command#show_help.comment: Display the help message for the command.

Gem::Command#show_lookup_failure.name: show_lookup_failure
Gem::Command#show_lookup_failure.params: (gem_name, version, errors, suppress_suggestions = false, required_by = nil)
Gem::Command#show_lookup_failure.comment: Display to the user that a gem couldn't be found and reasons why

Gem::Command#usage.name: usage
Gem::Command#usage.comment:
Override to display the usage for an individual gem command.

The text "[options]" is automatically appended to the usage text.

Gem::Command#when_invoked.name: when_invoked
Gem::Command#when_invoked.comment:
Call the given block when invoked.

Normal command invocations just executes the <tt>execute</tt> method of the
command.  Specifying an invocation block allows the test methods to override
the normal action of a command to determine that it has been invoked
correctly.

Gem::Command#add_parser_run_info.name: add_parser_run_info
Gem::Command#add_parser_run_info.comment:
Adds a section with <tt>title</tt> and <tt>content</tt> to the parser help
view.  Used for adding command arguments and default arguments.

Gem::Command#create_option_parser.name: create_option_parser
Gem::Command#create_option_parser.comment: Creates an option parser and fills it in with the help info for the command.

Gem::CommandManager.name: Gem::CommandManager
Gem::CommandManager.comment:
The command manager registers and installs all the individual sub-commands
supported by the gem command.

Extra commands can be provided by writing a rubygems_plugin.rb file in an
installed gem.  You should register your command against the
Gem::CommandManager instance, like this:

  # file rubygems_plugin.rb
  require 'rubygems/command_manager'

  Gem::CommandManager.instance.register_command :edit

You should put the implementation of your command in rubygems/commands.

  # file rubygems/commands/edit_command.rb
  class Gem::Commands::EditCommand < Gem::Command
    # ...
  end

See Gem::Command for instructions on writing gem commands.

Gem::CommandManager::instance.name: instance
Gem::CommandManager::instance.comment: Return the authoritative instance of the command manager.

Gem::CommandManager::new.name: new
Gem::CommandManager::new.comment: Register all the subcommands supported by the gem command.

Gem::CommandManager::reset.name: reset
Gem::CommandManager::reset.comment: Reset the authoritative instance of the command manager.

Gem::CommandManager#command_names.name: command_names
Gem::CommandManager#command_names.comment: Return a sorted list of all command names as strings.

Gem::CommandManager#instance.name: instance
Gem::CommandManager#instance.comment:
Returns self. Allows a CommandManager instance to stand in for the class
itself.

Gem::CommandManager#register_command.name: register_command
Gem::CommandManager#register_command.comment: Register the Symbol <tt>command</tt> as a gem command.

Gem::CommandManager#unregister_command.name: unregister_command
Gem::CommandManager#unregister_command.comment: Unregister the Symbol <tt>command</tt> as a gem command.

Gem::Commands.name: Gem::Commands
Gem::Commands.comment: Commands will be placed in this namespace

Gem::Commands::GenerateIndexCommand::new.name: new
Gem::Commands::GenerateIndexCommand::new.comment: remove_method(:initialize) warns, but removing new does not warn

Gem::Commands::InstallCommand.name: Gem::Commands::InstallCommand
Gem::Commands::InstallCommand.comment:
Gem installer command line tool

See `gem help install`

Gem::Commands::ListCommand.name: Gem::Commands::ListCommand
Gem::Commands::ListCommand.comment: Searches for gems starting with the supplied argument.

Gem::Commands::OutdatedCommand#execute_w.name: execute_with_cooldown
Gem::Commands::OutdatedCommand#execute_w.comment:
Like Gem::Specification.outdated_and_latest_version, but the newest version
outside the cooldown period becomes the update candidate, and newer versions
still within the period are annotated.

Gem::Commands::OutdatedCommand#partition.name: partition_by_cooldown
Gem::Commands::OutdatedCommand#partition.comment:
Splits [NameTuple, Gem::Source] pairs into versions outside and within the
cooldown period.  Tuples with an unknown publish time count as outside the
period, so the cooldown fails open.

Gem::Commands::SetupCommand.name: Gem::Commands::SetupCommand
Gem::Commands::SetupCommand.comment:
Installs RubyGems itself.  This command is ordinarily only available from a
RubyGems checkout or tarball.

Gem::Commands::UninstallCommand.name: Gem::Commands::UninstallCommand
Gem::Commands::UninstallCommand.comment:
Gem uninstaller command line tool

See `gem help uninstall`

Gem::Commands::UnpackCommand#find_in_cac.name: find_in_cache
Gem::Commands::UnpackCommand#find_in_cac.comment: Find cached filename in Gem.path. Returns nil if the file cannot be found.

Gem::Commands::UnpackCommand#get_path.name: get_path
Gem::Commands::UnpackCommand#get_path.comment:
Return the full path to the cached gem file matching the given name and
version requirement.  Returns 'nil' if no match.

Example:

  get_path 'rake', '> 0.4' # "/usr/lib/ruby/gems/1.8/cache/rake-0.4.2.gem"
  get_path 'rake', '< 0.1' # nil
  get_path 'rak'           # nil (exact name required)

Gem::Commands::UpdateCommand#update_ruby.name: update_rubygems
Gem::Commands::UpdateCommand#update_ruby.comment: Update RubyGems software to the latest version.

Gem::Commands::UpdateCommand#oldest_supp.name: oldest_supported_version
Gem::Commands::UpdateCommand#oldest_supp.comment:
Oldest version we support downgrading to. This is the version that originally
ships with the oldest supported patch version of ruby.

Gem::CompactIndexClient.name: Gem::CompactIndexClient
Gem::CompactIndexClient.comment:
The CompactIndexClient fetches and parses the compact index files (names,
versions and info/[gem]) served by a gem server, keeping a local cache so
subsequent fetches only transfer what changed.

This is the single shared client: Bundler ships a copy of it and uses it
underneath its own fetcher orchestration, injecting its fetcher and filesystem
access hook.

Gem::CompactIndexClient::filesystem_acce.name: filesystem_access
Gem::CompactIndexClient::filesystem_acce.comment:
Filesystem reads and writes funnel through this hook so that a host (e.g.
Bundler) can translate low-level Errno exceptions into its own friendlier
errors. The default just yields the path.

Gem::CompactIndexClient::new.name: new
Gem::CompactIndexClient::new.comment:
The client is instantiated with:
* `directory`: the root directory where the cache files are stored.
* `fetcher`: (optional) an object that responds to #call(uri_path, headers)
  and returns a Gem::Net::HTTP response. When the fetcher is not provided, the
  client only reads cached files from disk.

Gem::CompactIndexClient#fetch_info.name: fetch_info
Gem::CompactIndexClient#fetch_info.comment:
Fetches a single gem's info without consulting the versions index, using a
conditional request to refresh the cached file. Useful when only a few gems
are needed and the versions index download would dominate, as in gem install.

Gem::CompactIndexClient::Cache.name: Gem::CompactIndexClient::Cache
Gem::CompactIndexClient::Cache.comment:
Calls the Updater to update the cached files on disk, reads the cached files
and returns their contents.

Gem::CompactIndexClient::Cache#fetch_inf.name: fetch_info
Gem::CompactIndexClient::Cache#fetch_inf.comment:
Fetch a single gem's info file without consulting the versions index,
refreshing the cached file with a conditional request.

Gem::CompactIndexClient::Cache#validate_.name: validate_name!
Gem::CompactIndexClient::Cache#validate_.comment:
Gem names come from the remote index and are not otherwise validated, so
refuse anything that would escape the cache directory when used as a path
component.

Gem::CompactIndexClient::CacheFile.name: Gem::CompactIndexClient::CacheFile
Gem::CompactIndexClient::CacheFile.comment:
write cache files in a way that is robust to concurrent modifications if
digests are given, the checksums will be verified

Gem::CompactIndexClient::CacheFile::copy.name: copy
Gem::CompactIndexClient::CacheFile::copy.comment: Initialize with a copy of the original file, then yield the instance.

Gem::CompactIndexClient::CacheFile::writ.name: write
Gem::CompactIndexClient::CacheFile::writ.comment:
Write data to a temp file, then replace the original file with it verifying
the digests if given.

Gem::CompactIndexClient::CacheFile#appen.name: append
Gem::CompactIndexClient::CacheFile#appen.comment:
Returns false without appending when no digests since appending is too error
prone to do without digests.

Gem::CompactIndexClient::CacheFile#close.name: close
Gem::CompactIndexClient::CacheFile#close.comment:
Remove the temp file without replacing the original file. The file is
permanently closed.

Gem::CompactIndexClient::CacheFile#commi.name: commit
Gem::CompactIndexClient::CacheFile#commi.comment:
Replace the original file with the temp file without verifying digests. The
file is permanently closed.

Gem::CompactIndexClient::CacheFile#diges.name: digests=
Gem::CompactIndexClient::CacheFile#diges.comment: set the digests that will be verified at the end

Gem::CompactIndexClient::CacheFile#initi.name: initialize_digests
Gem::CompactIndexClient::CacheFile#initi.comment:
initialize the digests using CompactIndexClient::SUPPORTED_DIGESTS, or a
subset based on keys.

Gem::CompactIndexClient::CacheFile#open.name: open
Gem::CompactIndexClient::CacheFile#open.comment:
Open the temp file for writing, reusing original permissions, yielding the IO
object.

Gem::CompactIndexClient::CacheFile#reset.name: reset_digests
Gem::CompactIndexClient::CacheFile#reset.comment: reset the digests so they don't contain any previously read data

Gem::CompactIndexClient::CacheFile#verif.name: verify
Gem::CompactIndexClient::CacheFile#verif.comment: Verify the digests, returning true on match, false on mismatch.

Gem::CompactIndexClient::HTTPFetcher.name: Gem::CompactIndexClient::HTTPFetcher
Gem::CompactIndexClient::HTTPFetcher.comment:
Fetches compact index files relative to <tt>base_uri</tt> using
Gem::RemoteFetcher's connection infrastructure (proxy, TLS, connection
pooling). Implements the fetcher interface expected by
Gem::CompactIndexClient: #call(path, headers) returning a Gem::Net::HTTP
response.

Gem::CompactIndexClient::HTTPFetcher#req.name: request
Gem::CompactIndexClient::HTTPFetcher#req.comment:
The callers fall back to the Marshal index when a fetch fails, and they only
recognize a failure that arrives as a FetchError.

Gem::CompactIndexClient::Parser::new.name: new
Gem::CompactIndexClient::Parser::new.comment:
`compact_index` - an object responding to #names, #versions, #info(name,
checksum),
  returning the file contents as a string

Gem::CompactIndexClient::Parser#parse_ve.name: parse_version_checksum
Gem::CompactIndexClient::Parser#parse_ve.comment:
This is mostly the same as `split(" ", 3)` but it avoids allocating extra
objects. This method gets called at least once for every gem when parsing
versions.

Gem::CompactIndexClient::Updater.name: Gem::CompactIndexClient::Updater
Gem::CompactIndexClient::Updater.comment:
Updates the cached files on disk, keeping them in sync with the server using
conditional requests (ETag) and ranged requests where possible.

Gem::CompactIndexClient::Updater#byte_se.name: byte_sequence
Gem::CompactIndexClient::Updater#byte_se.comment:
Unwrap surrounding colons (byte sequence) The wrapping characters must be
matched or we return nil. Also handles quotes because right now rubygems.org
sends them.

Gem::CompactIndexClient::Updater#parse_d.name: parse_digests
Gem::CompactIndexClient::Updater#parse_d.comment:
Unwraps and returns a Hash of digest algorithms and base64 values according to
RFC 8941 Structured Field Values for HTTP.
https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8941#name-parsing-a-byte-sequence Ignores
unsupported algorithms.

Gem::CompactIndexClient::Updater#replace.name: replace
Gem::CompactIndexClient::Updater#replace.comment: request without range header to get the full file or a 304 Not Modified

Gem::ConfigFile.name: Gem::ConfigFile
Gem::ConfigFile.comment:
Gem::ConfigFile RubyGems options and gem command options from gemrc.

gemrc is a YAML file that uses strings to match gem command arguments and
symbols to match RubyGems options.

Gem command arguments use a String key that matches the command name and allow
you to specify default arguments:

  install: --no-rdoc --no-ri
  update: --no-rdoc --no-ri

You can use <tt>gem:</tt> to set default arguments for all commands.

RubyGems options use symbol keys.  Valid options are:

<tt>:backtrace</tt>:
  See #backtrace

<tt>:bulk_threshold</tt>:
  See #bulk_threshold

<tt>:cooldown</tt>:
  See #cooldown

<tt>:verbose</tt>:
  See #verbose

<tt>:update_sources</tt>:
  See #update_sources

<tt>:concurrent_downloads</tt>:
  See #concurrent_downloads

<tt>:cert_expiration_length_days</tt>:
  See #cert_expiration_length_days

<tt>:install_extension_in_lib</tt>:
  See #install_extension_in_lib

<tt>:ipv4_fallback_enabled</tt>:
  See #ipv4_fallback_enabled

<tt>:global_gem_cache</tt>:
  See #global_gem_cache

<tt>:use_psych</tt>:
  See #use_psych

<tt>:credential_store</tt>:
  See #credential_store

<tt>:gemhome</tt>:
  See #home

<tt>:gempath</tt>:
  See #path

<tt>:sources</tt>:
  Sets Gem::sources

<tt>:disable_default_gem_server</tt>:
  See #disable_default_gem_server

<tt>:ssl_verify_mode</tt>:
  See #ssl_verify_mode

<tt>:ssl_ca_cert</tt>:
  See #ssl_ca_cert

<tt>:ssl_client_cert</tt>:
  See #ssl_client_cert

gemrc files may exist in various locations and are read and merged in the
following order:

* system wide (/etc/gemrc)
* per user (~/.gemrc)
* per environment (gemrc files listed in the GEMRC environment variable)

Gem::ConfigFile::new.name: new
Gem::ConfigFile::new.comment:
Create the config file object.  <tt>args</tt> is the list of arguments from
the command line.

The following command line options are handled early here rather than later at
the time most command options are processed.

<tt>--config-file</tt>, <tt>--config-file==NAME</tt>:
  Obviously these need to be handled by the ConfigFile object to ensure we get
  the right config file.

<tt>--backtrace</tt>:
  Backtrace needs to be turned on early so that errors before normal option
  parsing can be properly handled.

<tt>--debug</tt>:
  Enable Ruby level debug messages.  Handled early for the same reason as
  --backtrace.

Gem::ConfigFile::credential_store_accoun.name: credential_store_account
Gem::ConfigFile::credential_store_accoun.comment:
Built on the same normalized form the credentials file uses, so the two never
disagree about which host a spelling refers to. Userinfo is dropped because
the account reaches the backend as a command argument, where any other user on
the machine can read it.

Gem::ConfigFile::normalize_credentials_k.name: normalize_credentials_key
Gem::ConfigFile::normalize_credentials_k.comment:
A trailing slash, or the underscore pair standing in for a dot, comes back
rewritten from #load_file, so a raw host would silently miss.

Gem::ConfigFile#api_keys.name: api_keys
Gem::ConfigFile#api_keys.comment:
Hash of RubyGems.org and alternate API keys, as they appear in the credentials
file. Keys held in the credential store are not included, so this is not the
full set of keys a command can authenticate with. Use
#credential_store_api_key_for or #credential_store_default_api_key to reach
those.

Gem::ConfigFile#backtrace.name: backtrace
Gem::ConfigFile#backtrace.comment: True if we print backtraces on errors.

Gem::ConfigFile#check_credentials_permis.name: check_credentials_permissions
Gem::ConfigFile#check_credentials_permis.comment:
Checks the permissions of the credentials file.  If they are not 0600 an error
message is displayed and RubyGems aborts.

Gem::ConfigFile#config_file_name.name: config_file_name
Gem::ConfigFile#config_file_name.comment: The name of the configuration file.

Gem::ConfigFile#credential_store_api_key.name: credential_store_api_key_for
Gem::ConfigFile#credential_store_api_key.comment:
Looks up <tt>host</tt>'s own API key from the credential store, when the
#credential_store setting is on. Only the host-specific account is consulted:
falling back to the default account here would send the RubyGems.org key to
whatever host was asked for, ahead of that host's own key in the credentials
file. #credential_store_default_api_key covers the default account, at the
precedence the credentials file uses for it.

Gem::ConfigFile#credential_store_default.name: credential_store_default_api_key
Gem::ConfigFile#credential_store_default.comment:
The default RubyGems.org API key from the credential store, or <tt>nil</tt>.
This is the stored counterpart of #rubygems_api_key, and belongs at the same
point in the lookup order.

Gem::ConfigFile#credential_store_read_fa.name: credential_store_read_failed_for?
Gem::ConfigFile#credential_store_read_fa.comment:
True when a read for <tt>host</tt> failed rather than finding nothing. Whether
the store holds a key for it is unknowable once the read fails, which is the
point: a caller that would otherwise fall through to a key belonging to a
different host has to treat "unknown" differently from "absent".

Gem::ConfigFile#last_update_check.name: last_update_check
Gem::ConfigFile#last_update_check.comment: Reads time of last update check from state file

Gem::ConfigFile#last_update_check=.name: last_update_check=
Gem::ConfigFile#last_update_check=.comment: Writes time of last update check to state file

Gem::ConfigFile#really_verbose.name: really_verbose
Gem::ConfigFile#really_verbose.comment: Really verbose mode gives you extra output.

Gem::ConfigFile#rubygems_api_key=.name: rubygems_api_key=
Gem::ConfigFile#rubygems_api_key=.comment: Sets the RubyGems.org API key to <tt>api_key</tt>

Gem::ConfigFile#set_api_key.name: set_api_key
Gem::ConfigFile#set_api_key.comment: Set a specific host's API key to <tt>api_key</tt>

Gem::ConfigFile#state_file_name.name: state_file_name
Gem::ConfigFile#state_file_name.comment: The name of the state file.

Gem::ConfigFile#state_file_writable?.name: state_file_writable?
Gem::ConfigFile#state_file_writable?.comment:
Check state file is writable. Creates empty file if not present to ensure we
can write to it.

Gem::ConfigFile#unset_api_key!.name: unset_api_key!
Gem::ConfigFile#unset_api_key!.comment:
Remove the +~/.gem/credentials+ file to clear all the current sessions, and
every RubyGems key from the credential store when the #credential_store
setting is on, including keys saved for other hosts with <tt>gem signin
--host</tt>.

Gem::ConfigFile#write.name: write
Gem::ConfigFile#write.comment: Writes out this config file, replacing its source.

Gem::ConflictError.name: Gem::ConflictError
Gem::ConflictError.comment: Raised when there are conflicting gem specs loaded

Gem::ConsoleUI.name: Gem::ConsoleUI
Gem::ConsoleUI.comment:
Subclass of StreamUI that instantiates the user interaction using $stdin,
$stdout, and $stderr.

Gem::ConsoleUI::new.name: new
Gem::ConsoleUI::new.comment:
The Console UI has no arguments as it defaults to reading input from stdin,
output to stdout and warnings or errors to stderr.

Gem::ContentAddress.name: Gem::ContentAddress
Gem::ContentAddress.comment:
Gem::ContentAddress is the single home for content-addressing semantics: what
an address and a Ruby ABI look like, which specs are eligible, how addresses
are generated and verified against gem files.

Gem::ContentAddress::address_for.name: address_for
Gem::ContentAddress::address_for.comment:
Generates the content address for <tt>bytes</tt>: the first <tt>length</tt>
characters of the hexadecimal SHA256 digest of the contents.

Gem::ContentAddress::content_addressed?.name: content_addressed?
Gem::ContentAddress::content_addressed?.comment:
Whether <tt>spec</tt> is content-addressed: it is eligible for content
addressing and has a valid content address set. See eligible? for when to pass
<tt>validate_ruby_abi: false</tt>.

Gem::ContentAddress::content_addressed_r.name: content_addressed_row?
Gem::ContentAddress::content_addressed_r.comment:
Whether an index row describes a content-addressed gem: an address-shaped
<tt>suffix</tt>, a pinned <tt>platform</tt>, and a
<tt>required_ruby_version</tt> pinning a single Ruby ABI. Rows missing any of
these must not assign a content address, so specs cannot be constructed half
content-addressed. See eligible? for when to pass <tt>validate_ruby_abi:
false</tt>.

Gem::ContentAddress::eligible!.name: eligible!
Gem::ContentAddress::eligible!.comment: Raises ArgumentError unless <tt>spec</tt> is eligible for content addressing

Gem::ContentAddress::eligible?.name: eligible?
Gem::ContentAddress::eligible?.comment:
Whether <tt>spec</tt> is eligible for content addressing. A gem must pin its
required_ruby_version to a single Ruby ABI ("~> X.Y.0") and declare a non-RUBY
platform to be content addressed. This makes `content_addressed? implies
ruby_abi present` structural: no spec can count as content addressed without
an ABI to scope it by.

Gem::ContentAddress::file_name_claim.name: file_name_claim
Gem::ContentAddress::file_name_claim.comment:
The content address claimed by a gem file name, or nil when the name makes no
claim. <tt>filename</tt> is the file's base name without the ".gem" extension
("name-version[-suffix]"). A name claims an address when its suffix is
address-shaped and is not just <tt>spec</tt>'s own platform: a platform string
that happens to look like hexadecimal (both normalized and original spellings)
is a platform name, not a claim.

Gem::ContentAddress::match?.name: match?
Gem::ContentAddress::match?.comment:
Whether <tt>value</tt> is a valid content address (a string of 8-64 lowercase
hexadecimal characters). This only checks the shape of a string: use
content_addressed? to ask whether a spec is actually content addressed, and
file_name_claim to ask whether a file name claims an address.

Gem::ContentAddress::platform_eligible?.name: platform_eligible?
Gem::ContentAddress::platform_eligible?.comment:
Whether <tt>platform</tt> is eligible for content addressing: present and not
the generic RUBY platform.

Gem::ContentAddress::ruby_abi_for.name: ruby_abi_for
Gem::ContentAddress::ruby_abi_for.comment:
Derives the Ruby ABI ("X.Y") from <tt>required_ruby_version</tt>. Only a
single pessimistic requirement with three segments ending in zero ("~> X.Y.0")
pins an ABI. Returns nil for any other shape.

Gem::ContentAddress::ruby_abi_requiremen.name: ruby_abi_requirement
Gem::ContentAddress::ruby_abi_requiremen.comment:
The required_ruby_version that pins <tt>ruby_abi</tt> ("X.Y" to "~> X.Y.0").
Inverse of <tt>ruby_abi_for</tt>.

Gem::ContentAddress::ruby_abi_specificit.name: ruby_abi_specificity_match
Gem::ContentAddress::ruby_abi_specificit.comment:
Ranks <tt>spec</tt> for candidate selection against <tt>ruby_version</tt>: a
content-addressed spec built for that Ruby ranks first (0), any
non-content-addressed spec next (1), and a content-addressed spec built for
another Ruby last (2), since its binary cannot load there.

Gem::ContentAddress::valid_ruby_abi?.name: valid_ruby_abi?
Gem::ContentAddress::valid_ruby_abi?.comment: Whether <tt>value</tt> is a well-formed Ruby ABI ("X.Y").

Gem::ContentAddress::verified_file_name_.name: verified_file_name_claim
Gem::ContentAddress::verified_file_name_.comment:
Verifies the content address claimed by the gem file at <tt>path</tt> against
the SHA256 digest of its contents. Returns the verified address, or nil when
the file name makes no claim. Raises Gem::InstallError when the contents do
not match the claim, regardless of whether the packaged <tt>spec</tt> is
eligible, so swapped contents cannot hide behind an ineligible specification.

Gem::Cooldown.name: Gem::Cooldown
Gem::Cooldown.comment:
Applies a cooldown period to remote gem versions as a supply chain attack
mitigation.  When a cooldown of N days is configured, gem versions published
within the last N days are not considered for installation or update.
Versions whose publish time is unknown are never excluded, so sources that do
not provide publish times keep working.

The cooldown period comes from the <tt>--cooldown DAYS</tt> option when given,
and 0 there disables the cooldown.  Without the option the <tt>:cooldown:</tt>
setting in the gemrc file and Bundler's own cooldown setting both apply and
the longer of the two wins, so a 0 in either of them disables nothing while
the other names a period.

Gem::Cooldown::from_options.name: from_options
Gem::Cooldown::from_options.comment:
Creates a Cooldown from the command line <tt>options</tt>.  The --cooldown
option wins outright, so <tt>--cooldown 0</tt> bypasses the cooldown however
the two tools are configured.  Without it the :cooldown: gemrc setting and
Bundler's cooldown setting are both read and the longer of the two applies, so
a cooldown configured for only one of them still covers gem commands.

Gem::Cooldown::output_skipped_summary.name: output_skipped_summary
Gem::Cooldown::output_skipped_summary.comment:
Reports, per gem, the newest version the cooldown kept out of a completed
installation or update.  <tt>entries</tt> are hashes with :name, :version,
:resolved and :available_in_days keys; when several entries name the same gem
only the newest version is shown.

Gem::Cooldown::parse_created_at.name: parse_created_at
Gem::Cooldown::parse_created_at.comment:
Parses a <tt>created_at</tt> timestamp from the compact index.  A timestamp
without a time zone offset is read as UTC, because reading it as local time
would shift the cooldown window by the environment's offset. Returns nil for
anything unparsable, including a year outside four digits, so the cooldown
fails open.

Gem::Cooldown::warn_missing_created_at.name: warn_missing_created_at
Gem::Cooldown::warn_missing_created_at.comment:
Warns once per process that <tt>source</tt> did not provide publish times, so
the cooldown cannot be applied to gems from it.

Gem::Cooldown#active?.name: active?
Gem::Cooldown#active?.comment: True when a cooldown period is configured.

Gem::Cooldown#remaining_days.name: remaining_days
Gem::Cooldown#remaining_days.comment:
Number of days until a gem version published at <tt>created_at</tt> leaves the
cooldown period, rounded up and at least 1.

Gem::Cooldown#skip?.name: skip?
Gem::Cooldown#skip?.comment:
True when a gem version published at <tt>created_at</tt> must not be
considered.  Versions with an unknown publish time (<tt>nil</tt>) are kept.

Gem::CooldownOption.name: Gem::CooldownOption
Gem::CooldownOption.comment: Mixin methods for the cooldown option for Gem::Commands.

Gem::CooldownOption#add_cooldown_option.name: add_cooldown_option
Gem::CooldownOption#add_cooldown_option.comment: Add the --cooldown option to the option parser.

Gem::CooldownSettings.name: Gem::CooldownSettings
Gem::CooldownSettings.comment:
The rules RubyGems and Bundler share for reading a configured cooldown period.
 Bundler ships a copy of this file, so it deliberately has no requires: none
of the rest of RubyGems is guaranteed to be around it.

Gem::CooldownSettings::combine.name: combine
Gem::CooldownSettings::combine.comment:
The cooldown that applies when RubyGems and Bundler are configured separately:
the longest of <tt>values</tt>, so a cooldown configured for only one of the
two tools protects both.  Returns nil when none of them is usable.

A configured 0 takes part like any other value rather than switching the
cooldown off, which leaves <tt>--cooldown 0</tt> as the way to bypass a
cooldown that the other tool configures.

Gem::CooldownSettings::days.name: days
Gem::CooldownSettings::days.comment:
<tt>value</tt> read as a number of days, or nil when it is absent or cannot be
read as a non-negative integer.  A gemrc entry and a Bundler config entry are
both arbitrary YAML, so either can be any type at all.

Gem::CooldownSettings::invalid?.name: invalid?
Gem::CooldownSettings::invalid?.comment: True when <tt>value</tt> is configured but cannot be read as a number of days.

Gem::CredentialStore.name: Gem::CredentialStore
Gem::CredentialStore.comment:
Gem::CredentialStore is opt-in storage for authentication secrets (API keys,
host credentials) in the operating system's native secret store instead of a
plain text file:

* macOS: Keychain, via the <tt>security</tt> command line tool.
* Linux: the Secret Service API (GNOME Keyring, KWallet, ...), via
  <tt>secret-tool</tt>.
* Windows: Credential Manager, via the
  <tt>Windows.Security.Credentials.PasswordVault</tt> API from PowerShell.

A third party can add another backend (1Password, pass, HashiCorp Vault, ...)
by shipping a gem that provides
<tt>rubygems/credential_store/backends/<name></tt> and calls .register_backend
from it. Users then select it by name instead of <tt>true</tt> (see
.resolve_backend).

Every public method traps all errors and returns <tt>nil</tt>/<tt>false</tt>
instead of raising, so that callers can transparently fall back to their
existing file-based storage when the native store is unavailable or fails (a
locked keychain over SSH, a headless Linux session without a keyring daemon,
...).

Gem::CredentialStore::backend=.name: backend=
Gem::CredentialStore::backend=.comment:
Installs a shared backend that .for wraps for every spec and service. Intended
for tests that need RubyGems and Bundler credentials to land in one backend
under their own service names.

Gem::CredentialStore::for.name: for
Gem::CredentialStore::for.comment:
Returns the store to use for <tt>spec</tt>, or <tt>nil</tt> when the
credential store is off. <tt>spec</tt> is either <tt>true</tt> (use this
platform's native backend) or the name of a registered backend such as
"1password". <tt>service</tt> names the account namespace within the backend,
so RubyGems and Bundler keep separate credentials in one native store. The
store is memoized per <tt>spec</tt> and <tt>service</tt> for the life of the
process, so the read cache and any expensive backend startup are shared across
callers. A test may install a stand-in via #instance= that is returned here
for any enabled <tt>spec</tt>, or inject a shared backend via #backend=.

Gem::CredentialStore::instance.name: instance
Gem::CredentialStore::instance.comment:
The default-backed store for this platform, i.e. <tt>for(true)</tt>. Kept for
callers and tests that only care about the native backend.

Gem::CredentialStore::instance=.name: instance=
Gem::CredentialStore::instance=.comment:
Installs a stand-in store that .for returns for any enabled setting. Intended
for tests that inject a fake backend.

Gem::CredentialStore::new.name: new
Gem::CredentialStore::new.comment:
<tt>backend</tt> is only used by tests to inject a fake backend regardless of
the platform the test suite happens to run on. <tt>service</tt> is the account
namespace this store reads and writes under.

Gem::CredentialStore::register_backend.name: register_backend
Gem::CredentialStore::register_backend.comment:
Registers <tt>backend</tt> under <tt>name</tt> so it can be selected with
<tt>credential_store = <name></tt>. A third-party backend gem calls this from
the file RubyGems loads for that name (see .resolve_backend).

Gem::CredentialStore::reset!.name: reset!
Gem::CredentialStore::reset!.comment:
Clears the memoized stores, the injected overrides, and the warned messages.
Intended for tests only.

Gem::CredentialStore::resolve_backend.name: resolve_backend
Gem::CredentialStore::resolve_backend.comment:
Resolves a registered backend by <tt>name</tt>, requiring
<tt>rubygems/credential_store/backends/<name></tt> on first use so a backend
shipped as its own gem loads only when actually selected. Returns <tt>nil</tt>
(warning once) when the name is malformed or no gem provides it, which makes
callers fall back to file storage. The fixed require prefix and the restricted
name charset keep the setting a piece of data, never a path or a command.

Gem::CredentialStore::warn_handler=.name: warn_handler=
Gem::CredentialStore::warn_handler=.comment:
Sends warnings to <tt>handler</tt> (anything responding to #call) instead of
Gem.ui. Bundler sets this because it replaces Gem.ui with a subclass of
Gem::SilentUI, which discards alert_warning entirely, so a credential store
failure would otherwise be silent for the whole bundle command.

Gem::CredentialStore::warn_once.name: warn_once
Gem::CredentialStore::warn_once.comment:
Warns once per distinct message. A single flag for every message would let an
early warning about, say, a misspelled backend name suppress the later warning
that a secret was written in plain text.

Gem::CredentialStore#available?.name: available?
Gem::CredentialStore#available?.comment: True if a native credential backend is usable on this platform.

Gem::CredentialStore#delete.name: delete
Gem::CredentialStore#delete.comment:
Removes the secret stored for <tt>account</tt>. Returns <tt>true</tt> if the
entry is gone, whether or not it existed beforehand.

Gem::CredentialStore#delete_all.name: delete_all
Gem::CredentialStore#delete_all.comment:
Removes every entry this store owns (all accounts under its service). Returns
<tt>true</tt> when the store is now clear. Used by +gem signout+ to end every
session at once, mirroring deletion of the whole credentials file.

Gem::CredentialStore#get.name: get
Gem::CredentialStore#get.comment:
Returns the secret stored for <tt>account</tt>, or <tt>nil</tt> if there is
none or the backend is unavailable/fails.

Gem::CredentialStore#list.name: list
Gem::CredentialStore#list.comment:
The accounts this store holds, or <tt>nil</tt> when the backend cannot
enumerate them. Listing is optional in the backend protocol: the native
backends implement it, but a third-party backend that only resolves
credentials on demand has nothing to enumerate. Callers must treat
<tt>nil</tt> as "unknown", not as "empty". Secrets are never returned.

Gem::CredentialStore#read_failed?.name: read_failed?
Gem::CredentialStore#read_failed?.comment:
True when #get returned <tt>nil</tt> for <tt>account</tt> because the backend
could not answer, rather than because nothing is stored under it. Callers that
would otherwise fall back to a different credential need the difference: a
missing entry means "use something else", an unreadable one does not.

Gem::CredentialStore#invalidate_list.name: invalidate_list
Gem::CredentialStore#invalidate_list.comment: The listing is memoized, so a write has to drop it.

Gem::CredentialStore#validate_credential.name: validate_credential
Gem::CredentialStore#validate_credential.comment:
A newline in an account would start a second command in the macOS batch input.
#set turns the raise back into a warning and a false.

Gem::CredentialStore::LinuxBackend.name: Gem::CredentialStore::LinuxBackend
Gem::CredentialStore::LinuxBackend.comment:
Stores credentials in the Secret Service API (GNOME Keyring, KWallet, ...) via
the <tt>secret-tool</tt> command line tool from libsecret.

Gem::CredentialStore::LinuxBackend::list.name: list
Gem::CredentialStore::LinuxBackend::list.comment:
secret-tool writes attributes to stderr and secrets to stdout, so accounts are
read from stderr. Discarding stdout also keeps a secret containing a newline
from being mistaken for an attribute line.

Gem::CredentialStore::LinuxBackend::rese.name: reset!
Gem::CredentialStore::LinuxBackend::rese.comment: Clears the memoized #available? result. Intended for tests only.

Gem::CredentialStore::LinuxBackend::clea.name: cleared?
Gem::CredentialStore::LinuxBackend::clea.comment:
libsecret clears only unlocked items and reports no error for the ones it
skipped, so a locked keyring answers a clear with success while keeping every
secret. search exits zero either way, so its output is the answer.

Gem::CredentialStore::MacOSBackend.name: Gem::CredentialStore::MacOSBackend
Gem::CredentialStore::MacOSBackend.comment:
Stores credentials in the macOS Keychain via the <tt>security</tt> command
line tool. <tt>security</tt> has no way to read a password from stdin as raw
bytes for <tt>add-generic-password</tt>, so #set uses +security -i+
(batch/interactive mode, one tokenized command per stdin line) to keep the
secret off argv and out of <tt>ps</tt> output.

A newline would start a second command in the +security -i+ batch, and
+security find-generic-password -w+ prints any non-printable byte back as a
hex string rather than the original value, so a non-ASCII secret would
round-trip corrupted. Those are the limits Gem::CredentialStore#set enforces
for every backend, so the caller falls back to file storage rather than
storing something that cannot be read back.

Gem::CredentialStore::MacOSBackend::dele.name: delete_all
Gem::CredentialStore::MacOSBackend::dele.comment:
security deletes one entry per call, so keep going until it reports there is
nothing left (exit 44). Other services are untouched.

Gem::CredentialStore::MacOSBackend::list.name: list
Gem::CredentialStore::MacOSBackend::list.comment:
security has no "list by service" subcommand, so this reads the dump, which
never reports the secrets.

Gem::CredentialStore::WindowsBackend.name: Gem::CredentialStore::WindowsBackend
Gem::CredentialStore::WindowsBackend.comment:
Stores credentials in the Windows Credential Manager via the
<tt>Windows.Security.Credentials.PasswordVault</tt> WinRT API, driven from
PowerShell. Account/service/secret values are passed as environment variables
rather than interpolated into the script text, so no quoting scheme is needed
and values cannot break out of the script.

Windows PowerShell is used rather than PowerShell 7 (<tt>pwsh</tt>) because
the WinRT projection used here is not reliably available under pwsh. It is
spawned as <tt>powershell</tt> rather than <tt>powershell.exe</tt>, the way
this codebase spawns <tt>git</tt>, so PATHEXT resolves it. That also lets the
tests put a shim ahead of it on Windows, where a file with a shebang is not
executable.

Gem::CredentialStore::WindowsBackend::li.name: list
Gem::CredentialStore::WindowsBackend::li.comment:
FindAllByResource raises when the resource has no entries, which is an empty
list rather than an error.

Gem::DefaultUserInteraction.name: Gem::DefaultUserInteraction
Gem::DefaultUserInteraction.comment:
Module that defines the default UserInteraction.  Any class including this
module will have access to the <tt>ui</tt> method that returns the default UI.

Gem::DefaultUserInteraction::ui=.name: ui=
Gem::DefaultUserInteraction::ui=.comment:
Set the default UI.  If the default UI is never explicitly set, a simple
console based UserInteraction will be used automatically.

Gem::Dependency.name: Gem::Dependency
Gem::Dependency.comment: The Dependency class holds a Gem name and a Gem::Requirement.

Gem::Dependency::new.name: new
Gem::Dependency::new.comment:
Constructs a dependency with <tt>name</tt> and <tt>requirements</tt>. The last
argument can optionally be the dependency type, which defaults to
<tt>:runtime</tt>.

Gem::Dependency#=~.comment:
Uses this dependency as a pattern to compare to <tt>other</tt>. This
dependency will match if the name matches the other's name, and other has only
an equal version requirement that satisfies this dependency.

Gem::Dependency#latest_version?.name: latest_version?
Gem::Dependency#latest_version?.comment: Is this dependency simply asking for the latest version of a gem?

Gem::Dependency#match?.name: match?
Gem::Dependency#match?.call_seq:
dep.match? name          => true or false
dep.match? name, version => true or false
dep.match? spec          => true or false
Gem::Dependency#match?.comment:
Does this dependency match the specification described by <tt>name</tt> and
<tt>version</tt> or match <tt>spec</tt>?

NOTE:  Unlike #matches_spec? this method does not return true when the version
is a prerelease version unless this is a prerelease dependency.

Gem::Dependency#matches_spec?.name: matches_spec?
Gem::Dependency#matches_spec?.comment:
Does this dependency match <tt>spec</tt>?

NOTE:  This is not a convenience method.  Unlike #match? this method returns
true when <tt>spec</tt> is a prerelease version even if this dependency is not
a prerelease dependency.

Gem::Dependency#merge.name: merge
Gem::Dependency#merge.comment: Merges the requirements of <tt>other</tt> into this dependency

Gem::Dependency#prerelease?.name: prerelease?
Gem::Dependency#prerelease?.comment: Does this dependency require a prerelease?

Gem::Dependency#specific?.name: specific?
Gem::Dependency#specific?.comment: True if the dependency will not always match the latest version.

Gem::DependencyInstaller.name: Gem::DependencyInstaller
Gem::DependencyInstaller.comment: Installs a gem along with all its dependencies from local and remote gems.

Gem::DependencyInstaller::new.name: new
Gem::DependencyInstaller::new.comment:
Creates a new installer instance.

Options are:
:cache_dir:
  Alternate repository path to store .gem files in.

:domain:
  :local, :remote, or :both.  :local only searches gems in the current
  directory.  :remote searches only gems in Gem::sources. :both searches both.

:env_shebang:
  See Gem::Installer::new.

:force:
  See Gem::Installer#install.

:format_executable:
  See Gem::Installer#initialize.

:ignore_dependencies:
  Don't install any dependencies.

:install_dir:
  See Gem::Installer#install.

:prerelease:
  Allow prerelease versions.  See #install.

:security_policy:
  See Gem::Installer::new and Gem::Security.

:user_install:
  See Gem::Installer.new

:wrappers:
  See Gem::Installer::new

:build_args:
  See Gem::Installer::new

Gem::DependencyInstaller#consider_local?.name: consider_local?
Gem::DependencyInstaller#consider_local?.comment: Indicated, based on the requested domain, if local gems should be considered.

Gem::DependencyInstaller#consider_remote.name: consider_remote?
Gem::DependencyInstaller#consider_remote.comment: Indicated, based on the requested domain, if remote gems should be considered.

Gem::DependencyInstaller#install.name: install
Gem::DependencyInstaller#install.comment:
Installs the gem <tt>dep_or_name</tt> and all its dependencies.  Returns an
Array of installed gem specifications.

If the <tt>:prerelease</tt> option is set and there is a prerelease for
<tt>dep_or_name</tt> the prerelease version will be installed.

Unless explicitly specified as a prerelease dependency, prerelease gems that
<tt>dep_or_name</tt> depend on will not be installed.

If c-1.a depends on b-1 and a-1.a and there is a gem b-1.a available then
c-1.a, b-1 and a-1.a will be installed.  b-1.a will need to be installed
separately.

Gem::DependencyList.name: Gem::DependencyList
Gem::DependencyList.comment:
Gem::DependencyList is used for installing and uninstalling gems in the
correct order to avoid conflicts.

Gem::DependencyList::from_specs.name: from_specs
Gem::DependencyList::from_specs.comment: Creates a DependencyList from the current specs.

Gem::DependencyList::new.name: new
Gem::DependencyList::new.comment:
Creates a new DependencyList.  If <tt>development</tt> is true, development
dependencies will be included.

Gem::DependencyList#dependency_order.name: dependency_order
Gem::DependencyList#dependency_order.comment:
Return a list of the gem specifications in the dependency list, sorted in
order so that no gemspec in the list depends on a gemspec earlier in the list.

This is useful when removing gems from a set of installed gems.  By removing
them in the returned order, you don't get into as many dependency issues.

If there are circular dependencies (yuck!), then gems will be returned in
order until only the circular dependents and anything they reference are left.
 Then arbitrary gemspecs will be returned until the circular dependency is
broken, after which gems will be returned in dependency order again.

Gem::DependencyList#ok?.name: ok?
Gem::DependencyList#ok?.comment: Are all the dependencies in the list satisfied?

Gem::DependencyList#ok_to_remove?.name: ok_to_remove?
Gem::DependencyList#ok_to_remove?.comment:
It is ok to remove a gemspec from the dependency list?

If removing the gemspec creates breaks a currently ok dependency, then it is
NOT ok to remove the gemspec.

Gem::DependencyList#remove_by_name.name: remove_by_name
Gem::DependencyList#remove_by_name.comment: Removes the gemspec matching <tt>full_name</tt> from the dependency list

Gem::DependencyList#remove_specs_unsatis.name: remove_specs_unsatisfied_by
Gem::DependencyList#remove_specs_unsatis.comment:
Remove everything in the DependencyList that matches but doesn't satisfy items
in <tt>dependencies</tt> (a hash of gem names to arrays of dependencies).

Gem::DependencyList#spec_predecessors.name: spec_predecessors
Gem::DependencyList#spec_predecessors.comment:
Return a hash of predecessors.  <tt>result[spec]</tt> is an Array of gemspecs
that have a dependency satisfied by the named gemspec.

Gem::DependencyList#active_count.name: active_count
Gem::DependencyList#active_count.comment:
Count the number of gemspecs in the list <tt>specs</tt> that are not in
<tt>ignored</tt>.

Gem::DependencyResolutionError.name: Gem::DependencyResolutionError
Gem::DependencyResolutionError.comment: Raised by Gem::Resolver when dependency resolution fails.

Gem::Deprecate.name: Gem::Deprecate
Gem::Deprecate.comment:
Provides 3 methods for declaring when something is going away.

<tt>deprecate(name, repl, year, month)</tt>:
  Indicate something may be removed on/after a certain date.

<tt>rubygems_deprecate(name, replacement=:none)</tt>:
  Indicate something will be removed in the next major RubyGems version,
  and (optionally) a replacement for it.

<tt>rubygems_deprecate_command</tt>:
  Indicate a RubyGems command (in +lib/rubygems/commands/*.rb+) will be
  removed in the next RubyGems version.

Also provides <tt>skip_during</tt> for temporarily turning off deprecation
warnings. This is intended to be used in the test suite, so deprecation
warnings don't cause test failures if you need to make sure stderr is
otherwise empty.

Example usage of <tt>deprecate</tt> and <tt>rubygems_deprecate</tt>:

  class Legacy
    def self.some_class_method
      # ...
    end

    def some_instance_method
      # ...
    end

    def some_old_method
      # ...
    end

    extend Gem::Deprecate
    deprecate :some_instance_method, "X.z", 2011, 4
    rubygems_deprecate :some_old_method, "Modern#some_new_method"

    class << self
      extend Gem::Deprecate
      deprecate :some_class_method, :none, 2011, 4
    end
  end

Example usage of <tt>rubygems_deprecate_command</tt>:

  class Gem::Commands::QueryCommand < Gem::Command
    extend Gem::Deprecate
    rubygems_deprecate_command

    # ...
  end

Example usage of <tt>skip_during</tt>:

  class TestSomething < Gem::Testcase
    def test_some_thing_with_deprecations
      Gem::Deprecate.skip_during do
        actual_stdout, actual_stderr = capture_output do
          Gem.something_deprecated
        end
        assert_empty actual_stdout
        assert_equal(expected, actual_stderr)
      end
    end
  end

Gem::Deprecate::rubygems_deprecate.name: rubygems_deprecate
Gem::Deprecate::rubygems_deprecate.comment:
Simple deprecation method that deprecates <tt>name</tt> by wrapping it up in a
dummy method. It warns on each call to the dummy method telling the user of
<tt>repl</tt> (unless <tt>repl</tt> is :none) and the Rubygems version that it
is planned to go away.

Gem::Deprecate::rubygems_deprecate_comma.name: rubygems_deprecate_command
Gem::Deprecate::rubygems_deprecate_comma.comment: Deprecation method to deprecate Rubygems commands

Gem::Deprecate::skip_during.name: skip_during
Gem::Deprecate::skip_during.comment: Temporarily turn off warnings. Intended for tests only.

Gem::Deprecate#deprecate.name: deprecate
Gem::Deprecate#deprecate.comment:
Simple deprecation method that deprecates <tt>name</tt> by wrapping it up in a
dummy method. It warns on each call to the dummy method telling the user of
<tt>repl</tt> (unless <tt>repl</tt> is :none) and the year/month that it is

Gem::Ext::CmakeBuilder.name: Gem::Ext::CmakeBuilder

This builder creates extensions defined using CMake. Its is invoked if a Gem's
spec file sets the `extension` property to a string that contains
`CMakeLists.txt`.

In general, CMake projects are built in two steps:

  * configure
  * build

The builder follow this convention. First it runs a configuration step and
then it runs a build step.

CMake projects can be quite configurable - it is likely you will want to
specify options when installing a gem. To pass options to CMake specify them
after `--` in the gem install command. For example:

  gem install <gem_name> -- --preset <preset_name>

Note that options are ONLY sent to the configure step - it is not currently
possible to specify options for the build step. If this becomes and issue then
the CMake builder can be updated to support build options.

Useful options to know are:

  -G to specify a generator (-G Ninja is recommended)
  -D<CMAKE_VARIABLE> to set a CMake variable (for example -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release)
  --preset <preset_name> to use a preset

If the Gem author provides presets, via CMakePresets.json file, you will
likely want to use one of them. If not, you may wish to specify a generator.
Ninja is recommended because it can build projects in parallel and thus much
faster than building them serially like Make does.

Gem::GemcutterUtilities.name: Gem::GemcutterUtilities
Gem::GemcutterUtilities.comment:
Utility methods for using the RubyGems API.
The WebauthnListener class retrieves an OTP after a user successfully
WebAuthns with the Gem host. An instance opens a socket using the TCPServer
instance given and listens for a request from the Gem host. The request should
be a GET request to the root path and contains the OTP code in the form of a
query parameter `code`. The listener will return the code which will be used
as the OTP for API requests.

Types of responses sent by the listener after receiving a request:
  - 200 OK: OTP code was successfully retrieved
  - 204 No Content: If the request was an OPTIONS request
  - 400 Bad Request: If the request did not contain a query parameter `code`
  - 404 Not Found: The request was not to the root path
  - 405 Method Not Allowed: OTP code was not retrieved because the request was not a GET/OPTIONS request

Example usage:

  thread = Gem::WebauthnListener.listener_thread("https://rubygems.example", server)
  thread.join
  otp = thread[:otp]
  error = thread[:error]
The WebauthnListener Response class is used by the WebauthnListener to create
responses to be sent to the Gem host. It creates a Gem::Net::HTTPResponse
instance when initialized and can be converted to the appropriate format to be
sent by a socket using `to_s`. Gem::Net::HTTPResponse instances cannot be
directly sent over a socket.

Types of response classes:
  - OkResponse
  - NoContentResponse
  - BadRequestResponse
  - NotFoundResponse
  - MethodNotAllowedResponse

Example usage:

  server = TCPServer.new(0)
  socket = server.accept

  response = OkResponse.for("https://rubygems.example")
  socket.print response.to_s
  socket.close
The WebauthnPoller class retrieves an OTP after a user successfully WebAuthns.
An instance polls the Gem host for the OTP code. The polling request
(api/v1/webauthn_verification/<webauthn_token>/status.json) is sent to the Gem
host every 5 seconds and will timeout after 5 minutes. If the status field in
the json response is "success", the code field will contain the OTP code.

Example usage:

  thread = Gem::WebauthnPoller.poll_thread(
    {},
    "RubyGems.org",
    "https://rubygems.org/api/v1/webauthn_verification/odow34b93t6aPCdY",
    { email: "email@example.com", password: "password" }
  )
  thread.join
  otp = thread[:otp]
  error = thread[:error]

Gem::GemcutterUtilities#stored_api_key_n.name: stored_api_key_named
Gem::GemcutterUtilities#stored_api_key_n.comment:
The default key, when <tt>name</tt> is the name the credentials file knows it
by. That file renames :rubygems_api_key to :rubygems on the way in, so the
name survives only there, and moving the key into the store would otherwise
put it out of reach of --key.

Only that one name. The store is keyed by host, and --key names a key, so
looking any other name up there would let --key reach a host's key and send it
somewhere else. The credentials file keeps the two apart by type, since --key
arrives as a Symbol and host entries are strings.

Gem::GemcutterUtilities#verify_api_key.name: verify_api_key

If the response was not successful, shows an error to the user including the
<tt>error_prefix</tt> and the response body. If the response was a permanent
redirect, shows an error to the user including the redirect location.

Gem::Installer.name: Gem::Installer
Gem::Installer.comment:
The installer installs the files contained in the .gem into the Gem.home.

Gem::Installer does the work of putting files in all the right places on the
filesystem including unpacking the gem into its gem dir, installing the
gemspec in the specifications dir, storing the cached gem in the cache dir,
and installing either wrappers or symlinks for executables.

The installer invokes pre and post install hooks.  Hooks can be added either
through a rubygems_plugin.rb file in an installed gem or via a
rubygems/defaults/#{RUBY_ENGINE}.rb or rubygems/defaults/operating_system.rb
file.  See Gem.pre_install and Gem.post_install for details.

Gem::Installer::at.name: at
Gem::Installer::at.comment: Construct an installer object for the gem file located at <tt>path</tt>

Gem::Installer::exec_format.name: exec_format
Gem::Installer::exec_format.comment:
Overrides the executable format.

This is a sprintf format with a "%s" which will be replaced with the
executable name.  It is based off the ruby executable name's difference from
"ruby".

Gem::Installer::for_spec.name: for_spec
Gem::Installer::for_spec.comment:
Construct an installer object for an ephemeral gem (one where we don't
actually have a .gem file, just a spec)

Gem::Installer::new.name: new
Gem::Installer::new.comment:
Constructs an Installer instance that will install the gem at <tt>package</tt>
which can either be a path or an instance of Gem::Package.  <tt>options</tt>
is a Hash with the following keys:

:bin_dir:
  Where to put a bin wrapper if needed.

:development:
  Whether or not development dependencies should be installed.

:env_shebang:
  Use /usr/bin/env in bin wrappers.

:force:
  Overrides all version checks and security policy checks, except for a
  signed-gems-only policy.

:format_executable:
  Format the executable the same as the Ruby executable. If your Ruby is
  ruby18, foo_exec will be installed as foo_exec18.

:ignore_dependencies:
  Don't raise if a dependency is missing.

:install_dir:
  The directory to install the gem into.

:security_policy:
  Use the specified security policy.  See Gem::Security

:user_install:
  Indicate that the gem should be unpacked into the users personal gem
  directory.

:only_install_dir:
  Only validate dependencies against what is in the install_dir

:wrappers:
  Install wrappers if true, symlinks if false.

:build_args:
  An Array of arguments to pass to the extension builder process. If not set,
  then Gem::Command.build_args is used

:post_install_message:
  Print gem post install message if true

Gem::Installer#gem_dir.name: gem_dir
Gem::Installer#gem_dir.comment: Lazy accessor for the spec's gem directory.

Gem::Installer#generate_bin_symlink.name: generate_bin_symlink

Gem::Installer#install.name: install
Gem::Installer#install.comment:
Installs the gem and returns a loaded Gem::Specification for the installed
gem.

The gem will be installed with the following structure:

  @gem_home/
    cache/<gem-version>.gem #=> a cached copy of the installed gem
    gems/<gem-version>/... #=> extracted files
    specifications/<gem-version>.gemspec #=> the Gem::Specification

Gem::Installer#pre_install_checks.name: pre_install_checks

repository is writable and its directories exist, required Ruby and rubygems
versions are met and that dependencies are installed.

Version and dependency checks are skipped if this install is forced.

The dependent check will be skipped if the install is ignoring dependencies.

The template supports 4 expansions:

  $env    the path to the unix env utility
  $ruby   the path to the currently running ruby interpreter
  $exec   the path to the gem's executable
  $name   the name of the gem the executable is for
