Each of the returned values <tt>cur_limit</tt> and <tt>max_limit</tt> is an
integer; see Process.setrlimit.

Example:

  Process.getrlimit(:CORE) # => [0, 18446744073709551615]

See Process.setrlimit.

Not available on all platforms.

Process::getsid.name: getsid
Process::getsid.comment:
Returns the session ID of the given process ID <tt>pid</tt>, or of the current
process if not given:

  Process.getsid                # => 27422
  Process.getsid(0)             # => 27422
  Process.getsid(Process.pid()) # => 27422

Not available on all platforms.

Process::gid.name: gid
Process::gid.call_seq:
Process.gid         -> integer
Process::GID.rid    -> integer
Process::Sys.getgid -> integer
Process::gid.comment:
Returns the (real) group ID for the current process:

  Process.gid # => 1000

Process::gid=.name: gid=
Process::gid=.comment:
Sets the group ID for the current process to <tt>new_gid</tt>:

  Process.gid = 1000 # => 1000

Process::groups.name: groups
Process::groups.comment:
Returns an array of the group IDs in the supplemental group access list for
the current process:

  Process.groups # => [4, 24, 27, 30, 46, 122, 135, 136, 1000]

These properties of the returned array are system-dependent:

* Whether (and how) the array is sorted.
* Whether the array includes effective group IDs.
* Whether the array includes duplicate group IDs.
* Whether the array size exceeds the value of Process.maxgroups.

Use this call to get a sorted and unique array:

  Process.groups.uniq.sort

Process::groups=.name: groups=
Process::groups=.comment:
Sets the supplemental group access list to the given array of group IDs.

  Process.groups                     # => [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 10, 11, 20, 26, 27]
  Process.groups = [27, 6, 10, 11]   # => [27, 6, 10, 11]
  Process.groups                     # => [27, 6, 10, 11]

Process::initgroups.name: initgroups
Process::initgroups.comment:
Sets the supplemental group access list; the new list includes:

* The group IDs of those groups to which the user given by <tt>username</tt>
  belongs.
* The group ID <tt>gid</tt>.

Example:

  Process.groups                # => [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 10, 11, 20, 26, 27]
  Process.initgroups('me', 30)  # => [30, 6, 10, 11]
  Process.groups                # => [30, 6, 10, 11]

Not available on all platforms.

Process::kill.name: kill
Process::kill.comment:
Sends a signal to each process specified by <tt>ids</tt> (which must specify
at least one ID); returns the count of signals sent.

For each given <tt>id</tt>, if <tt>id</tt> is:

* Positive, sends the signal to the process whose process ID is <tt>id</tt>.
* Zero, send the signal to all processes in the current process group.
* Negative, sends the signal to a system-dependent collection of processes.

Argument <tt>signal</tt> specifies the signal to be sent; the argument may be:

* An integer signal number: e.g., <tt>-29</tt>, <tt>0</tt>, <tt>29</tt>.
* A signal name (string), with or without leading <tt>'SIG'</tt>, and with or
  without a further prefixed minus sign (<tt>'-'</tt>): e.g.:

  * <tt>'SIGPOLL'</tt>.
  * <tt>'POLL'</tt>,
  * <tt>'-SIGPOLL'</tt>.
  * <tt>'-POLL'</tt>.

* A signal symbol, with or without leading <tt>'SIG'</tt>, and with or without
  a further prefixed minus sign (<tt>'-'</tt>): e.g.:

  * <tt>:SIGPOLL</tt>.
  * <tt>:POLL</tt>.
  * <tt>:'-SIGPOLL'</tt>.
  * <tt>:'-POLL'</tt>.

If <tt>signal</tt> is:

* A non-negative integer, or a signal name or symbol without prefixed
  <tt>'-'</tt>, each process with process ID <tt>id</tt> is signalled.
* A negative integer, or a signal name or symbol with prefixed <tt>'-'</tt>,
  each process group with group ID <tt>id</tt> is signalled.

Use method Signal.list to see which signals are supported by Ruby on the
underlying platform; the method returns a hash of the string names and
non-negative integer values of the supported signals. The size and content of
the returned hash varies widely among platforms.

Additionally, signal <tt>0</tt> is useful to determine if the process exists.

Example:

  pid = fork do
    Signal.trap('HUP') { puts 'Ouch!'; exit }
    # ... do some work ...
  end
  # ...
  Process.kill('HUP', pid)
  Process.wait

Output:

  Ouch!

Exceptions:

* Raises Errno::EINVAL or RangeError if <tt>signal</tt> is an integer but
  invalid.
* Raises ArgumentError if <tt>signal</tt> is a string or symbol but invalid.
* Raises Errno::ESRCH or RangeError if one of <tt>ids</tt> is invalid.
* Raises Errno::EPERM if needed permissions are not in force.

In the last two cases, signals may have been sent to some processes.

Process::last_status.name: last_status
Process::last_status.comment:
Returns a Process::Status object representing the most recently exited child
process in the current thread, or <tt>nil</tt> if none:

  Process.spawn('ruby', '-e', 'exit 13')
  Process.wait
  Process.last_status # => #<Process::Status: pid 14396 exit 13>

  Process.spawn('ruby', '-e', 'exit 14')
  Process.wait
  Process.last_status # => #<Process::Status: pid 4692 exit 14>

  Process.spawn('ruby', '-e', 'exit 15')
  # 'exit 15' has not been reaped by #wait.
  Process.last_status # => #<Process::Status: pid 4692 exit 14>
  Process.wait
  Process.last_status # => #<Process::Status: pid 1380 exit 15>

Process::maxgroups.name: maxgroups
Process::maxgroups.comment:
Returns the maximum number of group IDs allowed in the supplemental group
access list:

  Process.maxgroups # => 32

Process::maxgroups=.name: maxgroups=
Process::maxgroups=.comment:
Sets the maximum number of group IDs allowed in the supplemental group access
list.

Process::pid.name: pid
Process::pid.comment:
Returns the process ID of the current process:

  Process.pid # => 15668

Process::ppid.name: ppid
Process::ppid.comment:
Returns the process ID of the parent of the current process:

  puts "Pid is #{Process.pid}."
  fork { puts "Parent pid is #{Process.ppid}." }

Output:

  Pid is 271290.
  Parent pid is 271290.

May not return a trustworthy value on certain platforms.

Process::setpgid.name: setpgid
Process::setpgid.comment:
Sets the process group ID for the process given by process ID <tt>pid</tt> to
<tt>pgid</tt>.

Not available on all platforms.

Process::setpgrp.name: setpgrp
Process::setpgrp.comment:
Equivalent to <tt>setpgid(0, 0)</tt>.

Not available on all platforms.

Process::setpriority.name: setpriority
Process::setpriority.comment:
See Process.getpriority.

Examples:

  Process.setpriority(Process::PRIO_USER, 0, 19)    # => 0
  Process.setpriority(Process::PRIO_PROCESS, 0, 19) # => 0
  Process.getpriority(Process::PRIO_USER, 0)        # => 19
  Process.getpriority(Process::PRIO_PROCESS, 0)     # => 19

Not available on all platforms.

Process::setproctitle.name: setproctitle
Process::setproctitle.comment:
Sets the process title that appears on the ps(1) command.  Not necessarily
effective on all platforms.  No exception will be raised regardless of the
result, nor will NotImplementedError be raised even if the platform does not
support the feature.

Calling this method does not affect the value of $0.

  Process.setproctitle('myapp: worker #%d' % worker_id)

This method first appeared in Ruby 2.1 to serve as a global variable free
means to change the process title.

Process::setrlimit.name: setrlimit
Process::setrlimit.comment:
Sets limits for the current process for the given <tt>resource</tt> to
<tt>cur_limit</tt> (soft limit) and <tt>max_limit</tt> (hard limit); returns
<tt>nil</tt>.

Argument <tt>resource</tt> specifies the resource whose limits are to be set;
the argument may be given as a symbol, as a string, or as a constant beginning
with <tt>Process::RLIMIT_</tt> (e.g., <tt>:CORE</tt>, <tt>'CORE'</tt>, or
<tt>Process::RLIMIT_CORE</tt>.

The resources available and supported are system-dependent, and may include
(here expressed as symbols):

* <tt>:AS</tt>: Total available memory (bytes) (SUSv3, NetBSD, FreeBSD,
  OpenBSD except 4.4BSD-Lite).
* <tt>:CORE</tt>: Core size (bytes) (SUSv3).
* <tt>:CPU</tt>: CPU time (seconds) (SUSv3).
* <tt>:DATA</tt>: Data segment (bytes) (SUSv3).
* <tt>:FSIZE</tt>: File size (bytes) (SUSv3).
* <tt>:MEMLOCK</tt>: Total size for mlock(2) (bytes) (4.4BSD, GNU/Linux).
* <tt>:MSGQUEUE</tt>: Allocation for POSIX message queues (bytes) (GNU/Linux).
* <tt>:NICE</tt>: Ceiling on process's nice(2) value (number) (GNU/Linux).
* <tt>:NOFILE</tt>: File descriptors (number) (SUSv3).
* <tt>:NPROC</tt>: Number of processes for the user (number) (4.4BSD,
  GNU/Linux).
* <tt>:NPTS</tt>: Number of pseudo terminals (number) (FreeBSD).
* <tt>:RSS</tt>: Resident memory size (bytes) (4.2BSD, GNU/Linux).
* <tt>:RTPRIO</tt>: Ceiling on the process's real-time priority (number)
  (GNU/Linux).
* <tt>:RTTIME</tt>: CPU time for real-time process (us) (GNU/Linux).
* <tt>:SBSIZE</tt>: All socket buffers (bytes) (NetBSD, FreeBSD).
* <tt>:SIGPENDING</tt>: Number of queued signals allowed (signals)
  (GNU/Linux).
* <tt>:STACK</tt>: Stack size (bytes) (SUSv3).

Arguments <tt>cur_limit</tt> and <tt>max_limit</tt> may be:

* Integers (<tt>max_limit</tt> should not be smaller than <tt>cur_limit</tt>).
* Symbol <tt>:SAVED_MAX</tt>, string <tt>'SAVED_MAX'</tt>, or constant
  <tt>Process::RLIM_SAVED_MAX</tt>: saved maximum limit.
* Symbol <tt>:SAVED_CUR</tt>, string <tt>'SAVED_CUR'</tt>, or constant
  <tt>Process::RLIM_SAVED_CUR</tt>: saved current limit.
* Symbol <tt>:INFINITY</tt>, string <tt>'INFINITY'</tt>, or constant
  <tt>Process::RLIM_INFINITY</tt>: no limit on resource.

This example raises the soft limit of core size to the hard limit to try to
make core dump possible:

  Process.setrlimit(:CORE, Process.getrlimit(:CORE)[1])

Not available on all platforms.

Process::setsid.name: setsid
Process::setsid.comment:
Establishes the current process as a new session and process group leader,
with no controlling tty; returns the session ID:

  Process.setsid # => 27422

Not available on all platforms.

Process::spawn.name: spawn
Process::spawn.call_seq:
spawn([env, ] command_line, options = {}) -> pid
spawn([env, ] exe_path, *args, options  = {}) -> pid
Process::spawn.comment: Creates a new child process by doing one of the following in that process: * Passing string command_line to the shell. * Invoking the executable at exe_path. This method has potential security vulnerabilities if called with untrusted input; see {Command Injection}[rdoc-ref:security/command_injection.rdoc]. Returns the process ID (pid) of the new process, without waiting for it to complete. To avoid zombie processes, the parent process should call either: * Process.wait, to collect the termination statuses of its children. * Process.detach, to register disinterest in their status. The new process is created using the {exec system call}[https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799.2018edition/functions/e xecve.html]; it may inherit some of its environment from the calling program (possibly including open file descriptors). Argument env, if given, is a hash that affects ENV for the new process; see {Execution Environment}[rdoc-ref:Process@Execution+Environment]. Argument options is a hash of options for the new process; see {Execution Options}[rdoc-ref:Process@Execution+Options]. The first required argument is one of the following: * command_line if it is a string, and if it begins with a shell reserved word or special built-in, or if it contains one or more meta characters. * exe_path otherwise. Argument command_line String argument command_line is a command line to be passed to a shell; it must begin with a shell reserved word, begin with a special built-in, or contain meta characters: spawn('if true; then echo "Foo"; fi') # => 798847 # Shell reserved word. Process.wait # => 798847 spawn('exit') # => 798848 # Built-in. Process.wait # => 798848 spawn('date > /tmp/date.tmp') # => 798879 # Contains meta character. Process.wait # => 798849 spawn('date > /nop/date.tmp') # => 798882 # Issues error message. Process.wait # => 798882 The command line may also contain arguments and options for the command: spawn('echo "Foo"') # => 799031 Process.wait # => 799031 Output: Foo See {Execution Shell}[rdoc-ref:Process@Execution+Shell] for details about the shell. Raises an exception if the new process could not execute. Argument exe_path Argument exe_path is one of the following: * The string path to an executable to be called. * A 2-element array containing the path to an executable to be called, and the string to be used as the name of the executing process. spawn('/usr/bin/date') # Path to date on Unix-style system. Process.wait Output: Mon Aug 28 11:43:10 AM CDT 2023 Ruby invokes the executable directly. This form does not use the shell; see {Arguments args}[rdoc-ref:Process@Arguments+args] for caveats. If one or more args is given, each is an argument or option to be passed to the executable: spawn('echo', 'C*') # => 799392 Process.wait # => 799392 spawn('echo', 'hello', 'world') # => 799393 Process.wait # => 799393 Output: C* hello world Raises an exception if the new process could not execute.

Process::times.name: times
Process::times.comment:
Returns a Process::Tms structure that contains user and system CPU times for
the current process, and for its children processes:

  Process.times
  # => #<struct Process::Tms utime=55.122118, stime=35.533068, cutime=0.0, cstime=0.002846>

The precision is platform-defined.

Process::uid.name: uid
Process::uid.call_seq:
Process.uid         -> integer
Process::UID.rid    -> integer
Process::Sys.getuid -> integer
Process::uid.comment:
Returns the (real) user ID of the current process.

  Process.uid # => 1000

Process::uid=.name: uid=
Process::uid=.comment:
Sets the (user) user ID for the current process to <tt>new_uid</tt>:

  Process.uid = 1000 # => 1000

Not available on all platforms.

Process::wait.name: wait
Process::wait.comment:
Waits for a suitable child process to exit, returns its process ID, and sets
<tt>$?</tt> to a Process::Status object containing information on that
process. Which child it waits for depends on the value of the given
<tt>pid</tt>:

* Positive integer: Waits for the child process whose process ID is
  <tt>pid</tt>:

    pid0 = Process.spawn('ruby', '-e', 'exit 13') # => 230866
    pid1 = Process.spawn('ruby', '-e', 'exit 14') # => 230891
    Process.wait(pid0)                            # => 230866
    $?                                            # => #<Process::Status: pid 230866 exit 13>
    Process.wait(pid1)                            # => 230891
    $?                                            # => #<Process::Status: pid 230891 exit 14>
    Process.wait(pid0)                            # Raises Errno::ECHILD

* <tt>0</tt>: Waits for any child process whose group ID is the same as that
  of the current process:

    parent_pgpid = Process.getpgid(Process.pid)
    puts "Parent process group ID is #{parent_pgpid}."
    child0_pid = fork do
      puts "Child 0 pid is #{Process.pid}"
      child0_pgid = Process.getpgid(Process.pid)
      puts "Child 0 process group ID is #{child0_pgid} (same as parent's)."
    end
    child1_pid = fork do
      puts "Child 1 pid is #{Process.pid}"
      Process.setpgid(0, Process.pid)
      child1_pgid = Process.getpgid(Process.pid)
      puts "Child 1 process group ID is #{child1_pgid} (different from parent's)."
    end
    retrieved_pid = Process.wait(0)
    puts "Process.wait(0) returned pid #{retrieved_pid}, which is child 0 pid."
    begin
      Process.wait(0)
    rescue Errno::ECHILD => x
      puts "Raised #{x.class}, because child 1 process group ID differs from parent process group ID."
    end

  Output:

    Parent process group ID is 225764.
    Child 0 pid is 225788
    Child 0 process group ID is 225764 (same as parent's).
    Child 1 pid is 225789
    Child 1 process group ID is 225789 (different from parent's).
    Process.wait(0) returned pid 225788, which is child 0 pid.
    Raised Errno::ECHILD, because child 1 process group ID differs from parent process group ID.

* <tt>-1</tt> (default): Waits for any child process:

    parent_pgpid = Process.getpgid(Process.pid)
    puts "Parent process group ID is #{parent_pgpid}."
    child0_pid = fork do
      puts "Child 0 pid is #{Process.pid}"
      child0_pgid = Process.getpgid(Process.pid)
      puts "Child 0 process group ID is #{child0_pgid} (same as parent's)."
    end
    child1_pid = fork do
      puts "Child 1 pid is #{Process.pid}"
      Process.setpgid(0, Process.pid)
      child1_pgid = Process.getpgid(Process.pid)
      puts "Child 1 process group ID is #{child1_pgid} (different from parent's)."
      sleep 3 # To force child 1 to exit later than child 0 exit.
    end
    child_pids = [child0_pid, child1_pid]
    retrieved_pid = Process.wait(-1)
    puts child_pids.include?(retrieved_pid)
    retrieved_pid = Process.wait(-1)
    puts child_pids.include?(retrieved_pid)

  Output:

    Parent process group ID is 228736.
    Child 0 pid is 228758
    Child 0 process group ID is 228736 (same as parent's).
    Child 1 pid is 228759
    Child 1 process group ID is 228759 (different from parent's).
    true
    true

* Less than <tt>-1</tt>: Waits for any child whose process group ID is
  <tt>-pid</tt>:

    parent_pgpid = Process.getpgid(Process.pid)
    puts "Parent process group ID is #{parent_pgpid}."
    child0_pid = fork do
      puts "Child 0 pid is #{Process.pid}"
      child0_pgid = Process.getpgid(Process.pid)
      puts "Child 0 process group ID is #{child0_pgid} (same as parent's)."
    end
    child1_pid = fork do
      puts "Child 1 pid is #{Process.pid}"
      Process.setpgid(0, Process.pid)
      child1_pgid = Process.getpgid(Process.pid)
      puts "Child 1 process group ID is #{child1_pgid} (different from parent's)."
    end
    sleep 1
    retrieved_pid = Process.wait(-child1_pid)
    puts "Process.wait(-child1_pid) returned pid #{retrieved_pid}, which is child 1 pid."
    begin
      Process.wait(-child1_pid)
    rescue Errno::ECHILD => x
      puts "Raised #{x.class}, because there's no longer a child with process group id #{child1_pid}."
    end

  Output:

    Parent process group ID is 230083.
    Child 0 pid is 230108
    Child 0 process group ID is 230083 (same as parent's).
    Child 1 pid is 230109
    Child 1 process group ID is 230109 (different from parent's).
    Process.wait(-child1_pid) returned pid 230109, which is child 1 pid.
    Raised Errno::ECHILD, because there's no longer a child with process group id 230109.

Argument <tt>flags</tt> should be given as one of the following constants, or
as the logical OR of both:

* Process::WNOHANG: Does not block if no child process is available.
* Process::WUNTRACED: May return a stopped child process, even if not yet
  reported.

Not all flags are available on all platforms.

Raises Errno::ECHILD if there is no suitable child process.

Not available on all platforms.

Process.waitpid is an alias for Process.wait.

Process::wait2.name: wait2
Process::wait2.comment:
Like Process.waitpid, but returns an array containing the child process
<tt>pid</tt> and Process::Status <tt>status</tt>:

  pid = Process.spawn('ruby', '-e', 'exit 13') # => 309581
  Process.wait2(pid)
  # => [309581, #<Process::Status: pid 309581 exit 13>]

Process.waitpid2 is an alias for Process.wait2.

Process::waitall.name: waitall
Process::waitall.comment:
Waits for all children, returns an array of 2-element arrays; each subarray
contains the integer pid and Process::Status status for one of the reaped
child processes:

  pid0 = Process.spawn('ruby', '-e', 'exit 13') # => 325470
  pid1 = Process.spawn('ruby', '-e', 'exit 14') # => 325495
  Process.waitall
  # => [[325470, #<Process::Status: pid 325470 exit 13>], [325495, #<Process::Status: pid 325495 exit 14>]]

Process::waitpid.name: waitpid
Process::waitpid.comment:
Waits for a suitable child process to exit, returns its process ID, and sets
<tt>$?</tt> to a Process::Status object containing information on that
process. Which child it waits for depends on the value of the given
<tt>pid</tt>:

* Positive integer: Waits for the child process whose process ID is
  <tt>pid</tt>:

    pid0 = Process.spawn('ruby', '-e', 'exit 13') # => 230866
    pid1 = Process.spawn('ruby', '-e', 'exit 14') # => 230891
    Process.wait(pid0)                            # => 230866
    $?                                            # => #<Process::Status: pid 230866 exit 13>
    Process.wait(pid1)                            # => 230891
    $?                                            # => #<Process::Status: pid 230891 exit 14>
    Process.wait(pid0)                            # Raises Errno::ECHILD

* <tt>0</tt>: Waits for any child process whose group ID is the same as that
  of the current process:

    parent_pgpid = Process.getpgid(Process.pid)
    puts "Parent process group ID is #{parent_pgpid}."
    child0_pid = fork do
      puts "Child 0 pid is #{Process.pid}"
      child0_pgid = Process.getpgid(Process.pid)
      puts "Child 0 process group ID is #{child0_pgid} (same as parent's)."
    end
    child1_pid = fork do
      puts "Child 1 pid is #{Process.pid}"
      Process.setpgid(0, Process.pid)
      child1_pgid = Process.getpgid(Process.pid)
      puts "Child 1 process group ID is #{child1_pgid} (different from parent's)."
    end
    retrieved_pid = Process.wait(0)
    puts "Process.wait(0) returned pid #{retrieved_pid}, which is child 0 pid."
    begin
      Process.wait(0)
    rescue Errno::ECHILD => x
      puts "Raised #{x.class}, because child 1 process group ID differs from parent process group ID."
    end

  Output:

    Parent process group ID is 225764.
    Child 0 pid is 225788
    Child 0 process group ID is 225764 (same as parent's).
    Child 1 pid is 225789
    Child 1 process group ID is 225789 (different from parent's).
    Process.wait(0) returned pid 225788, which is child 0 pid.
    Raised Errno::ECHILD, because child 1 process group ID differs from parent process group ID.

* <tt>-1</tt> (default): Waits for any child process:

    parent_pgpid = Process.getpgid(Process.pid)
    puts "Parent process group ID is #{parent_pgpid}."
    child0_pid = fork do
      puts "Child 0 pid is #{Process.pid}"
      child0_pgid = Process.getpgid(Process.pid)
      puts "Child 0 process group ID is #{child0_pgid} (same as parent's)."
    end
    child1_pid = fork do
      puts "Child 1 pid is #{Process.pid}"
      Process.setpgid(0, Process.pid)
      child1_pgid = Process.getpgid(Process.pid)
      puts "Child 1 process group ID is #{child1_pgid} (different from parent's)."
      sleep 3 # To force child 1 to exit later than child 0 exit.
    end
    child_pids = [child0_pid, child1_pid]
    retrieved_pid = Process.wait(-1)
    puts child_pids.include?(retrieved_pid)
    retrieved_pid = Process.wait(-1)
    puts child_pids.include?(retrieved_pid)

  Output:

    Parent process group ID is 228736.
    Child 0 pid is 228758
    Child 0 process group ID is 228736 (same as parent's).
    Child 1 pid is 228759
    Child 1 process group ID is 228759 (different from parent's).
    true
    true

* Less than <tt>-1</tt>: Waits for any child whose process group ID is
  <tt>-pid</tt>:

    parent_pgpid = Process.getpgid(Process.pid)
    puts "Parent process group ID is #{parent_pgpid}."
    child0_pid = fork do
      puts "Child 0 pid is #{Process.pid}"
      child0_pgid = Process.getpgid(Process.pid)
      puts "Child 0 process group ID is #{child0_pgid} (same as parent's)."
    end
    child1_pid = fork do
      puts "Child 1 pid is #{Process.pid}"
      Process.setpgid(0, Process.pid)
      child1_pgid = Process.getpgid(Process.pid)
      puts "Child 1 process group ID is #{child1_pgid} (different from parent's)."
    end
    sleep 1
    retrieved_pid = Process.wait(-child1_pid)
    puts "Process.wait(-child1_pid) returned pid #{retrieved_pid}, which is child 1 pid."
    begin
      Process.wait(-child1_pid)
    rescue Errno::ECHILD => x
      puts "Raised #{x.class}, because there's no longer a child with process group id #{child1_pid}."
    end

  Output:

    Parent process group ID is 230083.
    Child 0 pid is 230108
    Child 0 process group ID is 230083 (same as parent's).
    Child 1 pid is 230109
    Child 1 process group ID is 230109 (different from parent's).
    Process.wait(-child1_pid) returned pid 230109, which is child 1 pid.
    Raised Errno::ECHILD, because there's no longer a child with process group id 230109.

Argument <tt>flags</tt> should be given as one of the following constants, or
as the logical OR of both:

* Process::WNOHANG: Does not block if no child process is available.
* Process::WUNTRACED: May return a stopped child process, even if not yet
  reported.

Not all flags are available on all platforms.

Raises Errno::ECHILD if there is no suitable child process.

Not available on all platforms.

Process.waitpid is an alias for Process.wait.

Process::waitpid2.name: waitpid2
Process::waitpid2.comment:
Like Process.waitpid, but returns an array containing the child process
<tt>pid</tt> and Process::Status <tt>status</tt>:

  pid = Process.spawn('ruby', '-e', 'exit 13') # => 309581
  Process.wait2(pid)
  # => [309581, #<Process::Status: pid 309581 exit 13>]

Process.waitpid2 is an alias for Process.wait2.

Process::warmup.name: warmup
Process::warmup.comment:
Notify the Ruby virtual machine that the boot sequence is finished, and that
now is a good time to optimize the application. This is useful for long
running applications.

This method is expected to be called at the end of the application boot. If
the application is deployed using a pre-forking model, <tt>Process.warmup</tt>
should be called in the original process before the first fork.

The actual optimizations performed are entirely implementation specific and
may change in the future without notice.

On CRuby, <tt>Process.warmup</tt>:

* Performs a major GC.
* Compacts the heap.
* Promotes all surviving objects to the old generation.
* Precomputes the coderange of all strings.
* Frees all empty heap pages and increments the allocatable pages counter by
  the number of pages freed.
* Invoke <tt>malloc_trim</tt> if available to free empty malloc pages.
* Eagerly loads the <tt>error_highlight</tt>, <tt>did_you_mean</tt>, and
  <tt>syntax_suggest</tt> gems, which are otherwise loaded lazily on the first
  error display.

Process::GID.name: Process::GID
Process::GID.comment:
The Process::GID module contains a collection of module functions which can be
used to portably get, set, and switch the current process's real, effective,
and saved group IDs.

Process::GID::change_privilege.name: change_privilege
Process::GID::change_privilege.comment: Change the current process's real and effective group ID to that specified by group. Returns the new group ID. Not available on all platforms. [Process.gid, Process.egid] #=> [0, 0] Process::GID.change_privilege(33) #=> 33 [Process.gid, Process.egid] #=> [33, 33]

Process::GID::eid.name: eid
Process::GID::eid.call_seq:
Process.egid        -> integer
Process::GID.eid    -> integer
Process::Sys.geteid -> integer
Process::GID::eid.comment:
Returns the effective group ID for the current process:

  Process.egid # => 500

Not available on all platforms.

Process::GID::from_name.name: from_name
Process::GID::from_name.comment: Get the group ID by the name. If the group is not found, ArgumentError will be raised. Process::GID.from_name("wheel") #=> 0 Process::GID.from_name("nosuchgroup") #=> can't find group for nosuchgroup (ArgumentError)

Process::GID::grant_privilege.name: grant_privilege
Process::GID::grant_privilege.comment: Set the effective group ID, and if possible, the saved group ID of the process to the given group. Returns the new effective group ID. Not available on all platforms. [Process.gid, Process.egid] #=> [0, 0] Process::GID.grant_privilege(31) #=> 33 [Process.gid, Process.egid] #=> [0, 33]

Process::GID::re_exchange.name: re_exchange
Process::GID::re_exchange.comment:
Exchange real and effective group IDs and return the new effective group ID.
Not available on all platforms.

  [Process.gid, Process.egid]   #=> [0, 33]
  Process::GID.re_exchange      #=> 0
  [Process.gid, Process.egid]   #=> [33, 0]

Process::GID::re_exchangeable?.name: re_exchangeable?
Process::GID::re_exchangeable?.comment:
Returns <tt>true</tt> if the real and effective group IDs of a process may be
exchanged on the current platform.

Process::GID::rid.name: rid
Process::GID::rid.call_seq:
Process.gid         -> integer
Process::GID.rid    -> integer
Process::Sys.getgid -> integer
Process::GID::rid.comment:
Returns the (real) group ID for the current process:

  Process.gid # => 1000

Process::GID::sid_available?.name: sid_available?
Process::GID::sid_available?.comment:
Returns <tt>true</tt> if the current platform has saved group ID
functionality.

Process::GID::switch.name: switch
Process::GID::switch.comment: Switch the effective and real group IDs of the current process. If a block is given, the group IDs will be switched back after the block is executed. Returns the new effective group ID if called without a block, and the return value of the block if one is given.

Process::Status.name: Process::Status
Process::Status.comment:
A Process::Status contains information about a system process.

Thread-local variable <tt>$?</tt> is initially <tt>nil</tt>. Some methods
assign to it a Process::Status object that represents a system process (either
running or terminated):

  `ruby -e "exit 99"`
  stat = $?       # => #<Process::Status: pid 1262862 exit 99>
  stat.class      # => Process::Status
  stat.to_i       # => 25344
  stat.stopped?   # => false
  stat.exited?    # => true
  stat.exitstatus # => 99

Process::Status::wait.name: wait
Process::Status::wait.comment:
Like Process.wait, but returns a Process::Status object (instead of an integer
pid or nil); see Process.wait for the values of <tt>pid</tt> and
<tt>flags</tt>.

If there are child processes, waits for a child process to exit and returns a
Process::Status object containing information on that process. Unlike
Process.wait, this method does not set thread-local variable <tt>$?</tt>:

  Process.spawn('cat /nop') # => 1155880
  Process::Status.wait      # => #<Process::Status: pid 1155880 exit 1>
  $?                        # => nil # Not set.

If there is no child process, returns an "empty" Process::Status object that
does not represent an actual process:

  Process::Status.wait # => #<Process::Status: pid -1 exit 0>

May invoke the scheduler hook Fiber::Scheduler#process_wait.

Not available on all platforms.

Process::Status#==.comment:
Returns whether the value of #to_i == <tt>other</tt>:

  `cat /nop`
  stat = $?                # => #<Process::Status: pid 1170366 exit 1>
  sprintf('%x', stat.to_i) # => "100"
  stat == 0x100            # => true

Process::Status#coredump?.name: coredump?
Process::Status#coredump?.comment:
Returns <tt>true</tt> if the process generated a coredump when it terminated,
<tt>false</tt> if not.

Not available on all platforms.

Process::Status#exited?.name: exited?
Process::Status#exited?.comment:
Returns <tt>true</tt> if the process exited normally (for example using an
<tt>exit()</tt> call or finishing the program), <tt>false</tt> if not.

Process::Status#exitstatus.name: exitstatus
Process::Status#exitstatus.comment:
Returns the least significant eight bits of the return code of the process if
it has exited; <tt>nil</tt> otherwise:

  `exit 99`
  $?.exitstatus # => 99

Process::Status#inspect.name: inspect
Process::Status#inspect.comment:
Returns a string representation of <tt>self</tt>:

  system("false")
  $?.inspect # => "#<Process::Status: pid 1303494 exit 1>"

Process::Status#pid.name: pid
Process::Status#pid.comment:
Returns the process ID of the process:

  system("false")
  $?.pid # => 1247002

Process::Status#signaled?.name: signaled?
Process::Status#signaled?.comment:
Returns <tt>true</tt> if the process terminated because of an uncaught signal,
<tt>false</tt> otherwise.

Process::Status#stopped?.name: stopped?
Process::Status#stopped?.comment:
Returns <tt>true</tt> if this process is stopped, and if the corresponding
#wait call had the Process::WUNTRACED flag set, <tt>false</tt> otherwise.

Process::Status#stopsig.name: stopsig
Process::Status#stopsig.comment:
Returns the number of the signal that caused the process to stop, or
<tt>nil</tt> if the process is not stopped.

Process::Status#success?.name: success?
Process::Status#success?.comment:
Returns:

* <tt>true</tt> if the process has completed successfully and exited.
* <tt>false</tt> if the process has completed unsuccessfully and exited.
* <tt>nil</tt> if the process has not exited.

Process::Status#termsig.name: termsig
Process::Status#termsig.comment:
Returns the number of the signal that caused the process to terminate or
<tt>nil</tt> if the process was not terminated by an uncaught signal.

Process::Status#to_i.name: to_i
Process::Status#to_i.comment:
Returns the system-dependent integer status of <tt>self</tt>:

  `cat /nop`
  $?.to_i # => 256

Process::Status#to_s.name: to_s
Process::Status#to_s.comment:
Returns a string representation of <tt>self</tt>:

  `cat /nop`
  $?.to_s # => "pid 1262141 exit 1"

Process::Sys.name: Process::Sys
Process::Sys.comment:
The Process::Sys module contains UID and GID functions which provide direct
bindings to the system calls of the same names instead of the more-portable
versions of the same functionality found in the <tt>Process</tt>,
Process::UID, and Process::GID modules.

Process::Sys::getegid.name: getegid
Process::Sys::getegid.call_seq:
Process.egid        -> integer
Process::GID.eid    -> integer
Process::Sys.geteid -> integer
Process::Sys::getegid.comment:
Returns the effective group ID for the current process:

  Process.egid # => 500

Not available on all platforms.

Process::Sys::geteuid.name: geteuid
Process::Sys::geteuid.call_seq:
Process.euid         -> integer
Process::UID.eid     -> integer
Process::Sys.geteuid -> integer
Process::Sys::geteuid.comment:
Returns the effective user ID for the current process.

  Process.euid # => 501

Process::Sys::getgid.name: getgid
Process::Sys::getgid.call_seq:
Process.gid         -> integer
Process::GID.rid    -> integer
Process::Sys.getgid -> integer
Process::Sys::getgid.comment:
Returns the (real) group ID for the current process:

  Process.gid # => 1000

Process::Sys::getuid.name: getuid
Process::Sys::getuid.call_seq:
Process.uid         -> integer
Process::UID.rid    -> integer
Process::Sys.getuid -> integer
Process::Sys::getuid.comment:
Returns the (real) user ID of the current process.

  Process.uid # => 1000

Process::Sys::issetugid.name: issetugid
Process::Sys::issetugid.comment:
Returns <tt>true</tt> if the process was created as a result of an execve(2)
system call which had either of the setuid or setgid bits set (and extra
privileges were given as a result) or if it has changed any of its real,
effective or saved user or group IDs since it began execution.

Process::Sys::setegid.name: setegid
Process::Sys::setegid.comment: Set the effective group ID of the calling process to group. Not available on all platforms.

Process::Sys::seteuid.name: seteuid
Process::Sys::seteuid.comment: Set the effective user ID of the calling process to user. Not available on all platforms.

Process::Sys::setgid.name: setgid
Process::Sys::setgid.comment: Set the group ID of the current process to group. Not available on all platforms.

Process::Sys::setregid.name: setregid
Process::Sys::setregid.comment: Sets the (group) real and/or effective group IDs of the current process to rid and eid, respectively. A value of -1 for either means to leave that ID unchanged. Not available on all platforms.

Process::Sys::setresgid.name: setresgid
Process::Sys::setresgid.comment: Sets the (group) real, effective, and saved user IDs of the current process to rid, eid, and sid respectively. A value of -1 for any value means to leave that ID unchanged. Not available on all platforms.

Process::Sys::setresuid.name: setresuid
Process::Sys::setresuid.comment: Sets the (user) real, effective, and saved user IDs of the current process to rid, eid, and sid respectively. A value of -1 for any value means to leave that ID unchanged. Not available on all platforms.

Process::Sys::setreuid.name: setreuid
Process::Sys::setreuid.comment: Sets the (user) real and/or effective user IDs of the current process to rid and eid, respectively. A value of -1 for either means to leave that ID unchanged. Not available on all platforms.

Process::Sys::setrgid.name: setrgid
Process::Sys::setrgid.comment: Set the real group ID of the calling process to group. Not available on all platforms.

Process::Sys::setruid.name: setruid
Process::Sys::setruid.comment: Set the real user ID of the calling process to user. Not available on all platforms.

Process::Sys::setuid.name: setuid
Process::Sys::setuid.comment: Set the user ID of the current process to user. Not available on all platforms.

Process::UID.name: Process::UID
Process::UID.comment:
The Process::UID module contains a collection of module functions which can be
used to portably get, set, and switch the current process's real, effective,
and saved user IDs.

Process::UID::change_privilege.name: change_privilege
Process::UID::change_privilege.comment: Change the current process's real and effective user ID to that specified by user. Returns the new user ID. Not available on all platforms. [Process.uid, Process.euid] #=> [0, 0] Process::UID.change_privilege(31) #=> 31 [Process.uid, Process.euid] #=> [31, 31]

Process::UID::eid.name: eid
Process::UID::eid.call_seq:
Process.euid         -> integer
Process::UID.eid     -> integer
Process::Sys.geteuid -> integer
Process::UID::eid.comment:
Returns the effective user ID for the current process.

  Process.euid # => 501

Process::UID::from_name.name: from_name
Process::UID::from_name.comment: Get the user ID by the name. If the user is not found, ArgumentError will be raised. Process::UID.from_name("root") #=> 0 Process::UID.from_name("nosuchuser") #=> can't find user for nosuchuser (ArgumentError)

Process::UID::grant_privilege.name: grant_privilege
Process::UID::grant_privilege.comment: Set the effective user ID, and if possible, the saved user ID of the process to the given user. Returns the new effective user ID. Not available on all platforms. [Process.uid, Process.euid] #=> [0, 0] Process::UID.grant_privilege(31) #=> 31 [Process.uid, Process.euid] #=> [0, 31]

Process::UID::re_exchange.name: re_exchange
Process::UID::re_exchange.comment:
Exchange real and effective user IDs and return the new effective user ID. Not
available on all platforms.

  [Process.uid, Process.euid]   #=> [0, 31]
  Process::UID.re_exchange      #=> 0
  [Process.uid, Process.euid]   #=> [31, 0]

Process::UID::re_exchangeable?.name: re_exchangeable?
Process::UID::re_exchangeable?.comment:
Returns <tt>true</tt> if the real and effective user IDs of a process may be
exchanged on the current platform.

Process::UID::rid.name: rid
Process::UID::rid.call_seq:
Process.uid         -> integer
Process::UID.rid    -> integer
Process::Sys.getuid -> integer
Process::UID::rid.comment:
Returns the (real) user ID of the current process.

  Process.uid # => 1000

Process::UID::sid_available?.name: sid_available?
Process::UID::sid_available?.comment: Returns <tt>true</tt> if the current platform has saved user ID functionality.

Process::UID::switch.name: switch
Process::UID::switch.comment: Switch the effective and real user IDs of the current process. If a block is given, the user IDs will be switched back after the block is executed. Returns the new effective user ID if called without a block, and the return value of the block if one is given.

Psych.name: Psych
Psych.comment:
= Overview

Psych is a YAML parser and emitter. Psych leverages libyaml [Home page:
https://pyyaml.org/wiki/LibYAML] or [git repo:
https://github.com/yaml/libyaml] for its YAML parsing and emitting
capabilities. In addition to wrapping libyaml, Psych also knows how to
serialize and de-serialize most Ruby objects to and from the YAML format.

= I NEED TO PARSE OR EMIT YAML RIGHT NOW!

  # Parse some YAML
  Psych.load("--- foo") # => "foo"

  # Emit some YAML
  Psych.dump("foo")     # => "--- foo\n...\n"
  { :a => 'b'}.to_yaml  # => "---\n:a: b\n"

Got more time on your hands?  Keep on reading!

== YAML Parsing

Psych provides a range of interfaces for parsing a YAML document ranging from
low level to high level, depending on your parsing needs.  At the lowest
level, is an event based parser.  Mid level is access to the raw YAML AST, and
at the highest level is the ability to unmarshal YAML to Ruby objects.

== YAML Emitting

Psych provides a range of interfaces ranging from low to high level for
producing YAML documents.  Very similar to the YAML parsing interfaces, Psych
provides at the lowest level, an event based system, mid-level is building a
YAML AST, and the highest level is converting a Ruby object straight to a YAML
document.

== High-level API

=== Parsing

The high level YAML parser provided by Psych simply takes YAML as input and
returns a Ruby data structure.  For information on using the high level parser
see Psych.load

==== Reading from a string

  Psych.safe_load("--- a")             # => 'a'
  Psych.safe_load("---\n - a\n - b")   # => ['a', 'b']
  # From a trusted string:
  Psych.load("--- !ruby/range\nbegin: 0\nend: 42\nexcl: false\n") # => 0..42

==== Reading from a file

  Psych.safe_load_file("data.yml", permitted_classes: [Date])
  Psych.load_file("trusted_database.yml")

==== Exception handling

  begin
    # The second argument changes only the exception contents
    Psych.parse("--- `", "file.txt")
  rescue Psych::SyntaxError => ex
    ex.file    # => 'file.txt'
    ex.message # => "(file.txt): found character that cannot start any token"
  end

=== Emitting

The high level emitter has the easiest interface.  Psych simply takes a Ruby
data structure and converts it to a YAML document.  See Psych.dump for more
information on dumping a Ruby data structure.

==== Writing to a string

  # Dump an array, get back a YAML string
  Psych.dump(['a', 'b'])  # => "---\n- a\n- b\n"

  # Dump an array to an IO object
  Psych.dump(['a', 'b'], StringIO.new)  # => #<StringIO:0x000001009d0890>

  # Dump an array with indentation set
  Psych.dump(['a', ['b']], :indentation => 3) # => "---\n- a\n-  - b\n"

  # Dump an array to an IO with indentation set
  Psych.dump(['a', ['b']], StringIO.new, :indentation => 3)

==== Writing to a file

Currently there is no direct API for dumping Ruby structure to file:

  File.open('database.yml', 'w') do |file|
    file.write(Psych.dump(['a', 'b']))
  end

== Mid-level API

=== Parsing

Psych provides access to an AST produced from parsing a YAML document.  This
tree is built using the Psych::Parser and Psych::TreeBuilder.  The AST can be
examined and manipulated freely.  Please see Psych::parse_stream,
Psych::Nodes, and Psych::Nodes::Node for more information on dealing with YAML
syntax trees.

==== Reading from a string

  # Returns Psych::Nodes::Stream
  Psych.parse_stream("---\n - a\n - b")

  # Returns Psych::Nodes::Document
  Psych.parse("---\n - a\n - b")

==== Reading from a file

  # Returns Psych::Nodes::Stream
  Psych.parse_stream(File.read('database.yml'))

  # Returns Psych::Nodes::Document
  Psych.parse_file('database.yml')

==== Exception handling

  begin
    # The second argument changes only the exception contents
    Psych.parse("--- `", "file.txt")
  rescue Psych::SyntaxError => ex
    ex.file    # => 'file.txt'
    ex.message # => "(file.txt): found character that cannot start any token"
  end

=== Emitting

At the mid level is building an AST.  This AST is exactly the same as the AST
used when parsing a YAML document.  Users can build an AST by hand and the AST
knows how to emit itself as a YAML document.  See Psych::Nodes,
Psych::Nodes::Node, and Psych::TreeBuilder for more information on building a
YAML AST.

==== Writing to a string

  # We need Psych::Nodes::Stream (not Psych::Nodes::Document)
  stream = Psych.parse_stream("---\n - a\n - b")

  stream.to_yaml # => "---\n- a\n- b\n"

==== Writing to a file

  # We need Psych::Nodes::Stream (not Psych::Nodes::Document)
  stream = Psych.parse_stream(File.read('database.yml'))

  File.open('database.yml', 'w') do |file|
    file.write(stream.to_yaml)
  end

== Low-level API

=== Parsing

The lowest level parser should be used when the YAML input is already known,
and the developer does not want to pay the price of building an AST or
automatic detection and conversion to Ruby objects.  See Psych::Parser for
more information on using the event based parser.

==== Reading to Psych::Nodes::Stream structure

  parser = Psych::Parser.new(TreeBuilder.new) # => #<Psych::Parser>
  parser = Psych.parser                       # it's an alias for the above

  parser.parse("---\n - a\n - b")             # => #<Psych::Parser>
  parser.handler                              # => #<Psych::TreeBuilder>
  parser.handler.root                         # => #<Psych::Nodes::Stream>

==== Receiving an events stream

  recorder = Psych::Handlers::Recorder.new
  parser = Psych::Parser.new(recorder)

  parser.parse("---\n - a\n - b")
  recorder.events # => [list of [event, args] lists]
                  # event is one of: Psych::Handler::EVENTS
                  # args are the arguments passed to the event

=== Emitting

The lowest level emitter is an event based system.  Events are sent to a
Psych::Emitter object.  That object knows how to convert the events to a YAML
document.  This interface should be used when document format is known in
advance or speed is a concern.  See Psych::Emitter for more information.

==== Writing to a Ruby structure

  Psych.parser.parse("--- a")       # => #<Psych::Parser>

  parser.handler.first              # => #<Psych::Nodes::Stream>
  parser.handler.first.to_ruby      # => ["a"]

  parser.handler.root.first         # => #<Psych::Nodes::Document>
  parser.handler.root.first.to_ruby # => "a"

  # You can instantiate an Emitter manually
  Psych::Visitors::ToRuby.new.accept(parser.handler.root.first)
  # => "a"

Psych::dump.name: dump
Psych::dump.call_seq:
Psych.dump(o)               -> string of yaml
Psych.dump(o, options)      -> string of yaml
Psych.dump(o, io)           -> io object passed in
Psych.dump(o, io, options)  -> io object passed in
Psych::dump.comment:
Dump Ruby object <tt>o</tt> to a YAML string.  Optional <tt>options</tt> may
be passed in to control the output format.  If an IO object is passed in, the
YAML will be dumped to that IO object.

Currently supported options are:

<tt>:indentation</tt>:
  Number of space characters used to indent. Acceptable value should be in
  <tt>0..9</tt> range, otherwise option is ignored.

  Default: <tt>2</tt>.

<tt>:line_width</tt>:
  Max character to wrap line at. For unlimited line width use <tt>-1</tt>.

  Default: <tt>0</tt> (meaning "wrap at 81").

<tt>:canonical</tt>:
  Write "canonical" YAML form (very verbose, yet strictly formal).

  Default: <tt>false</tt>.

<tt>:header</tt>:
  Write <tt>%YAML [version]</tt> at the beginning of document.

  Default: <tt>false</tt>.

<tt>:stringify_names</tt>:
  Dump symbol keys in Hash objects as string.

  Default: <tt>false</tt>.

Example:

  # Dump an array, get back a YAML string
  Psych.dump(['a', 'b'])  # => "---\n- a\n- b\n"

  # Dump an array to an IO object
  Psych.dump(['a', 'b'], StringIO.new)  # => #<StringIO:0x000001009d0890>

  # Dump an array with indentation set
  Psych.dump(['a', ['b']], indentation: 3) # => "---\n- a\n-  - b\n"

  # Dump an array to an IO with indentation set
  Psych.dump(['a', ['b']], StringIO.new, indentation: 3)

  # Dump hash with symbol keys as string
  Psych.dump({a: "b"}, stringify_names: true) # => "---\na: b\n"

Psych::dump_stream.name: dump_stream
Psych::dump_stream.comment:
Dump a list of objects as separate documents to a document stream.

Example:

  Psych.dump_stream("foo\n  ", {}) # => "--- ! \"foo\\n  \"\n--- {}\n"

Psych::libfyaml_version.name: libfyaml_version
Psych::libfyaml_version.comment:
Returns the libfyaml version string. This method is only defined when psych
was built with the experimental libfyaml backend (<tt>--enable-libfyaml</tt>).

Psych::libyaml_version.name: libyaml_version
Psych::libyaml_version.comment:
Returns the version of the underlying YAML library as a three-element array.
This is libyaml by default. On the experimental libfyaml backend, where
libyaml is not linked, it reports the libfyaml version instead.

Psych::load.name: load
Psych::load.params: (yaml, permitted_classes: [Symbol], permitted_symbols: [], aliases: false, filename: nil, fallback: nil, symbolize_names: false, freeze: false, strict_integer: false, parse_symbols: true)
Psych::load.comment:
Load <tt>yaml</tt> in to a Ruby data structure.  If multiple documents are
provided, the object contained in the first document will be returned.
<tt>filename</tt> will be used in the exception message if any exception is
raised while parsing.  If <tt>yaml</tt> is empty, it returns the specified
<tt>fallback</tt> return value, which defaults to <tt>nil</tt>.

Raises a Psych::SyntaxError when a YAML syntax error is detected.

Example:

  Psych.load("--- a")             # => 'a'
  Psych.load("---\n - a\n - b")   # => ['a', 'b']

  begin
    Psych.load("--- `", filename: "file.txt")
  rescue Psych::SyntaxError => ex
    ex.file    # => 'file.txt'
    ex.message # => "(file.txt): found character that cannot start any token"
  end

When the optional <tt>symbolize_names</tt> keyword argument is set to a true
value, returns symbols for keys in Hash objects (default: strings).

  Psych.load("---\n foo: bar")                         # => {"foo"=>"bar"}
  Psych.load("---\n foo: bar", symbolize_names: true)  # => {:foo=>"bar"}

Raises a TypeError when `yaml` parameter is NilClass.  This method is similar
to `safe_load` except that `Symbol` objects are allowed by default.

Psych::load_file.name: load_file
Psych::load_file.comment:
Loads the document contained in <tt>filename</tt>.  Returns the yaml contained
in <tt>filename</tt> as a Ruby object, or if the file is empty, it returns the
specified <tt>fallback</tt> return value, which defaults to <tt>nil</tt>. See
load for options.

Psych::load_stream.name: load_stream
Psych::load_stream.comment:
Load multiple documents given in <tt>yaml</tt>.  Returns the parsed documents
as a list.  If a block is given, each document will be converted to Ruby and
passed to the block during parsing

Example:

  Psych.load_stream("--- foo\n...\n--- bar\n...") # => ['foo', 'bar']

  list = []
  Psych.load_stream("--- foo\n...\n--- bar\n...") do |ruby|
    list << ruby
  end
  list # => ['foo', 'bar']

Psych::parse.name: parse
Psych::parse.comment:
Parse a YAML string in <tt>yaml</tt>.  Returns the Psych::Nodes::Document.
<tt>filename</tt> is used in the exception message if a Psych::SyntaxError is
raised.

Raises a Psych::SyntaxError when a YAML syntax error is detected.

Example:

  Psych.parse("---\n - a\n - b") # => #<Psych::Nodes::Document:0x00>

  begin
    Psych.parse("--- `", filename: "file.txt")
  rescue Psych::SyntaxError => ex
    ex.file    # => 'file.txt'
    ex.message # => "(file.txt): found character that cannot start any token"
  end

See Psych::Nodes for more information about YAML AST.

Psych::parse_file.name: parse_file
Psych::parse_file.comment:
Parse a file at <tt>filename</tt>. Returns the Psych::Nodes::Document.

Raises a Psych::SyntaxError when a YAML syntax error is detected.

Psych::parse_stream.name: parse_stream
Psych::parse_stream.comment:
Parse a YAML string in <tt>yaml</tt>.  Returns the Psych::Nodes::Stream. This
method can handle multiple YAML documents contained in <tt>yaml</tt>.
<tt>filename</tt> is used in the exception message if a Psych::SyntaxError is
raised.

If a block is given, a Psych::Nodes::Document node will be yielded to the
block as it's being parsed.

Raises a Psych::SyntaxError when a YAML syntax error is detected.

Example:

  Psych.parse_stream("---\n - a\n - b") # => #<Psych::Nodes::Stream:0x00>

  Psych.parse_stream("--- a\n--- b") do |node|
    node # => #<Psych::Nodes::Document:0x00>
  end

  begin
    Psych.parse_stream("--- `", filename: "file.txt")
  rescue Psych::SyntaxError => ex
    ex.file    # => 'file.txt'
    ex.message # => "(file.txt): found character that cannot start any token"
  end

Raises a TypeError when NilClass is passed.

See Psych::Nodes for more information about YAML AST.

Psych::safe_dump.name: safe_dump
Psych::safe_dump.call_seq:
Psych.safe_dump(o)               -> string of yaml
Psych.safe_dump(o, options)      -> string of yaml
Psych.safe_dump(o, io)           -> io object passed in
Psych.safe_dump(o, io, options)  -> io object passed in
Psych::safe_dump.comment:
Safely dump Ruby object <tt>o</tt> to a YAML string. Optional <tt>options</tt>
may be passed in to control the output format.  If an IO object is passed in,
the YAML will be dumped to that IO object. By default, only the following
classes are allowed to be serialized:

* TrueClass
* FalseClass
* NilClass
* Integer
* Float
* String
* Array
* Hash

Arbitrary classes can be allowed by adding those classes to the
<tt>permitted_classes</tt> keyword argument.  They are additive.  For example,
to allow Date serialization:

  Psych.safe_dump(yaml, permitted_classes: [Date])

Now the Date class can be dumped in addition to the classes listed above.

A Psych::DisallowedClass exception will be raised if the object contains a
class that isn't in the <tt>permitted_classes</tt> list.

Currently supported options are:

<tt>:indentation</tt>:
  Number of space characters used to indent. Acceptable value should be in
  <tt>0..9</tt> range, otherwise option is ignored.

  Default: <tt>2</tt>.

<tt>:line_width</tt>:
  Max character to wrap line at. For unlimited line width use <tt>-1</tt>.

  Default: <tt>0</tt> (meaning "wrap at 81").

<tt>:canonical</tt>:
  Write "canonical" YAML form (very verbose, yet strictly formal).

  Default: <tt>false</tt>.

<tt>:header</tt>:
  Write <tt>%YAML [version]</tt> at the beginning of document.

  Default: <tt>false</tt>.

<tt>:stringify_names</tt>:
  Dump symbol keys in Hash objects as string.

  Default: <tt>false</tt>.

Example:

  # Dump an array, get back a YAML string
  Psych.safe_dump(['a', 'b'])  # => "---\n- a\n- b\n"

  # Dump an array to an IO object
  Psych.safe_dump(['a', 'b'], StringIO.new)  # => #<StringIO:0x000001009d0890>

  # Dump an array with indentation set
  Psych.safe_dump(['a', ['b']], indentation: 3) # => "---\n- a\n-  - b\n"

  # Dump an array to an IO with indentation set
  Psych.safe_dump(['a', ['b']], StringIO.new, indentation: 3)

  # Dump hash with symbol keys as string
  Psych.dump({a: "b"}, stringify_names: true) # => "---\na: b\n"

Psych::safe_load.name: safe_load
Psych::safe_load.params: (yaml, permitted_classes: [], permitted_symbols: [], aliases: false, filename: nil, fallback: nil, symbolize_names: false, freeze: false, strict_integer: false, parse_symbols: true)
Psych::safe_load.comment:
Safely load the yaml string in <tt>yaml</tt>.  By default, only the following
classes are allowed to be deserialized:

* TrueClass
* FalseClass
* NilClass
* Integer
* Float
* String
* Array
* Hash

Recursive data structures are not allowed by default.  Arbitrary classes can
be allowed by adding those classes to the <tt>permitted_classes</tt> keyword
argument.  They are additive.  For example, to allow Date deserialization:

  Psych.safe_load(yaml, permitted_classes: [Date])

Now the Date class can be loaded in addition to the classes listed above.

Aliases can be explicitly allowed by changing the <tt>aliases</tt> keyword
argument. For example:

  x = []
  x << x
  yaml = Psych.dump x
  Psych.safe_load yaml               # => raises an exception
  Psych.safe_load yaml, aliases: true # => loads the aliases

A Psych::DisallowedClass exception will be raised if the yaml contains a class
that isn't in the <tt>permitted_classes</tt> list.

A Psych::AliasesNotEnabled exception will be raised if the yaml contains
aliases but the <tt>aliases</tt> keyword argument is set to false.

<tt>filename</tt> will be used in the exception message if any exception is
raised while parsing.

When the optional <tt>symbolize_names</tt> keyword argument is set to a true
value, returns symbols for keys in Hash objects (default: strings).

  Psych.safe_load("---\n foo: bar")                         # => {"foo"=>"bar"}
  Psych.safe_load("---\n foo: bar", symbolize_names: true)  # => {:foo=>"bar"}

Psych::safe_load_file.name: safe_load_file
Psych::safe_load_file.comment:
Safely loads the document contained in <tt>filename</tt>.  Returns the yaml
contained in <tt>filename</tt> as a Ruby object, or if the file is empty, it
returns the specified <tt>fallback</tt> return value, which defaults to
<tt>nil</tt>. See safe_load for options.

Psych::safe_load_stream.name: safe_load_stream
Psych::safe_load_stream.comment:
Load multiple documents given in <tt>yaml</tt>. Returns the parsed documents
as a list.

Example:

  Psych.safe_load_stream("--- foo\n...\n--- bar\n...") # => ['foo', 'bar']

  list = []
  Psych.safe_load_stream("--- foo\n...\n--- bar\n...") do |ruby|
    list << ruby
  end
  list # => ['foo', 'bar']

Psych::to_json.name: to_json
Psych::to_json.comment: Dump Ruby <tt>object</tt> to a JSON string.

Psych::unsafe_load.name: unsafe_load
Psych::unsafe_load.params: (yaml, filename: nil, fallback: false, symbolize_names: false, freeze: false, strict_integer: false, parse_symbols: true)
Psych::unsafe_load.comment:
Load <tt>yaml</tt> in to a Ruby data structure.  If multiple documents are
provided, the object contained in the first document will be returned.
<tt>filename</tt> will be used in the exception message if any exception is
raised while parsing.  If <tt>yaml</tt> is empty, it returns the specified
<tt>fallback</tt> return value, which defaults to <tt>false</tt>.

Raises a Psych::SyntaxError when a YAML syntax error is detected.

Example:

  Psych.unsafe_load("--- a")             # => 'a'
  Psych.unsafe_load("---\n - a\n - b")   # => ['a', 'b']

  begin
    Psych.unsafe_load("--- `", filename: "file.txt")
  rescue Psych::SyntaxError => ex
    ex.file    # => 'file.txt'
    ex.message # => "(file.txt): found character that cannot start any token"
  end

When the optional <tt>symbolize_names</tt> keyword argument is set to a true
value, returns symbols for keys in Hash objects (default: strings).

  Psych.unsafe_load("---\n foo: bar")                         # => {"foo"=>"bar"}
  Psych.unsafe_load("---\n foo: bar", symbolize_names: true)  # => {:foo=>"bar"}

Raises a TypeError when `yaml` parameter is NilClass

NOTE: This method *should not* be used to parse untrusted documents, such as
YAML documents that are supplied via user input.  Instead, please use the load
method or the safe_load method.

Psych::unsafe_load_file.name: unsafe_load_file
Psych::unsafe_load_file.comment:
Load the document contained in <tt>filename</tt>.  Returns the yaml contained
in <tt>filename</tt> as a Ruby object, or if the file is empty, it returns the
specified <tt>fallback</tt> return value, which defaults to <tt>false</tt>.

NOTE: This method *should not* be used to parse untrusted documents, such as
YAML documents that are supplied via user input.  Instead, please use the
safe_load_file method.

Psych::Coder.name: Psych::Coder
Psych::Coder.comment:
If an object defines <tt>encode_with</tt>, then an instance of Psych::Coder
will be passed to the method when the object is being serialized.  The Coder
automatically assumes a Psych::Nodes::Mapping is being emitted.  Other objects
like Sequence and Scalar may be emitted if <tt>seq=</tt> or <tt>scalar=</tt>
are called, respectively.

Psych::Coder#map.name: map
Psych::Coder#map.comment: Emit a map.  The coder will be yielded to the block.

Psych::Emitter::new.name: new
Psych::Emitter::new.comment: Create a new Psych::Emitter that writes to <tt>io</tt>.

Psych::Emitter#alias.name: alias
Psych::Emitter#alias.comment:
Emit an alias with <tt>anchor</tt>.

See Psych::Handler#alias

Psych::Emitter#canonical.name: canonical
Psych::Emitter#canonical.comment: Get the output style, canonical or not.

Psych::Emitter#canonical=.name: canonical=
Psych::Emitter#canonical=.comment: Set the output style to canonical, or not.

Psych::Emitter#end_document.name: end_document
Psych::Emitter#end_document.comment:
End a document emission with an <tt>implicit</tt> ending.

See Psych::Handler#end_document

Psych::Emitter#end_mapping.name: end_mapping
Psych::Emitter#end_mapping.comment:
Emit the end of a mapping.

See Psych::Handler#end_mapping

Psych::Emitter#end_stream.name: end_stream
Psych::Emitter#end_stream.comment:
End a stream emission

See Psych::Handler#end_stream

Psych::Emitter#indentation=.name: indentation=
Psych::Emitter#indentation=.comment:
Set the indentation level to <tt>level</tt>.  The level must be less than 10
and greater than 1.

Psych::Emitter#line_width=.name: line_width=
Psych::Emitter#line_width=.comment: Set the preferred line with to <tt>width</tt>.

Psych::Emitter#scalar.name: scalar
Psych::Emitter#scalar.call_seq: emitter.scalar(value, anchor, tag, plain, quoted, style)
Psych::Emitter#scalar.comment:
Emit a scalar with <tt>value</tt>, <tt>anchor</tt>, <tt>tag</tt>, and a
<tt>plain</tt> or <tt>quoted</tt> string type with <tt>style</tt>.

See Psych::Handler#scalar

Psych::Emitter#start_document.name: start_document
Psych::Emitter#start_document.comment:
Start a document emission with YAML <tt>version</tt>, <tt>tags</tt>, and an
<tt>implicit</tt> start.

See Psych::Handler#start_document

Psych::Emitter#start_mapping.name: start_mapping
Psych::Emitter#start_mapping.comment:
Start emitting a YAML map with <tt>anchor</tt>, <tt>tag</tt>, an
<tt>implicit</tt> start and end, and <tt>style</tt>.

See Psych::Handler#start_mapping

Psych::Emitter#start_sequence.name: start_sequence
Psych::Emitter#start_sequence.comment:
Start emitting a sequence with <tt>anchor</tt>, a <tt>tag</tt>,
<tt>implicit</tt> sequence start and end, along with <tt>style</tt>.

See Psych::Handler#start_sequence

Psych::Emitter#start_stream.name: start_stream
Psych::Emitter#start_stream.comment:
Start a stream emission with <tt>encoding</tt>

See Psych::Handler#start_stream

Psych::Handler.name: Psych::Handler
Psych::Handler.comment:
Psych::Handler is an abstract base class that defines the events used when
dealing with Psych::Parser.  Clients who want to use Psych::Parser should
implement a class that inherits from Psych::Handler and define events that
they can handle.

Psych::Handler defines all events that Psych::Parser can possibly send to
event handlers.

See Psych::Parser for more details

Psych::Handler#alias.name: alias
Psych::Handler#alias.comment:
Called when an alias is found to <tt>anchor</tt>.  <tt>anchor</tt> will be the
name of the anchor found.

=== Example

Here we have an example of an array that references itself in YAML:

  --- &ponies
  - first element
  - *ponies

&ponies is the anchor, *ponies is the alias.  In this case, alias is called
with "ponies".

Psych::Handler#empty.name: empty
Psych::Handler#empty.comment: Called when an empty event happens. (Which, as far as I can tell, is never).

Psych::Handler#end_document.name: end_document
Psych::Handler#end_document.comment:
Called with the document ends.  <tt>implicit</tt> is a boolean value
indicating whether or not the document has an implicit ending.

=== Example

Given the following YAML:

  ---
    hello world

<tt>implicit</tt> will be true.  Given this YAML:

  ---
    hello world
  ...

<tt>implicit</tt> will be false.

Psych::Handler#end_stream.name: end_stream
Psych::Handler#end_stream.comment: Called when the YAML stream ends

Psych::Handler#event_location.name: event_location
Psych::Handler#event_location.comment: Called before each event with line/column information.

Psych::Handler#scalar.name: scalar
Psych::Handler#scalar.comment:
Called when a scalar <tt>value</tt> is found.  The scalar may have an
<tt>anchor</tt>, a <tt>tag</tt>, be implicitly <tt>plain</tt> or implicitly
<tt>quoted</tt>

<tt>value</tt> is the string value of the scalar <tt>anchor</tt> is an
associated anchor or nil <tt>tag</tt> is an associated tag or nil
<tt>plain</tt> is a boolean value <tt>quoted</tt> is a boolean value
<tt>style</tt> is an integer indicating the string style

See the constants in Psych::Nodes::Scalar for the possible values of
<tt>style</tt>

=== Example

Here is a YAML document that exercises most of the possible ways this method
can be called:

  ---
  - !str "foo"
  - &anchor fun
  - many
    lines
  - |
    many
    newlines

The above YAML document contains a list with four strings.  Here are the
parameters sent to this method in the same order:

  # value               anchor    tag     plain   quoted  style
  ["foo",               nil,      "!str", false,  false,  3    ]
  ["fun",               "anchor", nil,    true,   false,  1    ]
  ["many lines",        nil,      nil,    true,   false,  1    ]
  ["many\nnewlines\n",  nil,      nil,    false,  true,   4    ]

Psych::Handler#start_document.name: start_document
Psych::Handler#start_document.comment:
Called when the document starts with the declared <tt>version</tt>,
<tt>tag_directives</tt>, if the document is <tt>implicit</tt>.

<tt>version</tt> will be an array of integers indicating the YAML version
being dealt with, <tt>tag_directives</tt> is a list of tuples indicating the
prefix and suffix of each tag, and <tt>implicit</tt> is a boolean indicating
whether the document is started implicitly.

=== Example

Given the following YAML:

  %YAML 1.1
  %TAG ! tag:tenderlovemaking.com,2009:
  --- !squee

The parameters for start_document must be this:

  version         # => [1, 1]
  tag_directives  # => [["!", "tag:tenderlovemaking.com,2009:"]]
  implicit        # => false

Psych::Handler#start_mapping.name: start_mapping
Psych::Handler#start_mapping.comment:
Called when a map starts.

<tt>anchor</tt> is the anchor associated with the map or <tt>nil</tt>.
<tt>tag</tt> is the tag associated with the map or <tt>nil</tt>.
<tt>implicit</tt> is a boolean indicating whether or not the map was
implicitly started. <tt>style</tt> is an integer indicating the mapping style.

See the constants in Psych::Nodes::Mapping for the possible values of
<tt>style</tt>.

=== Example

Here is a YAML document that exercises most of the possible ways this method
can be called:

  ---
  k: !!map { hello: world }
  v: &pewpew
    hello: world

The above YAML document consists of three maps, an outer map that contains two
inner maps.  Below is a matrix of the parameters sent in order to represent
these three maps:

  # anchor    tag                       implicit  style
  [nil,       nil,                      true,     1     ]
  [nil,       "tag:yaml.org,2002:map",  false,    2     ]
  ["pewpew",  nil,                      true,     1     ]

Psych::Handler#start_sequence.name: start_sequence
Psych::Handler#start_sequence.comment:
Called when a sequence is started.

<tt>anchor</tt> is the anchor associated with the sequence or nil.
<tt>tag</tt> is the tag associated with the sequence or nil. <tt>implicit</tt>
a boolean indicating whether or not the sequence was implicitly started.
<tt>style</tt> is an integer indicating the list style.

See the constants in Psych::Nodes::Sequence for the possible values of
<tt>style</tt>.

=== Example

Here is a YAML document that exercises most of the possible ways this method
can be called:

  ---
  - !!seq [
    a
  ]
  - &pewpew
    - b

The above YAML document consists of three lists, an outer list that contains
two inner lists.  Here is a matrix of the parameters sent to represent these
lists:

  # anchor    tag                       implicit  style
  [nil,       nil,                      true,     1     ]
  [nil,       "tag:yaml.org,2002:seq",  false,    2     ]
  ["pewpew",  nil,                      true,     1     ]

Psych::Handler#start_stream.name: start_stream
Psych::Handler#start_stream.comment:
Called with <tt>encoding</tt> when the YAML stream starts.  This method is
called once per stream.  A stream may contain multiple documents.

See the constants in Psych::Parser for the possible values of
<tt>encoding</tt>.

Psych::Handler#streaming?.name: streaming?
Psych::Handler#streaming?.comment: Is this handler a streaming handler?

Psych::Handlers::Recorder.name: Psych::Handlers::Recorder
Psych::Handlers::Recorder.comment:
This handler will capture an event and record the event.  Recorder events are
available vial Psych::Handlers::Recorder#events.

For example:

  recorder = Psych::Handlers::Recorder.new
  parser = Psych::Parser.new recorder
  parser.parse '--- foo'

  recorder.events # => [list of events]

  # Replay the events

  emitter = Psych::Emitter.new $stdout
  recorder.events.each do |m, args|
    emitter.send m, *args
  end

Psych::JSON::TreeBuilder.name: Psych::JSON::TreeBuilder
Psych::JSON::TreeBuilder.comment:
Psych::JSON::TreeBuilder is an event based AST builder.  Events are sent to an
instance of Psych::JSON::TreeBuilder and a JSON AST is constructed.

Psych::Nodes.name: Psych::Nodes
Psych::Nodes.comment: = Overview When using Psych.load to deserialize a YAML document, the document is translated to an intermediary AST. That intermediary AST is then translated in to a Ruby object graph. In the opposite direction, when using Psych.dump, the Ruby object graph is translated to an intermediary AST which is then converted to a YAML document. Psych::Nodes contains all of the classes that make up the nodes of a YAML AST. You can manually build an AST and use one of the visitors (see Psych::Visitors) to convert that AST to either a YAML document or to a Ruby object graph. Here is an example of building an AST that represents a list with one scalar: # Create our nodes stream = Psych::Nodes::Stream.new doc = Psych::Nodes::Document.new seq = Psych::Nodes::Sequence.new scalar = Psych::Nodes::Scalar.new('foo') # Build up our tree stream.children << doc doc.children << seq seq.children << scalar The stream is the root of the tree. We can then convert the tree to YAML: stream.to_yaml => "---\n- foo\n" Or convert it to Ruby: stream.to_ruby => [["foo"]] == YAML AST Requirements A valid YAML AST must have one Psych::Nodes::Stream at the root. A Psych::Nodes::Stream node must have 1 or more Psych::Nodes::Document nodes as children. Psych::Nodes::Document nodes must have one and only one child. That child may be one of: * Psych::Nodes::Sequence * Psych::Nodes::Mapping * Psych::Nodes::Scalar Psych::Nodes::Sequence and Psych::Nodes::Mapping nodes may have many children, but Psych::Nodes::Mapping nodes should have an even number of children. All of these are valid children for Psych::Nodes::Sequence and Psych::Nodes::Mapping nodes: * Psych::Nodes::Sequence * Psych::Nodes::Mapping * Psych::Nodes::Scalar * Psych::Nodes::Alias Psych::Nodes::Scalar and Psych::Nodes::Alias are both terminal nodes and should not have any children.

Psych::Nodes::Alias.name: Psych::Nodes::Alias
Psych::Nodes::Alias.comment:
This class represents a {YAML Alias}[http://yaml.org/spec/1.1/#alias]. It
points to an <tt>anchor</tt>.

A Psych::Nodes::Alias is a terminal node and may have no children.

Psych::Nodes::Alias::new.name: new
Psych::Nodes::Alias::new.comment: Create a new Alias that points to an <tt>anchor</tt>

Psych::Nodes::Document.name: Psych::Nodes::Document
Psych::Nodes::Document.comment:
This represents a YAML Document.  This node must be a child of
Psych::Nodes::Stream.  A Psych::Nodes::Document must have one child, and that
child may be one of the following:

* Psych::Nodes::Sequence
* Psych::Nodes::Mapping
* Psych::Nodes::Scalar

Psych::Nodes::Document::new.name: new
Psych::Nodes::Document::new.comment:
Create a new Psych::Nodes::Document object.

<tt>version</tt> is a list indicating the YAML version.
<tt>tags_directives</tt> is a list of tag directive declarations
<tt>implicit</tt> is a flag indicating whether the document will be implicitly
started.

== Example:
This creates a YAML document object that represents a YAML 1.1 document with
one tag directive, and has an implicit start:

  Psych::Nodes::Document.new(
    [1,1],
    [["!", "tag:tenderlovemaking.com,2009:"]],
    true
  )

== See Also
See also Psych::Handler#start_document

Psych::Nodes::Document#root.name: root
Psych::Nodes::Document#root.comment:
Returns the root node.  A Document may only have one root node:
http://yaml.org/spec/1.1/#id898031

Psych::Nodes::Mapping.name: Psych::Nodes::Mapping
Psych::Nodes::Mapping.comment:
This class represents a {YAML Mapping}[http://yaml.org/spec/1.1/#mapping].

A Psych::Nodes::Mapping node may have 0 or more children, but must have an
even number of children.  Here are the valid children a Psych::Nodes::Mapping
node may have:

* Psych::Nodes::Sequence
* Psych::Nodes::Mapping
* Psych::Nodes::Scalar
* Psych::Nodes::Alias

Psych::Nodes::Mapping::new.name: new
Psych::Nodes::Mapping::new.params: (anchor = nil, tag = nil, implicit = true, style = BLOCK)
Psych::Nodes::Mapping::new.comment:
Create a new Psych::Nodes::Mapping object.

<tt>anchor</tt> is the anchor associated with the map or <tt>nil</tt>.
<tt>tag</tt> is the tag associated with the map or <tt>nil</tt>.
<tt>implicit</tt> is a boolean indicating whether or not the map was
implicitly started. <tt>style</tt> is an integer indicating the mapping style.

== See Also
See also Psych::Handler#start_mapping

Psych::Nodes::Node.name: Psych::Nodes::Node
Psych::Nodes::Node.comment:
The base class for any Node in a YAML parse tree.  This class should never be
instantiated.

Psych::Nodes::Node#each.name: each
Psych::Nodes::Node#each.comment:
Iterate over each node in the tree. Yields each node to <tt>block</tt> depth
first.

Psych::Nodes::Node#to_ruby.name: to_ruby
Psych::Nodes::Node#to_ruby.params: (symbolize_names: false, freeze: false, strict_integer: false, parse_symbols: true)
Psych::Nodes::Node#to_ruby.comment:
Convert this node to Ruby.

See also Psych::Visitors::ToRuby

Psych::Nodes::Node#transform.name: transform
Psych::Nodes::Node#transform.params: (symbolize_names: false, freeze: false, strict_integer: false, parse_symbols: true)

Psych::Nodes::Node#yaml.name: yaml
Psych::Nodes::Node#yaml.comment:
Convert this node to YAML.

See also Psych::Visitors::Emitter

Psych::Nodes::Scalar.name: Psych::Nodes::Scalar
Psych::Nodes::Scalar.comment:
This class represents a {YAML Scalar}[http://yaml.org/spec/1.1/#id858081].

This node type is a terminal node and should not have any children.

Psych::Nodes::Scalar::new.name: new
Psych::Nodes::Scalar::new.params: (value, anchor = nil, tag = nil, plain = true, quoted = false, style = ANY)
Psych::Nodes::Scalar::new.comment:
Create a new Psych::Nodes::Scalar object.

<tt>value</tt> is the string value of the scalar <tt>anchor</tt> is an
associated anchor or nil <tt>tag</tt> is an associated tag or nil
<tt>plain</tt> is a boolean value <tt>quoted</tt> is a boolean value
<tt>style</tt> is an integer indicating the string style

== See Also

See also Psych::Handler#scalar

Psych::Nodes::Sequence.name: Psych::Nodes::Sequence
Psych::Nodes::Sequence.comment:
This class represents a {YAML
sequence}[http://yaml.org/spec/1.1/#sequence/syntax].

A YAML sequence is basically a list, and looks like this:

  %YAML 1.1
  ---
  - I am
  - a Sequence

A YAML sequence may have an anchor like this:

  %YAML 1.1
  ---
  &A [
    "This sequence",
    "has an anchor"
  ]

A YAML sequence may also have a tag like this:

  %YAML 1.1
  ---
  !!seq [
    "This sequence",
    "has a tag"
  ]

This class represents a sequence in a YAML document.  A Psych::Nodes::Sequence
node may have 0 or more children.  Valid children for this node are:

* Psych::Nodes::Sequence
* Psych::Nodes::Mapping
* Psych::Nodes::Scalar
* Psych::Nodes::Alias

Psych::Nodes::Sequence::new.name: new
Psych::Nodes::Sequence::new.params: (anchor = nil, tag = nil, implicit = true, style = BLOCK)
Psych::Nodes::Sequence::new.comment:
Create a new object representing a YAML sequence.

<tt>anchor</tt> is the anchor associated with the sequence or nil.
<tt>tag</tt> is the tag associated with the sequence or nil. <tt>implicit</tt>
a boolean indicating whether or not the sequence was implicitly started.
<tt>style</tt> is an integer indicating the list style.

See Psych::Handler#start_sequence

Psych::Nodes::Stream.name: Psych::Nodes::Stream
Psych::Nodes::Stream.comment:
Represents a YAML stream.  This is the root node for any YAML parse tree.
This node must have one or more child nodes.  The only valid child node for a
Psych::Nodes::Stream node is Psych::Nodes::Document.

Psych::Nodes::Stream::new.name: new
Psych::Nodes::Stream::new.comment:
Create a new Psych::Nodes::Stream node with an <tt>encoding</tt> that defaults
to Psych::Nodes::Stream::UTF8.

See also Psych::Handler#start_stream

Psych::Parser.name: Psych::Parser
Psych::Parser.comment:
YAML event parser class.  This class parses a YAML document and calls events
on the handler that is passed to the constructor.  The events can be used for
things such as constructing a YAML AST or deserializing YAML documents.  It
can even be fed back to Psych::Emitter to emit the same document that was
parsed.

See Psych::Handler for documentation on the events that Psych::Parser emits.

Here is an example that prints out ever scalar found in a YAML document:

  # Handler for detecting scalar values
  class ScalarHandler < Psych::Handler
    def scalar value, anchor, tag, plain, quoted, style
      puts value
    end
  end

  parser = Psych::Parser.new(ScalarHandler.new)
  parser.parse(yaml_document)

Here is an example that feeds the parser back in to Psych::Emitter.  The YAML
document is read from STDIN and written back out to STDERR:

  parser = Psych::Parser.new(Psych::Emitter.new($stderr))
  parser.parse($stdin)

Psych uses Psych::Parser in combination with Psych::TreeBuilder to construct
an AST of the parsed YAML document.

Psych::Parser::new.name: new
Psych::Parser::new.comment:
Creates a new Psych::Parser instance with <tt>handler</tt>.  YAML events will
be called on <tt>handler</tt>.  See Psych::Parser for more details.

Psych::Parser#mark.name: mark
Psych::Parser#mark.comment:
Returns a Psych::Parser::Mark object that contains line, column, and index
information.

Psych::Parser#parse.name: parse
Psych::Parser#parse.comment:
Parse the YAML document contained in <tt>yaml</tt>.  Events will be called on
the handler set on the parser instance.

See Psych::Parser and Psych::Parser#handler

Psych::Parser#strip_bom.name: strip_bom
Psych::Parser#strip_bom.comment:
libyaml only skips a leading byte order mark when it detects the stream
encoding by itself.  Psych passes the encoding explicitly whenever it is
known, and on that path libyaml counts the BOM as a first-line character,
which shifts the column of every token on the first line and silently
terminates a block mapping at the second line [Bug #13615].

Psych::ScalarScanner.name: Psych::ScalarScanner
Psych::ScalarScanner.comment: Scan scalars for built in types

Psych::ScalarScanner#parse_int.name: parse_int
Psych::ScalarScanner#parse_int.comment: Parse and return an int from <tt>string</tt>

Psych::ScalarScanner#parse_time.name: parse_time
Psych::ScalarScanner#parse_time.comment: Parse and return a Time from <tt>string</tt>

Psych::Stream.name: Psych::Stream
Psych::Stream.comment:
Psych::Stream is a streaming YAML emitter.  It will not buffer your YAML, but
send it straight to an IO.

Here is an example use:

  stream = Psych::Stream.new($stdout)
  stream.start
